$comment: ARM64 (AArch64) target descriptor (plan 13 AS3 + plan 12 D-ML7-2.1). 100% JSON-configured — the same target-blind LIR substrate that drives x86_64 reads this file. Adding ARM64 = drop this file; no C++ change. Encoding shape: `fixed32` (32-bit fixed word + bit-field slots). Calling convention: AAPCS64 (https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa).

target.name: arm64
target.$isaComment: ★★★ THE INSTRUCTION-SET ARCHITECTURE THIS TARGET EXECUTES (D-ISA-LANGUAGE-BOUND-TO-ARCHITECTURE) — the x86_64 twin carries the full argument; read that file's copy and keep the two in step. ★★ NOTE THE VALUE IS `aarch64` WHILE THIS TARGET'S `name` IS `arm64`, AND THE DIVERGENCE IS DELIBERATE AND LOAD-BEARING. `aarch64` is ARM's own name for the 64-bit ISA and the spelling the psABI and every `elf64-aarch64-*` format document already use; `arm64` is the Apple/Microsoft marketing spelling this TARGET DOCUMENT is named by (and the one the `macho64-arm64-*` documents use — ✔MEASURED: the shipped format inventory does NOT agree with itself on an arch spelling, which is one more reason the axis has to be declared rather than parsed out of a name). Because the two differ here, an `if (target.name() == …)` impostor CANNOT reproduce the shipped verdicts without inventing a second mapping table — the property is visible in shipped config, not only in a test fixture.
target.$dwarfReturnAddressColumnComment: The CIE's `return_address_register` -- the DWARF column an unwinder reads to find where this frame's return address went, and the other half of the psABI numbering whose per-register half is `registers[].dwarfNumber`. ★ DECLARED, NOT DERIVED, and 30 happens to also be x30/LR's ordinary register number, which is exactly why a `the DWARF number of cc.linkRegister` derivation would look correct HERE and have nothing to read on x86_64. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 with binutils 2.42 -- `aarch64-linux-gnu-as + readelf --debug-dump=frames` on a `.cfi_startproc` probe prints `Return address column: 30`; the per-register numbers below were read the same way (each `.cfi_offset <name>` makes GAS itself translate the name, so the table is binutils' own rather than one typed from a document). ⚠ THE LOADER REQUIRES BOTH HALVES TOGETHER: this key without any `dwarfNumber`, or any `dwarfNumber` without this key, is REJECTED at load -- half a numbering loads clean and then makes `.eh_frame` silently never appear, which is the exact shape of D-UNWIND-NO-EH-FRAME-ANY-LANGUAGE-ON-ELF-OR-MACHO.
target.description: ARM64 AArch64 — minimal opcode set + AAPCS64 calling convention + fixed32 byte-encoder. Cycle-3 scope: ret (0xD65F03C0) + mov reg-reg via ORR alias (0xAA0003E0 base + Rd + Rm).

$defaultAssemblyLanguageComment:
★★★ A NAME, AND ONLY A NAME (D-DRIVER-ASM-DIALECT-SELECTED-BY-TARGET, 2026-08-13) — the x86_64 twin carries the full argument; the short form is that this key answers 'when the caller names no source language, which shipped `<stem>.lang.json` spells THIS processor's assembly?' and a `loadShipped` stem is the entire answer. No sigils, no comment characters, no operand order: those are (target, DIALECT) facts and an `asmSyntax` block carrying them was written here and REVERTED ([[D-CONFIG-ASM-DIALECT-DECLARED-AS-TARGET-VOCABULARY]]).
★★ THIS TARGET IS THE PROOF THAT THE VALUE HAD TO BE PER-TARGET AND THE GRAMMAR COULD NOT BE. `asm-arm64-gas` and `asm-x86_64-att` BOTH claim `.s`/`.S`, so the extension alone cannot name a dialect — but they disagree on the meaning of a single byte: `#` opens a line COMMENT in the AT&T document and introduces an IMMEDIATE here. No shared token table can hold both, which is why the dialect is a LANGUAGE and this file names it rather than describing it.
★ `gas` rather than `arm64-att`: AArch64 assembly has no AT&T/Intel-style split, so the ASSEMBLER is the axis that distinguishes it (a future `asm-arm64-armasm` is the sibling the naming leaves room for).
$aggregateLayoutComment: FC6 (D-FF3-1): per-ABI layout params. `natural` (scalar align = byte size, capped) is the AAPCS64 + Apple arm64 rule; maxAlignment 16 = the AArch64 max fundamental alignment (128-bit vector / __int128 / long double).
$tlsComment: TLS C2 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): the CPU's static-TLS layout convention — psABI-per-CPU data (AArch64 is Variant I under EVERY OS, so it lives on the TARGET, not the format; the x86_64 twin declares variant2). variant1 = the thread pointer (TPIDR_EL0) points AT the TCB head and the TLS block FOLLOWS it; a symbol's link-time thread-pointer offset is POSITIVE: tpoff = alignUp(tcbHeaderBytes, p_align) + templateOffset. tcbHeaderBytes = 16 — the AArch64 TCB header is two pointers (the psABI/glibc `tcbhead_t` prefix: dtv pointer + private). Consumed ONLY by the walker's tpoff helper (addTlsSymbolOffsets) when the format's tlsAccess.model is local-exec — a config-keyed formula selector, never a machine-identity branch.
$charIsUnsignedComment: TF-C56 + TF-C75 (D-CSUBSET-BARE-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-TARGET; D-TARGET-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-PLATFORM, CLOSED) — ★ THIS KEY IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR BARE-`char` SIGNEDNESS. The whole fact is here, in ONE key, in the ONE file that owns it: `default` is the AArch64 PROCESSOR's answer and `byObjectFormat` carries the PLATFORM overrides. Nothing on the object-format side declares this axis at all — a `charSignedness` key in a *.format.json is now REJECTED by the format loader's closed root-key vocabulary. WHY THE FACT CANNOT LIVE ON THE FORMAT: `elf` serves BOTH aarch64 (unsigned) and x86_64 (signed), so any flat value there is a lie on one of them, and making it honest would force all 24 format files to enumerate CPU architectures — a layering inversion. WHY IT CANNOT BE A BARE BOOLEAN EITHER: bare `char` (unqualified — NOT `signed char`) signedness is IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED (C 6.2.5p15), AAPCS64 leaves it implementation-defined too, the AArch64/GNU-Linux platform ABI chose UNSIGNED, APPLE'S PLATFORM ABI CHOSE SIGNED, and clang follows the PLATFORM, not the CPU — so `true` alone would be a claim about every AArch64 platform, and it was WRONG on Darwin. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 (Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, Apple clang 21.0.0 / clang-2100.1.1.101, /usr/bin/clang — note the PATH-default clang on that host is an Android NDK build that cannot link): `clang -dM -E` defines __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ 1 for aarch64-linux-gnu and NOT for arm64-apple-darwin; `_Static_assert((char)-1 < 0)` PASSES (signed) on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-linux and x86_64-windows-msvc, FAILS (unsigned) on aarch64-linux-gnu; codegen is a sign-extending byte load (ldrsb) native darwin-arm64 vs a zero-extending one (ldrb) under --target=aarch64-linux-gnu. THE `pe` ROW IS A FORWARD GUARD, not dead config: there is no pe64-arm64-*.format.json today, and if one lands while PE is silent here, Windows-ARM64 silently inherits `default: true` and re-acquires the exact zero-vs-sign-extend miscompile this anchor was opened for, with no diagnostic. Declaring it now states the RULE (“Windows, like Darwin, fixes `char` signedness for every CPU it serves”). ★ THE PREPROCESSOR FACE OF THIS KEY is the `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` row in `predefinedMacros` below, gated ["elf"] so it fires on exactly the leg where `default` is the effective answer. The two declarations must agree; examples/c/char_signedness_macro_coherence is the test that makes a drift between them impossible to leave green. Two corpus examples witness the CODEGEN half per platform, and their arm64 rows are SUPPOSED to differ: examples/c/char_signedness (macho 10 / elf 20) and examples/c/char_value (macho 132 / elf 131) — ★ never flip both arm64 rows of either example together; the elf row is the unsigned-`char` leg and is correct as it stands. x86_64/pe64 use signed `char` on every format they serve and x86_64.target.json therefore OMITS this key entirely (absent ⇒ signed everywhere). Resolved by `TargetSchema::charIsUnsigned(ObjectFormatKind)` — the object format is a REQUIRED argument, there is no no-arg overload, so a caller cannot silently get the processor half alone. Consumed by HIR→MIR: `isSignedIntKind(Char)` makes the one SExt-vs-ZExt decision for the char→int integer promotion, so `(char)0x80 < 0` is FALSE on arm64-elf (zero-extend, uxtb) and TRUE on arm64-macho (sign-extend, sxtb) — correct on both.
$atomicsComment: D-CSUBSET-PACKED-ATOMIC-MEMBER. ★★★ WHAT THE NATIVE INLINE ATOMIC FORM DOES WHEN THE ACCESS IS NOT NATURALLY ALIGNED, AND THE ANSWER HERE IS `traps` BY DIRECT MEASUREMENT ON REAL HARDWARE. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02 on the NATIVE arm64 VPS (aarch64, gcc 13.3.0), one `_Atomic int` at `&g.a` byte offset 1 inside a `__attribute__((packed))` struct: the inlined `stlr w16,[x15]` / `ldar w15,[x15]` pair — which is EXACTLY what DSS emits today and byte-for-byte what gcc emits — dies `rc 135, Bus error (core dumped)`. The SAME binary (one artifact, md5-checked on both hosts) exits 42 under qemu-aarch64, because qemu-user does not enforce the LDAR/STLR alignment check: ⚠⚠ THE arm64 GATE LEG IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO THIS ENTIRE CLASS AND A GREEN qemu RUN IS NOT EVIDENCE. Apple Silicon enforces the same check, and DSS's macho64-arm64 output was measured to emit the IDENTICAL inline pair, so both arm64 formats are exposed. ★ THE REMEDY IS THE ONE clang SHIPS, NOT AN INVENTION: clang 18.1.3 (`--target=aarch64-linux-gnu`) and Apple clang 21 both emit `bl __atomic_load` / `bl ___atomic_load` — the GENERIC, runtime-sized libatomic entry that dispatches through a lock table — for precisely this lvalue and inline `ldar` for a naturally-aligned one, so one working reference makes the libcall REQUIRED ([[feedback_the_goal_is_to_work_one_working_reference_2026_08_19]]). WHICH IMAGE carries those entries is the FORMAT's question, declared per `.format.json` in the `atomicsRuntime` block; this key is the PROCESSOR's half and says only what the hardware does. ⚠ A FORMAT THAT DECLARES NO ATOMICS RUNTIME UNDER `traps` REFUSES THE ACCESS LOUD rather than emitting a certain SIGBUS — that is the deliberate asymmetry with `losesAtomicity` (x86_64), where the native form is what gcc ships and works, so it stands.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C74: the per-ARCHITECTURE identity macros this CPU predefines, merged with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` at preprocess time. Declared on the TARGET (like charIsUnsigned/aggregateLayout/tls above) because they are per-CPU facts; putting them on the language would force c.lang.json to enumerate CPU architectures. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by BOTH this file and the language config is a LOAD-TIME-equivalent FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) — neither side silently wins. GATING (MEASURED 2026-07-28 with `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>`): `__aarch64__` and `__ARM_ARCH_ISA_A64` are defined by EVERY AArch64 toolchain (present on both arm64-apple-darwin and aarch64-linux-gnu) so they are UNGATED; `__arm64__` and `__arm64` are APPLE-ONLY (present on arm64-apple-darwin, ABSENT on aarch64-linux-gnu) so they are gated ["macho"] — shipping them ungated would leak an Apple spelling onto the ELF leg, and shipping only `__aarch64__` would clear nothing on macOS, whose SDK arch ladders (machine/_types.h, sys/cdefs.h) gate on `__arm64__`. ★ `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` is gated ["elf"] (TF-C75) and is the ONE ROW HERE WHOSE GATE IS AN ABI PROPERTY RATHER THAN A VENDOR SPELLING. It is not an identity macro at all: it is the PREPROCESSOR-VISIBLE FACE of this file's `charIsUnsigned` key above. That key is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for bare-`char` signedness — `default: true` (the AArch64 processor's answer) with `byObjectFormat` overrides making macho and pe SIGNED — so this macro must be defined on exactly the leg where the `default` is the effective answer, i.e. elf, and must NOT appear where an override fires. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 with `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (/usr/bin/clang, Apple clang 21.0.0 / clang-2100.1.1.101): DEFINED as 1 for aarch64-linux-gnu, and NOT defined for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc or x86_64-apple-darwin — so arm64×elf defines it, arm64×macho does not, and x86_64 never does (x86_64.target.json ships no such row and declares no `charIsUnsigned` at all). It could not be expressed before TF-C75 because the split is (architecture × PLATFORM) and this file is per-ARCHITECTURE; the gate now supplies the platform half, exactly as it already does for `__arm64__`. ★ THIS ROW AND THE `charIsUnsigned` KEY ABOVE STATE THE SAME FACT IN TWO NOTATIONS — a preprocessor macro and a codegen switch — SO THEY CAN DRIFT. No engine-side coherence check is possible: any such check would have to name `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` in engine code, which is a forbidden identity branch. The anti-drift device is therefore a TEST: examples/c/char_signedness_macro_coherence asserts the macro and the emitted char codegen in ONE program with per-leg exit codes, so a disagreement between the two declarations cannot be made green. If you change this row, change `charIsUnsigned` above to match, and expect that example to be the thing that tells you if you did not. SHIPPED, BUT NOT HERE -- LANDED ON THE OBJECT FORMAT (TF-C97, D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): `__LP64__`/`_LP64` are a DATA MODEL, not an architecture -- x86_64:pe64 is LLP64 while the SAME CPU is LP64 under elf64/macho64 -- so a row here would be wrong on one of this target's own formats. This note used to read 'DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED' and was a HANDOFF that went four cycles uncompleted; it is now DONE: every LP64 `*.format.json` declares both spellings through the format schema's own `predefinedMacros` key (the same key name, the same shared entry grammar, the same C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro collision policy as this file's), and every LLP64/ILP32 one declares NEITHER -- the negative being the whole reason the channel sits at the format layer. Do not add them here. ★ `__BYTE_ORDER__` WAS LISTED HERE AS 'DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED (its value must be a macro REFERENCE, e.g. `__ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__`, which needs a different mechanism than a literal Constant body)'. THAT CLAIM WAS NEVER TESTED AND IS NOW REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT (TF-C115, D-PP-ENDIANNESS-PREDEFINES): a materialized predefine is spliced over its invocation and RESCANNED like any other replacement (`preprocessor.cpp` — `spliceOver(...); continue;   // rescan from the materialized value`), so a `constant` body that NAMES another macro resolves for free. MEASURED 2026-08-04 against a patched config copy reached through DSS_CONFIG_ROOT: with `__BYTE_ORDER__` = `__ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__` the probe compiled rc 0 with all 8 `#error` legs silent (`defined(__BYTE_ORDER__)`, `__BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__`, `__BYTE_ORDER__ == 1234`, `__BYTE_ORDER__ != __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__`); the same probe on the UNPATCHED config fired 6 of the 8 (6 x P001E), one of which was the big-endian leg — the unshipped state SELECTED THE BIG-ENDIAN ARM (`0 == 0`, C 6.10.1p4), silently. The two legs that stayed SILENT on the unpatched config are the instructive pair: `__BYTE_ORDER__ != __ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__` was FALSE (both operands undefined, so `0 != 0`) — an accidental agreement that would have read as a pass — and the `__BIG_ENDIAN__`-absence leg, which was correctly quiet then and must stay quiet now. Zero engine change was required. The rows are SHIPPED below. Still DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: toolchain identity (`__GNUC__`/`__clang__`/`__APPLE_CC__`) which is a COMPILER profile, not a CPU, and is blocked on two absent parser features anyway (leading-position `__attribute__`, and the `inline` function specifier).
$endiannessPredefinesComment: TF-C115 (D-PP-ENDIANNESS-PREDEFINES) — the arm64 twin of the x86_64 note; read that file's copy for the full argument, and keep the two in step. ★ DOCUMENTATION KEY ONLY: there is deliberately NO `endianness` root key. THE LAYER: endianness varies by CPU (MEASURED 2026-08-04, `clang-19 -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>`, Ubuntu clang 19.1.1 — `aarch64_be-linux-gnu` defines `__BIG_ENDIAN__` 1 and `__BYTE_ORDER__` `__ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__`, while `aarch64-linux-gnu` defines `__LITTLE_ENDIAN__` 1 and `__BYTE_ORDER__` `__ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__`) and does NOT vary across the object formats one DSS target serves — arm64 is little-endian under BOTH elf64-aarch64-linux and macho64-arm64-darwin — so it passes the very test `__LP64__` failed and belongs on the TARGET. THAT IS ALSO WHY THIS ROW IS UNLIKE `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` ABOVE, the one row here whose gate is an ABI property: bare-`char` signedness genuinely splits (architecture × PLATFORM) and needed `availableObjectFormats`; endianness does not split on this CPU, so both rows are UNGATED. GATING (MEASURED, same run): `__LITTLE_ENDIAN__` is defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu AND x86_64-pc-windows-msvc — every triple DSS targets — so, unlike `__arm64__`/`__arm64`, it is NOT an Apple-only spelling and must not be gated `["macho"]`; gating it would leave the ELF leg answering `#if __BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__` with a silent TRUE. ★ `__BIG_ENDIAN__` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT AND THE ABSENCE IS THE DECLARATION — MEASURED present ONLY on the big-endian triple. Apple's `libkern/OSByteOrder.h:165` tests `defined(__BIG_ENDIAN__)` BEFORE the little-endian arm, so a stray row would silently select byte-swapping macros; `examples/c/endianness_predefines` is red if it ever appears on any leg. NO `endianness` KEY ACCOMPANIES THESE ROWS, on the `charIsUnsigned` lesson stated above: a second notation of one fact is a drift source that needs its own coherence example to be safe, and unlike `charIsUnsigned` — which HIR→MIR really reads — no engine consumer for an endianness value exists today. THE `__ORDER_*` CONSTANTS THE VALUE NAMES LIVE ON THE LANGUAGE (c.lang.json): they are invariant across every measured triple including the big-endian one, so they are a naming vocabulary, not a per-CPU fact.

opcodes.$comment: Slot 0 = the Invalid sentinel — same discipline as x86_64. Substrate's addInst guard rejects opcode 0 loudly.
Virtual-ISA pseudo-op — same role as x86's `arg`: 'this LirReg is the function's k-th input parameter'. ML7 callconv lowering rewrites to the real mov-from-arg-reg sequence.

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC7 C1c) — caller-side mirror of `arg`: 'this LirReg is the k-th return register of the preceding struct-returning call' (payload = per-class return ordinal). ML7 callconv lowering captures it from the return register. Declared for substrate uniformity; AAPCS64 struct returns land at C3.

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC7 C3, AAPCS64/Apple x8 sret) — callee-side mirror of `arg`: 'this LirReg is the incoming indirect-result (sret) pointer', read from the cc's indirectResultRegister (x8) at function entry. NO encoding: lir_callconv materializes it into `mov result, x8` (an ORR-alias), exactly like `arg`/`ret_piece`. payload unused. The caller side needs no opcode — the sret pointer is a normal prepended Call operand routed to x8 by the call payload's indirect-result bit.

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC12a-core, D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): the variadic register-save-area address. Declared for substrate uniformity (like read_indirect_result); AArch64's variadic ABI differs (no SysV-style register-save-area / vaListLayout this cycle), so its sysv-less CC never EMITS this op — it is materialized away by lir_callconv only for a CC that declares a vaListLayout. No encoding.

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC12a-core, D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): the incoming overflow-stack-args address. Declared for substrate uniformity; never emitted on a CC without a vaListLayout. No encoding (materialized away by lir_callconv).

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (D-FC12-VARIADIC-OVERFLOW-FIXED-AGGREGATE-STACK-ARGS): callee-side mirror of the caller's `ByValueStackArg` carrier — the ADDRESS of a FIXED by-value aggregate/HFA param placed WHOLLY on the incoming stack (it straddled the reg/stack boundary). lir_callconv materializes it into `lea result, [sp + totalFrameSize + callPushBytes + shadowSpaceBytes + payload]`; the PAYLOAD is this aggregate's byte offset within the incoming overflow area. DISTINCT from the va_* ops so it is NOT a va_start-detection signal (it occurs in non-variadic functions too). No encoding (materialized away).

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (c69, D-CSUBSET-ALLOCA-ADDRESS-REMATERIALIZE): a RE-REFERENCE of a body-local's stack slot — 'this fresh LirReg is the ADDRESS of local-alloca #k', k = PAYLOAD = the alloca's 0-based scan-order index. The c69 entry-block alloca-hoist makes every local's address live from entry; reusing ONE address vreg tips a register-pressure cliff, so MIR->LIR emits the `alloca` op ONCE (reserves the slot) and a fresh `lea_frame_slot k` at EACH use (tiny def->use range) — the conventional 'rematerialize frame addresses' treatment. lir_callconv materializes it into `lea result, [sp + localAreaOffset + offsetOf(k) + disp]` — byte-identical to the original alloca's `lea` (offset from the alloca-index->offset map built in scan order). An OPTIONAL single ImmInt operand is a folded CONSTANT byte displacement `disp` (a `&local[constIdx]`/`&s.field` Gep whose base IS this alloca, folded by lowerGep into ONE sp-based frame lea): cheaper (one lea) AND load-bearing — a >16 MiB `disp` in the un-folded two-lea form (`lea_frame_slot` base + `lea [base+disp]`) lowers to the arm64 MOVZ/MOVK macro `ADD Xd,base,Xd` which CLOBBERS base when regalloc coalesces the tiny-range remat base into the Gep result (base==Xd), a SIGSEGV; folding makes the base `sp` (a reserved physreg, never the result), so `MOVZ Xd;MOVK Xd;ADD Xd,sp,Xd` is safe. DISTINCT from `alloca` so it is INVISIBLE to the frame-layout slot-count scan (one slot per original alloca is preserved). On arm64 `lea` is the ADD-immediate frame-address form (the same op the alloca/va_* address pseudo-ops lower to). No encoding (materialized away). hasSideEffects=false (pure address computation, like lea/alloca); no LIR-tier pass removes/merges it.

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (c116 H1, D-WIN64-SEH-FUNCLETS): 'this fresh LirReg is the ADDRESS of local-slot #k IN THE FRAME the operand[0] register establishes' — the generic analog of llvm.localrecover. operand[0] = an establisher-frame base pointer register; PAYLOAD = k. lir_callconv materializes it into `lea result, [establisherReg + parentLocalAreaOffset(k)]` (the config FrameLayout of the frame the base establishes; on arm64 `lea` is the ADD-immediate frame-address form). Declared for substrate uniformity; x64 SEH funclets are its only consumer today (windows.json is pe-only, so no `__try` reaches arm64 and this op is never emitted here). No encoding (materialized away). hasSideEffects=false (pure address computation, like lea/alloca/lea_frame_slot).

Virtual-ISA pseudo-op (FC12b, D-FC12B-WIN64-VARIADIC-CALLEE): the Win64 HomogeneousPointer va_start base (&home[namedArgCount]). Declared for substrate uniformity; AAPCS64 uses the dual-cursor strategy (FC12c) and never emits this op. No encoding (materialized away by lir_callconv).

AAPCS64 has no native `mov reg, reg` instruction — the canonical encoding is `ORR Xd, XZR, Xm` (32-bit fixed word 0xAA0003E0 = base + Rn=XZR=31; Rd and Rm via slots). LIR's `mov` is 2-operand (result + 1 source); 3-address natively (no requires2Address).

variants.$comment: ★★ WIDTH-KEYED TO 64 AS OF 2026-08-13, AND THE KEY IS A SILENT-MISCOMPILE FIX RATHER THAN TIDYING. This variant carried NO `guard.width`, and `walker_util::variantMatchesInst` treats a width-absent guard as matching ANY width — so a width-32 `mov` with a register source selected THIS word and encoded `ORR Xd, XZR, Xm`, a 64-bit move. Nothing reported it: the guard matched, the encoder emitted, the build was green. It became reachable the moment a hand-written `.s` could write `mov w0, w1`, whose ONLY observable difference from `mov x0, x1` is that it zeroes bits 63:32. ✔MEASURED before the change: every `mov` the compiler emits with a REGISTER operand passes width-default flags (64) — the one flags-carrying emitter, `mir_to_lir.cpp`'s `emitMovToFresh`, is reached only from the constant-materialization paths, whose operand is an ImmInt32 or a LiteralIndex — so keying this to 64 and adding the W sibling below is BYTE-NEUTRAL for existing codegen. (The `["imm32"]` MOVZ variant below WAS deliberately left width-absent on that same reasoning — width-32 constants DO reach it, and an X-form MOVZ zeroes all 64 bits, which is value-identical to the W form. ⓘ UPDATED 2026-08-13: it is now width-keyed at 64 with a width-32 W sibling (D-ASM-ARM64-MOVZ-W-FORM-UNDECLARED), because value-identity was never the blocker — `variantHonorsDeclaredWidth` refuses a width-absent variant elected by a width-32 REQUEST, so `mov w0, #5` could not be written at all. Every variant of this opcode is width-keyed now.)

wires.$comment: ORR Xd, XZR, Xm — bits 16..20 hold Rm (the source register's encoding). The fixed word's bits 9..5 = 0b11111 (XZR) are baked in; the wire only adds Rm bits.

variants.$comment: ORR Wd, WZR, Wm — the sf=0 sibling (ARM ARM C6.2.206 ORR shifted-register): bit 31 cleared turns 0xAA0003E0 into 0x2A0003E0. Same slots, same Rn=WZR baked in. This is what `mov w0, w1` encodes, and writing a W register ZEROES bits 63:32 of the containing X register — the property the 64-bit form does not have and the reason the two cannot share one width-absent variant.

★ MOVN Xd, #~imm16 (D-ASM-ARM64-NEGATIVE-IMMEDIATE-UNENCODABLE) — the NEGATIVE-immediate sibling of the MOVZ variant below, and it MUST PRECEDE it: the MOVZ variant is magnitude-unbounded, so a negative immediate would first-match THERE and die at encode (which is exactly the fail-loud this variant closes). Fixed word 0x92800000 (sf=1, opc=00 = MOVN, fixed 100101, hw=00), imm16 at bits 5..20, Rd at 0..4 — the SAME field layout as MOVZ, which is why the two share one bit-window and differ only in `opc`. Semantics: `Xd := ~(imm16)`, so the slot is `imm16.inverted` and the ENCODER writes the complement; the guard's `negValue:true` routes ONLY a strictly-negative immediate here (a non-negative one falls through to MOVZ, byte-identically to before this variant existed), and `immMin:1`/`immMax:65536` bound |V| so V lands in [-65536,-1] ⇔ complement in [0,65535]. ✔MEASURED with aarch64-linux-gnu-as 2.42 + objdump: `mov x1,#-8` and `movn x1,#7` assemble to the IDENTICAL word 0x928000E1 — gas ALIASES the negative `mov` onto MOVN, which is precisely the aliasing this variant gives DSS. Boundaries measured the same way: `mov x1,#-1` = 0x92800001 (imm16 0), `mov x1,#-65536` = 0x929FFFE1 (imm16 0xFFFF). A more negative constant (`mov x1,#-65537` → gas emits the hw=1 form 0x92A00021) is a SEPARATE shifted variant and is NOT declared here — it stays fail-loud with the range named, a STATED boundary rather than a silent wrong constant.

★ MOVN Wd, #~imm16 — the sf=0 sibling (fixed word 0x12800000 = 0x92800000 with bit 31 cleared). ⚠ THIS ARM IS NOT OPTIONAL AND THE REASONING IS NOT THE MOVZ REASONING. `MOVN Xd,#7` writes 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF8 while `MOVN Wd,#7` writes 0x00000000FFFFFFF8, so a width-absent 64-bit MOVN serving a width-32 request would be the exact silent miscompile the `mov`-reg variant above was width-keyed to fix, one cycle later and in the same opcode. Both MOVN arms are therefore width-KEYED, and they are keyed for CORRECTNESS. ⓘ UPDATED 2026-08-13: the MOVZ variants below are now width-keyed too (D-ASM-ARM64-MOVZ-W-FORM-UNDECLARED), but for a DIFFERENT reason that is worth keeping distinct — MOVZ's two forms ARE value-identical, so keying them bought the ability to WRITE `mov w0, #5` rather than any correctness. ✔MEASURED (aarch64-linux-gnu-as 2.42): `mov w1,#-8` and `movn w1,#7` both assemble to 0x128000E1. A negative immediate at width 8/16 matches NEITHER MOVN arm and, since MOVZ is width-keyed as well, matches no variant at all — a loud A_NoMatchingEncodingVariant at the matcher rather than the encoder's range gate. No shipped path emits an 8/16-bit immediate move (`registerOpWidthFlags` collapses both to 32); either way there is no silent width guess.

MOVZ Xd, #imm16 — move a 16-bit UNSIGNED immediate (zeroing the rest of the register; hw shift = 0). Fixed word 0xD2800000 (sf=1, opc=10, fixed bits 100101, hw=00). The Imm16 slot writes imm16 at bits 5..20; Rd at bits 0..4. Selected by the `imm32` operand-kind guard (the engine's immediate-operand filter — the SLOT is 16-bit, MOVZ-specific). The entry trampoline uses this to load the exit-syscall number into x8 (D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64). A value wider than the 16-bit slot STILL fails loud at encode (A_ImmediateOperandOutOfRange) — but the MIR->LIR const materialization now splits wide inline constants into the MOVZ + MOVK ladder BEFORE encode when the movk_lsl* family below is declared (D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64-WIDE-IMMEDIATE, FC3.5 sweep-c3), so the encoder ceiling backstops hand-built LIR only.
★★ WIDTH-KEYED TO 64 AS OF 2026-08-13 — D-ASM-ARM64-MOVZ-W-FORM-UNDECLARED, closed on an OPERATOR RULING, and this key is one HALF of a two-part change (the W sibling below is the other). This variant carried NO `guard.width`, and `walker_util::variantMatchesInst` treats a width-absent guard as matching ANY width — so `asm_elect::variantHonorsDeclaredWidth` refused every width-32 request that landed here and `mov w0, #5` was a hard error in a hand-written `.s` ('would encode at the target's natural width, silently dropping the width this instruction asked for'). Declaring BOTH widths is the same shape `and`/`or`/`xor` and the two `mov`-reg arms above already have; leaving this one width-absent beside a new width-32 sibling would be a SECOND, order-dependent mechanism in one opcode.
⚠ THE COST WAS PAID KNOWINGLY AND IT IS A BYTE CHANGE, NOT A BUG FIX. A width-32 C constant used to elect THIS word and now elects the W sibling, so the C path's bytes MOVE for every 32-bit constant materialization. ✔MEASURED across the whole arm64 corpus: they move by EXACTLY the sf bit, the values are identical (a W-register write zero-extends into bits 63:32, which is what an X-form MOVZ already did), and the runtime exit codes are unchanged under qemu-aarch64.
⚠ AND ONE BEHAVIOUR THIS KEY DELIBERATELY CHANGES: an `imm32` `mov` at width 8 or 16 now matches NEITHER MOVZ arm and fails loud at the matcher (A_NoMatchingEncodingVariant) instead of silently taking the 64-bit form. ✔MEASURED that no shipped path produces one — `mir_to_lir`'s `registerOpWidthFlags` COLLAPSES byte and half-word widths to 32 for every register-resident value (D-CSUBSET-CHAR-STRING-VALUE-CODEGEN), the entry trampoline and the callconv variadic count-reg both emit at flags=0 (width 64), and this dialect derives width from `w`/`x` register spellings only. An unreachable shape that fails loud beats one that silently widens.

★ MOVZ Wd, #imm16 — the sf=0 sibling (fixed word 0x52800000 = 0xD2800000 with bit 31 cleared), and what `mov w0, #5` encodes. ✔MEASURED with `aarch64-linux-gnu-as` 2.42 + objdump, and the PAIR was measured rather than the W half alone: `mov w0,#5` = 0x528000a0 / `mov x0,#5` = 0xd28000a0; `mov w1,#8` = 0x52800101 / `mov x1,#8` = 0xd2800101; `mov w2,#0` = 0x52800002 / `mov x2,#0` = 0xd2800002; `mov w3,#65535` = 0x529fffe3 / `mov x3,#65535` = 0xd29fffe3; `mov w30,#1` = 0x5280003e / `mov x30,#1` = 0xd280003e. Every pair XORs to exactly 0x80000000, so sf IS the only difference — CHECKED, not assumed, because MOVZ/MOVN/MOVK are separated by `opc` at bits 30:29 and a wrong-opc word would still have read as a plausible move. gas ALIASES the W `mov` onto MOVZ: `movz w1,#8` assembles to the SAME 0x52800101. Same Imm16 slot (bits 5..20) and same Rd (bits 0..4) as the X form, which is why the two share one wire set.
★ WHY THIS PAIR'S ARGUMENT IS NOT THE MOVN PAIR'S ARGUMENT, stated because the two sit four lines apart and look interchangeable. The MOVN arms are width-keyed because their VALUES DIFFER (`MOVN Xd,#7` = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF8, `MOVN Wd,#7` = 0x00000000FFFFFFF8) — a width-absent MOVN would be a silent miscompile. MOVZ's two forms are VALUE-IDENTICAL (an X-form MOVZ zeroes all 64 bits; a W-form write zero-extends to the same 64-bit result), so nothing was ever miscompiled here: what was missing was any way for a caller to SAY width 32, which `variantHonorsDeclaredWidth` correctly refused to fake. ⇒ this variant buys EXPRESSIVENESS, the MOVN pair bought CORRECTNESS, and the byte change is the price of the first.
★ THE MOVK LADDER STILL SEEDS OFF MOVZ AND IS UNAFFECTED. `materializeViaMovkLadder` emits the seed at the constant's own width, so a width-32 ladder now seeds with THIS word; the zero-extension property `movk_lsl16` relies on to stay width-absent holds identically for the W form, and at width 32 the ladder emits only chunks 0..1, so bits 63:32 stay zero either way.

opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c3 (D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64-WIDE-IMMEDIATE): MOVK Xd, #imm16, LSL #16 — keep-other-bits 16-bit insert at bits 31:16. ARM ARM C6.2.227: sf [31] | opc=11 [30:29] | 100101 [28:23] | hw [22:21] | imm16 [20:5] | Rd [4:0]; X-base 0xF2800000, hw=01 -> 0xF2A00000. The MIR->LIR const materialization emits the MINIMAL ladder: MOVZ #chunk0 (zeroing all 64 bits) + one MOVK per NONZERO higher 16-bit chunk — selected by constant magnitude at the LOWERING (an operand's VALUE cannot guard encoding variants), capability-probed by mnemonic presence (x86's imm32 mov form never consults this family). requires2Address: the ISA reads Xd's other bits — the LIR shape is result==operand[0] (the accumulating register), wire index 0 lands in Rd (the 2-addr dest-wire satisfies the result-placement validate rule). ONE deliberately width-ABSENT X-form variant: the ladder is seeded by MOVZ (which zeroes bits 63:32), so the X-MOVK is value-correct for width-32 constants too (chunks 2/3 are never emitted at width 32) — the W-ORR zext / xor_rdx_zero width-invariance precedent.

MOVK Xd, #imm16, LSL #32 — hw=10 -> 0xF2C00000 (X-only: sf=0 reserves hw>=10). Chunk 2 of the wide-immediate ladder; emitted only for width-64 constants whose bits 47:32 are nonzero (sign-extended negative int32 patterns).
MOVK Xd, #imm16, LSL #48 — hw=11 -> 0xF2E00000 (X-only). Chunk 3 of the wide-immediate ladder.
AAPCS64 RET (X30 implicit) = 0xD65F03C0. No operands at LIR level; the link register x30 is implicit per the calling convention.
Hard-trap. AArch64 BRK #0 = 0xD4200000. Cycle-3 includes for completeness so a synthesized LIR can terminate without depending on `ret` semantics.

ARM64 binary ops (AS3b, all 3-address natively — no requires2Address). Fixed-word base patterns: ADD reg-reg = 0x8B000000; SUB = 0xCB000000; AND = 0x8A000000; ORR = 0xAA000000; EOR = 0xCA000000. Wires: Rd at 0..4 (dest), Rn at 5..9 (src1), Rm at 16..20 (src2).

encoding.$comment: FC3 c2 (D-CSUBSET-32BIT-ALU-FORMS): the reg-reg shape is width-keyed 64/32 — the W-form is the SAME shifted-register ADD word with sf (bit 31) CLEARED (ARM ARM C6.2.5: a W-register write zeroes the upper 32 bits of the X register, the C-defined unsigned-int wraparound for free). The imm12 shape stays width:64-only — its sole producer is the callconv sp-adjust (Ptr-width); a width-32 add-imm inst would match NOTHING and fail loud rather than silently compute with a 64-bit carry.

variants.$comment: ADD Wd, Wn, Wm — 0x0B000000 (the X-form 0x8B000000 with sf=0).

ADD Xd, Xn, #imm12 (immediate, single word). Fixed word 0x91000000 (sf=1, op=0 add, S=0, sh=0). imm12 at bits 10..21 via the Imm12 slot; Rd 0..4, Rn 5..9. Used by the callconv prologue/epilogue stack adjust (`add sp, sp, #frame`) when the frame fits 0..4095. 2-operand LIR form [reg, imm]: operand 0 → Rn (also the dest via resultSlot), operand 1 → Imm12. `immMax:4095` routes ONLY a frame ≤4095 here; a larger value falls through to the 2-word shifted variant below (D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-IMM12).

ADD Xd, Xn, #imm (shifted imm12 word-pair, D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-IMM12). For a frame in (4095, 0xFFFFFF] this emits TWO words: word0 = `ADD Xd, Xn, #(V & 0xFFF)` (0x91000000, sh=0), word1 = `ADD Xd, Xd, #((V>>12) & 0xFFF), LSL #12` (0x91400000 = 0x91000000|0x400000, sh=1). SCRATCH-FREE: word1 reads its OWN dest (Xd) as the source base — extraResultSlots thread the result reg into word1.Rd AND word1.Rn. The single imm12.hilo24 wire (word0) carries the VALUE; the encoder splits it and writes lo→word0 / hi→word1, both into the imm12 bit-window (10..21). `immMin:4096`/`immMax:16777215` route ONLY a >4095, ≤16MiB frame here; >16MiB stays fail-loud (D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-16MIB).

ADD sp, sp, #imm (MOVZ/MOVK + EXTENDED-register 3-word form, D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-16MIB). The epilogue mirror of SUB's 3-word form. word0 = `MOVZ x16, #(V & 0xFFFF)` (0xD2800010), word1 = `MOVK x16, #((V>>16) & 0xFFFF), LSL #16` (0xF2A00010), word2 = `ADD sp, sp, x16` (the EXTENDED-register form 0x8B3063FF: option=011 UXTX, bit 21 set, Rd=Rn=sp=31, Rm=x16=16). x16=IP0 scratch baked; NO resultSlot (sp=31 baked into word2 — rule-G baked-dest exemption). Same immMin/immMax routing + >2GiB fail-loud as SUB.
FC3 c2: SUB Wd, Wn, Wm — 0x4B000000 (the X-form 0xCB000000 with sf=0).

SUB Xd, Xn, #imm12 (immediate, single word). Fixed word 0xD1000000 (sf=1, op=1 sub, S=0, sh=0). imm12 at bits 10..21; Rd 0..4, Rn 5..9. Used by the callconv prologue stack adjust (`sub sp, sp, #frame`) when the frame fits 0..4095. Same 2-operand [reg, imm] LIR form as ADD-immediate. FC3 c2: width:64-only like add's imm12 shape (sole producer is the Ptr-width sp-adjust; a width-32 sub-imm fails loud). `immMax:4095` routes ONLY a ≤4095 frame here; larger falls through to the 2-word shifted variant (D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-IMM12).

SUB Xd, Xn, #imm (shifted imm12 word-pair, D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-IMM12). For a frame in (4095, 0xFFFFFF] this emits TWO words: word0 = `SUB Xd, Xn, #(V & 0xFFF)` (0xD1000000, sh=0), word1 = `SUB Xd, Xd, #((V>>12) & 0xFFF), LSL #12` (0xD1400000 = 0xD1000000|0x400000, sh=1). word1 reads its OWN dest (Xd) — SCRATCH-FREE via extraResultSlots. Single imm12.hilo24 wire (word0) carries the VALUE; the encoder splits lo→word0 / hi→word1. The prologue's `sub sp,sp,#frame` becomes `sub sp,sp,#lo; sub sp,sp,#hi,LSL#12` — the transient sp-lo misalignment between the two words is invisible (no access/call between them; V is 16-aligned). `immMin:4096`/`immMax:16777215`; >16MiB fail-loud.

SUB sp, sp, #imm (MOVZ/MOVK + EXTENDED-register 3-word form, D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-16MIB). For a frame in (0xFFFFFF, 0x7FFFFFFF] (>16 MiB, ≤2 GiB) this emits THREE words: word0 = `MOVZ x16, #(V & 0xFFFF)` (0xD2800010, Rd=x16=16 baked), word1 = `MOVK x16, #((V>>16) & 0xFFFF), LSL #16` (0xF2A00010, hw=01, Rd=x16), word2 = `SUB sp, sp, x16` (the EXTENDED-register form 0xCB3063FF: option=011 UXTX, bit 21 set, Rd=Rn=sp=31, Rm=x16=16 — NOT the shifted-register 0xCB000000 where #31=XZR → `sp±0` corrupt frame). x16 is AAPCS64 IP0, the architecturally-blessed intra-procedure scratch, free at the prologue/epilogue; it is BAKED into all three base words (NO resultSlot — the destination sp=31 is baked into word2, validate's rule-G `imm32.movzmovk` baked-dest exemption). The single imm32.movzmovk wire (operand 1, word0) carries the VALUE; the encoder splits lo16→word0 / hi16→word1. Operand 0 (sp) wires to word2's `rn` (re-confirming the baked sp=31). `immMin:16777216`/`immMax:2147483647` route ONLY a >16MiB, ≤2GiB frame here; a frame > 2 GiB flows through int32 as NEGATIVE → magnitude nullopt → no variant matches → fail-loud (D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-2GIB).

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): `sub_sp_reg sp, <sizeReg>` — subtract a RUNTIME byte count (in a register) from the stack pointer (the dynamic-alloca core, `int a[n]` => `sub sp, alignUp(n*4,16)`). ★ THE XZR-VS-SP TRAP: a shifted-register SUB (0xCB000000) encodes reg 31 as XZR, so `sub sp, sp, Xm` there would compute `sp - 0` and SILENTLY discard the size. The CORRECT form is the EXTENDED-register SUB (option=011 UXTX, bit 21 set), where reg 31 in Rd/Rn IS the stack pointer: fixedWord 0xCB2063FF (= the 0xCB3063FF precedent baked into the >16MiB sp-adjust macro, with Rm CLEARED to 0). Rd=Rn=sp=31 are BAKED; operand1(size) wires into Rm (bits 16..20). operand0(sp) wires into Rn (bits 5..9) — sp's hwEncoding IS 31, so this is IDEMPOTENT with the baked Rn=31 (the per-position wire check requires every operand wired). Sanity: 0xCB2063FF | (16<<16) == 0xCB3063FF (the `SUB sp,sp,x16` word). result:none (SP mutates in place); hasSideEffects=true so no pass drops/reorders it vs the sp_copy that captures the moved SP. Emitted by MIR->LIR with the physical stack-pointer operand; callconv passes it through.

D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): `sp_copy dst, src` = `add dst, src, #0` (the ADD-IMMEDIATE form, fixedWord 0x91000000, imm12=0 baked) — used for the three frame-pointer plumbing roles a VLA function needs: prologue FP<-SP, epilogue SP<-FP, and the VLA-base capture base<-SP. ★ Like sub_sp_reg this uses the SP-capable form: the add-immediate encoding treats reg 31 as the STACK POINTER (not XZR), so `add sp, x29, #0` / `add x29, sp, #0` / `add base, sp, #0` all move the real SP — a register-register ORR (`mov`, where reg 31 = XZR) would read/write XZR instead. resultSlot rd = dst; operand0=src -> rn. A DISTINCT mnemonic from `add`/`mov` so it can be hasSideEffects=true (reads/writes the physical SP; no pass may drop or reorder it across the sub_sp_reg).

variants.$comment: ★★★ MOV (to/from SP) AT WIDTH 64 — `ADD <Xd|SP>, <Xn|SP>, #0`, ARM ARM C6.2.209, and since 2026-09-03 also what the aarch64 gas dialect's `mov` spelling elects when either end is the stack pointer ([[D-ASM-ARM64-SP-AND-XZR-SHARE-ENCODING-31-SO-MOV-SP-SILENTLY-BECOMES-ZERO]]). ✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 probed SEPARATELY and agreeing: `mov x0, sp` = 0x910003E0, `mov sp, x0` = 0x9100001F, `mov x30, sp` = 0x910003FE, `mov sp, x30` = 0x910003DF, `mov sp, sp` = 0x910003FF — every one of them THIS word with Rd and Rn filled in, which is why ONE variant spells both directions. ★★ `requiresRegRole` IS WHAT KEEPS IT OUT OF THE ORDINARY CASE: `x0`/`x1` carry no role and fit every field, so without it this encoding would also accept `mov x0, x1` and the election would report an ambiguity against the ORR form on the commonest line in the dialect. The condition is the ARM ARM's own alias preference — *Rd or Rn is 31* — so the choice is a REFUSAL and never a declaration order. ⚠ The dialect list is NOT ranked and must not become so: correctness here comes from `mov` REFUSING `sp` (its ORR fields read 31 as the zero register) and this variant refusing everything that names no stack pointer.

★ MOV (to/from SP) AT WIDTH 32 — `ADD <Wd|WSP>, <Wn|WSP>, #0`, fixed word 0x11000000 = the X form with sf (bit 31) CLEARED. ✔MEASURED, both references: `mov w0, wsp` = 0x110003E0, `mov wsp, w0` = 0x1100001F, `add w0, wsp, #0` = 0x110003E0 (gas prints it back as `mov w0, wsp`). ⚠ THE ARM IS NOT COSMETIC AND THE ARGUMENT IS THE `movn` ONE, NOT THE `movz` ONE: a W-register write ZEROES bits 63:32 of the containing X register, so a width-absent 64-bit form serving a width-32 request would be a silent value change. It is also the only way `wsp` — the register row added by the same anchor — becomes writable at all. ⓘ NOT reachable from the compiler's own lowering: `mir_to_lir` emits `sp_copy` at flags=0 (width 64) for the frame-pointer capture, so this arm is byte-neutral for every compiled `.c`.

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-VLA (C5): `sp_restore sp, <savedReg>` = `mov sp, savedReg` = `add sp, savedReg, #0` (the ADD-IMMEDIATE form, fixedWord 0x9100001F: Rd=sp=31 baked, imm12=0) — RESTORE the stack pointer to a previously-captured watermark (a StackSave's `sp_copy`), the block-scope VLA teardown emitted on every NON-return exit of a VLA-declaring scope. ★ Like sub_sp_reg/sp_copy this uses the SP-capable ADD-immediate encoding (reg 31 = the STACK POINTER, NOT XZR): `add sp, saved, #0` moves the real SP, where a register-register ORR `mov` (reg 31 = XZR) would write XZR. Rd=sp=31 is BAKED; operand0(sp) wires into rd (IDEMPOTENT with the baked 31 — sp's hwEncoding IS 31, mirroring sub_sp_reg's idempotent operand0→rn), operand1(saved) wires into Rn (bits 5..9, the source). result:none (SP mutates in place — NOT an SSA value; NEVER the sp_copy-with-SP-as-result shape, audit fix #5). A DISTINCT mnemonic so it stays hasSideEffects=true (reads/writes the physical SP; no pass may drop or reorder it across the sub_sp_reg).
MUL Xd, Xn, Xm = MADD Xd, Xn, Xm, XZR. Base = 0x9B000000 | (XZR=31 << 10) = 0x9B007C00. Slots: Rd, Rn, Rm (Ra=XZR baked into fixedWord).

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: MUL Wd, Wn, Wm = MADD Wd, Wn, Wm, WZR — 0x1B007C00 (the X-form 0x9B007C00 with sf=0; the W product IS the C unsigned-int product mod 2^32).

opcodes.$comment: c103 (D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-UMULH): UMULH Xd, Xn, Xm — the high 64 bits of the unsigned 64x64 128-bit product. fixedWord 0x9BC07C00: data-processing (3-source) with op31=110 (bits 23:21 — UMULH; SMULH=010 → 0x9B407C00, MADD/MUL=000 → 0x9B007C00) + Ra=XZR(11111) baked in, o0=0, sf=1 (audit-recomputed vs the ARM ARM). The MIR->LIR Rule-1 NATIVE realization of MIR UMulH: a result-bearing 3-address op, no implicit registers, no pre-op (contrast x86's mov-rax + umul_op core). UMULH is inherently 64-bit (no W-form); the u64 `__umulh` is the only consumer, so a single width-64 variant.

FC17.9(b) (D-CSUBSET-BITCOUNT-INTRINSICS): CLZ Xd, Xn — count leading zeros (data-processing 1-source). fixedWord 0xDAC01000 (X, sf=1 = 3670020096) / 0x5AC01000 (W, sf=0 = 1522536448); opcode field 000100 (RBIT=000000 below; REV16/32=00000x/00001x). Rn (bits 9:5) = the source operand (wire 0), Rd (bits 4:0) = the result. arm64 CLZ is DEFINED at 0 = the width (32/64) — EXACTLY the MIR Clz contract — so it is Clz's NATIVE realization (the DSS `clz` verb, shared with x86 LZCNT). Also the 2nd half of arm64's ctz: RBIT then CLZ. A 1-source op like `neg`/`not` but the operand wires to `rn` (data-proc-1-source) not `rm`.

FC17.9(b) (D-CSUBSET-BITCOUNT-INTRINSICS): RBIT Xd, Xn — reverse the bit order (data-processing 1-source, opcode field 000000). fixedWord 0xDAC00000 (X = 3670016000) / 0x5AC00000 (W = 1522532352). Rn (bits 9:5) = source (wire 0), Rd (bits 4:0) = result. Used ONLY by arm64's ctz realization: ctz(x) = CLZ(RBIT(x)) — reversing turns the lowest set bit into the highest, so leading-zeros of the reversed value = trailing-zeros of the original (defined at 0 = width via CLZ(0)=width). x86 declares no `rbit` (it has direct TZCNT).

D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-BSWAP: byte reverse — a structural clone of `clz`/`rbit` above (data-processing 1-source: Rn bits 9:5 = source (wire 0), Rd bits 4:0 = result), differing ONLY in the opcode field (bits 15:10) and, at 64 bits, sf. Base words: 0x5AC00000 (W, sf=0) / 0xDAC00000 (X, sf=1), cross-validated against the shipped `rbit` (opcode 000000 -> 0x5AC00000) and `clz` (opcode 000100 -> 0x5AC01000) rows. THREE width-keyed variants, because arm64 — unlike x86 — encodes all three widths natively, so MIR Bswap never needs the universal-ALU expansion here:  width 16 -> REV16 Wd,Wn, opcode 000001 -> 0x5AC00400 = 1522533376;  width 32 -> REV Wd,Wn, opcode 000010 with sf=0 -> 0x5AC00800 = 1522534400;  width 64 -> REV Xd,Xn, opcode 000011 with sf=1 -> 0xDAC00C00 = 3670019072. ★★ THE 32-BIT SLOT IS **REV W-FORM**, NOT REV32 — a trap worth stating because the mnemonic reads like the right one and the deferred-anchor registry row named it wrongly. AArch64 `REV32` is X-FORM ONLY (0xDAC00800, opcode 000010 with sf=1) and reverses the bytes WITHIN EACH 32-BIT HALF of a 64-bit register — a DIFFERENT operation. A 32-bit byte swap is REV at sf=0. ★ REV16 IS PER-HALFWORD: `REV16 Wd,Wn` reverses the bytes of EACH halfword of the W register independently, so its low 16 bits are the correct swap of the input's low 16 bits REGARDLESS of what sits above them — which is exactly why the width-16 arm is safe against DSS's lazy-narrowing model (a U16 value may carry stale bits 31:16). Its OWN bits 31:16 are then the swapped garbage; that is permitted for a U16 result and the consumer's UXTH narrows it. Do NOT 'fix' this by substituting REV at width 16: REV would reverse all four bytes and put the input's bits 31:24 into the result's low byte — a silent wrong answer.

c104 (D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-ATOMIC-CAS): LDAXR Wt/Xt, [Xn] — load-acquire EXCLUSIVE (arms the exclusive monitor; the acquire half of the LL/SC CAS loop). W-form 0x885FFC00 = size=10 | 001000 | o2=0 L=1 o1=0 | Rs=11111 | o0=1 | Rt2=11111 | Rn | Rt; X-form flips size to 11 -> 0xC85FFC00. Result = the loaded value (Rt, bits 4:0 = the `rd` slot); operand 0 = the address base (Rn). The MIR AtomicCas value width picks W (the Win32 LONG i32 CAS) vs X.

c104 (D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-ATOMIC-CAS): STLXR Ws, Wt/Xt, [Xn] — store-release EXCLUSIVE (succeeds iff the monitor armed by LDAXR is still held; the release half of the LL/SC loop). W-form 0x8800FC00 = size=10 | 001000 | o2=0 L=0 o1=0 | Rs | o0=1 | Rt2=11111 | Rn | Rt; X-form 0xC800FC00. Result = the STATUS register Ws (0=stored, 1=monitor lost -> retry) — it lives in the Rs bit-field (20:16), which is the generic `rm` slot position, so resultSlot:'rm' (the slot vocabulary is bit-positional, not role-named). Operand 0 = the stored value (Rt, bits 4:0 = the `rd` slot position — an operand MAY wire to rd, the MOVK dest-wire precedent); operand 1 = the address base (Rn). The value width picks W vs X; the status is ALWAYS a W write (zero-extending — the loop's `cmp status, #0` runs at the default 64-bit width on the strength of that zero-extension).

FC17.9(d) atomic Phase C (D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC): LDAR Wt/Xt, [Xn] — load-ACQUIRE (RCsc), the acquire/seq_cst realization of MIR AtomicLoad. Derived from LDAXR by SETTING o2 (bit 23): LDAR = LDAXR | (1<<23). W-form 0x88DFFC00 (= 0x885FFC00 | 0x800000), X-form 0xC8DFFC00. VERIFIED by aarch64-as: `ldar w0,[x0]`=88dffc00, `ldar x0,[x0]`=c8dffc00. LDAR has NO offset field (addresses [Xn], disp 0), so the UNIFIED [ptr, MemBase, MemOffset] shape (which x86's mov-load needs) wires ptr->Rn (bits 5..9), result->Rd (bits 0..4 = Rt, the loaded value), MemBase->membase.noscale + MemOffset->memoffset.zero (width-0 markers; memoffset.zero FAILS LOUD on a nonzero disp — a naturally-aligned atomic is always offset 0, the base+index-lea precedent). Value width picks W (i32 / _Atomic int) vs X (i64 / pointer).

FC17.9(d) atomic Phase C (D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC): STLR Wt/Xt, [Xn] — store-RELEASE (RCsc), the release/acq_rel realization of MIR AtomicStore. Derived from STLXR by SETTING o2 (bit 23) AND baking Rs=11111 (STLR has NO status output, unlike STLXR whose Rs is the status reg): STLR = 0x8800FC00 | (1<<23) | (0x1F<<16) = 0x889FFC00 (W), 0xC89FFC00 (X). VERIFIED by aarch64-as: `stlr w0,[x0]`=889ffc00, `stlr x0,[x0]`=c89ffc00. result:none (no status reg). UNIFIED [value, ptr, MemBase, MemOffset] shape (the STUR store precedent): value->Rd (bits 0..4 = Rt data reg), ptr->Rn (bits 5..9), MemBase->membase.noscale + MemOffset->memoffset.zero (fail-loud nonzero disp). Value width picks W vs X.

FC17.9(d) atomic Phase C (D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC): STLR again — the SEQ_CST realization of MIR AtomicStore. LDAR/STLR are RCsc, so a release store IS a seq_cst store on arm64 (NO DMB) — BOTH the store_release and store_seqcst slots bind the IDENTICAL STLR encoding (the x86 twin diverges: store_release=mov, store_seqcst=xchg). Same words/wiring as store_release above (W 0x889FFC00, X 0xC89FFC00). Declared so the pure-slot-presence probe finds a seq_cst-store realization on arm64 (never fail-loud on a legal seq_cst store).

D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-FENCE (+ D-CSUBSET-SYNC-BUILTIN-BARRIER): DMB ISH — the STANDALONE seq_cst CPU fence MIR AtomicFence (__sync_synchronize) lowers to. 0xD5033BBF (3573758911), MEASURED via clang -c -arch arm64 + otool -t on `__sync_synchronize()` (this machine, 2026-07-30); cross-checked against the acquire-only `__atomic_thread_fence(__ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)` = dmb ishld 0xD50339BF — the two differ in exactly the CRm nibble (ISH=0xB full barrier vs ISHLD=0x9 load-only), so a transposed word FAILS the byte-pin. Zero operands, no result, no register fields — a fixed word (the setcc no-wire shape, minus the result). NOTE the deliberate asymmetry with store_seqcst above: STLR (RCsc) needs NO DMB when fencing a STORE it fuses with, but a store-LESS __sync_synchronize() call site (sqlite3MemoryBarrier) has no STLR to lean on — the standalone fence must be a real DMB ISH.

FC1 V2-4.X (2026-06-10): NEG Xd, Xm = SUB Xd, XZR, Xm (shifted-register alias, Rn=XZR baked). Base = 0xCB000000 | (XZR=31 << 5) = 0xCB0003E0. Slots: Rd, Rm. Surfaced by the modulo corpus' negative literals — under the BASELINE (no-ConstFold) pipeline a unary minus reaches LIR as a live `neg`, and arm64 had never declared one (every prior arm64 corpus avoided unary minus).

opcodes.$comment: Cluster-F F2 (core_bitwise): bitwise NOT (one's complement) — MVN Xd, Xm = ORN Xd, XZR, Xm (logical shifted-register alias, Rn=XZR baked, like NEG=SUB Xd,XZR,Xm above). arm64 had NO `not` opcode (the MIR Not op's LIR mnemonic), so source-level `~` failed L_RequiredLirOpcodeMissing while x86 had it. ORN = the ORR family (opc=01) with the N bit (bit 21) set; base = 0xAA2003E0 (sf=1 | opc=01 | 01010 | shift=0 | N=1 | Rm=00000[wire] | imm6=0 | Rn=11111[XZR] | Rd=00000[result]). 3-address native (no requires2Address — Rd and Rm differ, like neg/sdiv). Slots: Rd (result), Rm (wire 0).

variants.$comment: MVN Wd, Wm = ORN Wd, WZR, Wm — 0x2A2003E0 (the X-form 0xAA2003E0 with sf=0).

opcodes.$comment: FC1 V2-4.X (2026-06-10): SDIV Xd, Xn, Xm — data-processing (2 source), sf=1. Base = 0x9AC00C00 (sf=1 | S=0 | 11010110 | Rm[20:16] | opcode 000011[15:10] | Rn[9:5] | Rd[4:0]). The MIR→LIR div lowering's Rule-1 NATIVE realization: result-bearing 3-address op, no implicit registers, no pre-op (contrast x86 cqo+idiv_op). ARM64 SDIV never traps — divide-by-zero yields 0 and INT_MIN/-1 wraps (A-profile), so the C-UB divide cases are non-trapping on this target. SMod has no hardware instruction: the lowering realizes rem = n - (n/d)*d via sdiv + the fused `msub` (D-LIR-MOD-MSUB-FUSION ✅ closed FC3.5 sweep-c3; the generic mul+sub expansion remains the fallback for targets without a fused op).

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: SDIV Wd, Wn, Wm — 0x1AC00C00 (the X-form 0x9AC00C00 with sf=0; ARM ARM C6.2.250 data-processing 2-source).

opcodes.$comment: FC1 V2-4.X (2026-06-10): UDIV Xd, Xn, Xm — base = 0x9AC00800 (opcode field 000010 vs SDIV's 000011). Unsigned divide; same Rule-1 native shape as sdiv. UMod expands via udiv+mul+sub.

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: UDIV Wd, Wn, Wm — 0x1AC00800 (the X-form 0x9AC00800 with sf=0).

opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c3 (D-LIR-MOD-MSUB-FUSION): MSUB Xd, Xn, Xm, Xa = Xa − Xn·Xm — data-processing (3 source), ARM ARM C6.2.230: sf [31] | 00 [30:29] | 11011 [28:24] | 000 [23:21] | Rm [20:16] | o0=1 sub [15] | Ra [14:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0]. X-base = 0x9B000000 | (1<<15) = 0x9B008000 (the MADD base the `mul` alias builds on, with o0=1). The MIR→LIR rule-3 remainder expansion PREFERS this fused form when declared: msub r, q, d, n = n − q·d in ONE instruction (operand 0 = quotient → rn, operand 1 = divisor → rm, operand 2 = dividend → ra), replacing the generic mul+sub pair. First consumer of the fixed32 `ra` slot (bits 10..14).

variants.$comment: MSUB Wd, Wn, Wm, Wa — 0x1B008000 (the X-form 0x9B008000 with sf=0; the W result IS the C 32-bit remainder mod 2^32).

opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c1 (D-CSUBSET-32BIT-ALU-FORMS shifts residue): LSLV Xd, Xn, Xm — logical shift left, variable. Data-processing (2 source) like sdiv/udiv: sf [31] | 0 0 [30:29] | 11010110 [28:21] | Rm [20:16] | opcode 001000 LSLV [15:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] (ARM ARM C6.2.215) = base 0x9AC02000. NATIVE 3-address — no implicit registers, no count pin (contrast x86's CL contract); the MIR->LIR shift lowering's native arm emits ONE op. The hardware masks the count: Xm mod 64 (X-form) / Wm mod 32 (W-form, sf=0 = 0x1AC02000) — C declares counts >= width UB, so no masking is emitted. CONSTANT counts also ride this form (the count materializes through the const mov like any operand); the LSL-immediate alias (UBFM) is a peephole-class refinement, deliberately NOT declared this cycle.

variants.$comment: LSLV Wd, Wn, Wm — 0x1AC02000 (sf=0; count mod 32).

opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c1: LSRV Xd, Xn, Xm — LOGICAL shift right, variable (MIR LShr; zero-fill, unsigned operands). Same data-processing (2 source) shape; opcode field 001001 = base 0x9AC02400 (ARM ARM C6.2.217). W-form 0x1AC02400.

FC3.5 sweep-c1: ASRV Xd, Xn, Xm — ARITHMETIC shift right, variable (MIR AShr; sign-fill, signed operands). Opcode field 001010 = base 0x9AC02800 (ARM ARM C6.2.21). W-form 0x1AC02800. DSS defines C's implementation-defined negative >> as sign-fill on every target — same contract as x86 SAR.

AND Xd, Xn, Xm — logical shifted-register, base 0x8A000000. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 with `aarch64-linux-gnu-as` 2.42 + objdump: `and x0,x0,x0` = 0x8a000000, `and w0,w0,w0` = 0x0a000000, and the field placement is identical in both (`and w0,w1,w2` = 0x0a020020 ⇒ Rm[20:16], Rn[9:5], Rd[4:0]), so the two variants share one wire set.

NOT the same as the mov-alias which bakes Rn=XZR into the fixed word — this is the general-purpose 3-address OR. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 with `aarch64-linux-gnu-as` 2.42: `orr x0,x0,x0` = 0xaa000000, `orr w0,w0,w0` = 0x2a000000. ⓘ The W base cross-checks against `zext`'s own width-32 word 0x2A0003E0 = this base | (WZR=31<<5) — two independently-derived rows agreeing to the bit.

variants.$comment: ORR Wd, Wn, Wm — 0x2A000000 (the X-form 0xAA000000 with sf=0).

opcodes.$comment: D-AS3-COND-CODE-ARM64 (ARM64 control-flow): materialize a 0/1 GPR from the NZCV flags by condition — the AArch64 analog of x86 `setcc`. ARM64 has no `setcc`; the canonical idiom is `CSET Xd, <cond>` = `CSINC Xd, XZR, XZR, invert(cond)` (when the INVERTED condition is FALSE — i.e. the requested condition is TRUE — the false-arm increments XZR→1; otherwise 0). Single fixed word base 0x9A9F07E0 (2594113504): sf=1, CSINC opcode, Rm=XZR=31<<16, Rn=XZR=31<<5, op2=01, Rd at bits 0..4. The cond nibble is placed at bits 12..15 (condBitPos=12) and INVERTED (condInvert=true) from the inst payload via condCodeFromPayload + the schema's condCodeEncoding table. LIR shape mirrors x86 setcc: result=value, ZERO value operands (reads FLAGS), cond from payload. lowerICmp emits `cmp` then `setcc(cond)` then `zext`. VERIFY: `cset x0, gt` = GT(0xC) inverted to 0xD at bits 12..15 = 0x9A9FD7E0.

variants.$comment: width 64 — `CSET Xd, <cc>` (0x9A9F07E0, sf=1). ★ THE `width` KEY IS NEW BESIDE THE width-32 SIBLING BELOW AND IS NOT OPTIONAL: `variantMatchesInst` reads an ABSENT width as MATCH-ANY, so a match-any variant beside a width-keyed one either shadows it (if first) or silently absorbs the widths it does not declare (if last) — `validateTargetSchema`'s convergence-fix D refuses the mix outright (D-CSUBSET-32BIT-ALU-FORMS), which is why this key and the sibling below arrive together or not at all. ⓘ IT CHANGES NOTHING FOR THE COMPILER'S OWN PATH: every LIR `setcc` the C front-end emits comes from `lowerICmp`/`lowerFCmp`, which pass NO width flags, so `lirInstWidthBits(0)` = 64 and this guard is exactly what they already matched.

width 32 — `CSET Wd, <cc>` = CSINC Wd, WZR, WZR, invert(cc), fixed word 0x1A9F07E0 (446629856): the 64-bit word with sf CLEARED, and a genuinely DIFFERENT instruction rather than a spelling of the same one (the W-write zeroes bits 63:32 of the X register). ✔MEASURED 2026-08-15, `aarch64-linux-gnu-as` 2.42 + `aarch64-linux-gnu-objdump -d`, both widths in one file so the pair is read off ONE assembler run: `cset x0, eq` 9a9f17e0 / `cset w0, eq` 1a9f17e0 · `cset x1, ne` 9a9f07e1 / `cset w1, ne` 1a9f07e1 · `cset x0, ls` 9a9f87e0 / `cset w0, ls` 1a9f87e0. ⚠⚠ `condCodeFromPayload`/`condBitPos`/`condInvert` ARE REPEATED HERE ON PURPOSE AND ARE NOT REDUNDANT WITH THE ROW ABOVE: the inversion is a property of the CSET IDIOM (`CSET Xd,cc` IS `CSINC Xd,XZR,XZR,invert(cc)`), not of the operand width, so a 32-bit variant that omitted `condInvert` would encode the COMPLEMENT of every condition — green build, wrong branch taken. D-ASM-ARM64-SETCC-W-FORM-UNDECLARED.

opcodes.$comment: Zero-extend a 32-bit value to 64-bit — AArch64 `MOV Wd, Wm` = `ORR Wd, WZR, Wm` (a 32-bit register op auto-zeroes the upper 32 bits of the X register, so a W-form ORR IS the W→X zero-extend). Single fixed word base 0x2A0003E0 (704644064): sf=0 (32-bit), ORR opc=01, Rn=WZR=31<<5, Rd at bits 0..4, Rm (source) at bits 16..20 via the one reg wire. Mirrors x86_64's `zext` LIR shape: result=value, ONE reg operand. The natural consumer is lowerICmp's setcc→zext pair (a clean 0/1 r64); also reused by MIR ZExt. FC3.5 sweep-c1 (D-CSUBSET-ZEXT-32-TO-64) + D-CSUBSET-SUBNATIVE-ALU-FORMS: the variants are now WIDTH-KEYED (the byte/half forms below forced the split off match-any, per the convergence rule). This mov word (0x2A0003E0) realizes BOTH Bool (width 64) and U32 (width 32) — each zero-extends via the W-write (bits 63:32 cleared). The sub-native U16/U8 sources do NOT use the mov: a promoted U16/U8 register carries STALE upper bits the mov would copy, so they MASK via UBFM (UXTH 0x53003C00 / UXTB 0x53001C00). VERIFY: zext of w1→x0 via the mov form (Rd=0, Rm=1) = 0x2A0103E0.

variants.$comment: width 64 (Bool default, flags=0): MOV Wd, Wm = ORR Wd, WZR, Wm (0x2A0003E0). A Bool 0/1 register zero-extends to X via the W-write (bits 63:32 cleared). Width-keyed now that the byte/half forms below are declared (the convergence rule forbids a match-any sibling beside width-keyed ones).
width 32 (U32 source): the SAME MOV Wd, Wm (0x2A0003E0) — a full U32 in a W register zero-extends to X (the W-write zeroes 63:32). This IS the U32->U64 conversion.

width 16 (D-CSUBSET-SUBNATIVE-ALU-FORMS): UXTH Wd, Wn = UBFM Wd, Wn, #0, #15 (0x53003C00) — zero-extend the low HALF-WORD (the x86_64 movzx r64,r/m16 peer). MASKS to the low 16 bits, so a promoted U16 register's stale bits 31:16 are cleared (UNLIKE the width-32 mov, which would copy them). UBFM source is Rn (not Rm). Selected when the ZExt source type is U16 (width 16).

width 8 (D-CSUBSET-SUBNATIVE-ALU-FORMS): UXTB Wd, Wn = UBFM Wd, Wn, #0, #7 (0x53001C00) — zero-extend the low BYTE (the x86_64 movzx r64,r/m8 peer). MASKS to the low 8 bits. UBFM source is Rn (not Rm). Selected when the ZExt source type is U8 (width 8).

opcodes.$comment: FC3 c2 (D-CSUBSET-32BIT-ALU-FORMS): NEW opcode — sign-extend a 32-bit value to 64-bit. AArch64 `SXTW Xd, Wn` = the SBFM alias `SBFM Xd, Xn, #0, #31`: word 0x93407C00 = sf=1 [31] | opc=00 [30:29] | 100110 [28:23] | N=1 [22] | immr=000000 [21:16] | imms=011111 [15:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] (ARM ARM C6.2.263 SXTW / C6.2.234 SBFM). Mirrors x86_64's `sext` (movsxd r64, r/m32) LIR shape: result=value, ONE reg operand on the Rn slot. The MIR→LIR SExt gate admits I32 sources only — exactly this form's inherent width. First consumer: the LP64 `int` → `unsigned long` UAC conversion in the datamodel_runtime_width corpus.

variants.$comment: width 32: SXTW Xd, Wn (SBFM Xd,Xn,#0,#31 = 0x93407C00) — I32→I64. Width-keyed (was width-absent) now that the byte form below is declared — convergence-fix D forbids mixing a match-any sibling with a width-keyed one. The MIR→LIR SExt arm threads widthFlagsForType(source): an I32 source → width 32 → here.

width 8 (D-CSUBSET-CHAR-STRING-VALUE-CODEGEN): SXTB Xd, Wn = SBFM Xd, Xn, #0, #7 — sign-extend the low BYTE to 64 bits (the x86_64 `movsx r64,r/m8` peer). Word 0x93401C00 = the SXTW word with imms 31→7 (bits 15:10): sf=1 | opc=00 | 100110 | N=1 | immr=0 | imms=7 | Rn | Rd (ARM ARM C6.2.* SBFM/SXTB). Selected when the SExt source type is Char (width 8 on the LIR inst) — the char→int widening. Reads exactly the low byte (the char), so the source register's upper bits (zero-extended by the LDURB byte load) are irrelevant.

width 16 (D-CSUBSET-SUBNATIVE-ALU-FORMS): SXTH Xd, Wn = SBFM Xd, Xn, #0, #15 — sign-extend the low HALF-WORD to 64 bits (the x86_64 movsx r64,r/m16 peer). Word 0x93403C00 = the SXTW word with imms 31->15 (bits 15:10): sf=1 | opc=00 | 100110 | N=1 | immr=000000 | imms=001111 | Rn | Rd. Selected when the SExt source type is I16 (width 16) — the short->int widening. Reads exactly the low half-word, so the source register's upper bits are irrelevant.

opcodes.$comment: FC3 c2 (D-CSUBSET-32BIT-ALU-FORMS): NEW opcode — truncate a 64-bit value to 32 bits. AArch64 `MOV Wd, Wm` = `ORR Wd, WZR, Wm` (0x2A0003E0 — sf=0, Rn=WZR baked; the SAME word the `zext` opcode uses, because the ISA-level operation is identical: a W-register write zeroes the upper 32 bits). Two mnemonics deliberately exist over one word — each conversion mnemonic carries its INHERENT width pair (trunc: 64→32 mod-2^32, C's conversion semantics; zext: Bool/byte→64) and the MIR→LIR gates police each independently. The variant is WIDTH-KEYED 32 like x86's trunc: a Trunc to 16/8 bits reaching the assembler matches NOTHING and fails loud.

Allocate a stack-frame slot (virtual / pseudo-op — NO encoding, exactly like x86_64's `alloca`). Payload = spill-slot/local index threaded verbatim from MIR Alloca. Result is a pointer-class virtreg holding the slot's effective address. The ML7 callconv pass (lir_callconv) materializes this into a frame-relative `lea result, [sp + offset]` once the frame layout is known — target-blind, and arm64 already has `lea` (ADRP+ADD), so no encoder change is needed; this declaration just lets MIR Alloca lower on arm64. A function with body locals (`int n = 42;`) emits one alloca per local.

Direct AND indirect call, one mnemonic with per-callee-kind variants (FC4 c2). Direct call to a symbol — AArch64 `BL imm26` (branch-with-link); indirect call through a register — AArch64 `BLR Xn` (branch-with-link-to-register). Declared under the engine's GENERIC `call` verb (NOT the ISA spellings 'bl'/'blr'), the same convention every other opcode in this file already follows (`mov`=ORR-alias, `add`=ADD, `xor`=EOR, `or`=ORR): the target's mnemonics ARE the engine's verb vocabulary; the real ISA mnemonics live in this comment. This is what lets the format-blind trampoline emitter (`opcodeByMnemonic("call")`) and the MIR→LIR `MnemonicSlot::Call` resolve the call on ANY target — and keeping BLR a VARIANT (not a second opcode) keeps isCall / functionHasCalls / caller-saved-clobber semantics shared by construction. BL fixed-word base = 0x94000000 (opcode bits 26..31 = 0b100101); imm26 wire at bits 0..25 emits a call26 relocation, bits left at 0 (linker patches at link time). BLR fixed-word base = 0xD63F0000 with the callee register in the Rn slot (bits 5..9): BLR X9 = 0xD63F0120.

variants.$comment: FC4 c2: BLR Xn — 0xD63F0000 | Rn<<5 (indirect call through a register). fixedWord 3594452992 = 0xD63F0000; sanity precedent: the shipped ret row's 0xD65F03C0 = 3596551104 (RET X30, same D6 family).

opcodes.$comment: AArch64 SVC #0 = 0xD4000001 — supervisor call (the syscall instruction). Zero-operand at LIR level; the Linux AArch64 syscall ABI puts the syscall number in x8 (the format's processExit.syscallNumGpr), args in x0..x7, return in x0. Mirrors x86_64's `syscall` (0F 05). Added at D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64 so the entry trampoline can issue the exit_group syscall and terminate the process. fixedWord 3556769793 = 0xD4000001 (SVC with imm16=0).

Spill-reload pseudo-op (target-blind, NO encoding — exactly like x86_64's). Payload = spill-slot index. The ML7 callconv pass materializes this into the target's real `load` (the LDUR opcode below) ONLY when a function actually spills / restores a callee-saved reg; the spill-rewrite pass requires the mnemonic to EXIST upfront. A register-pressure-light leaf (e.g. `return 42`) never emits one.

Spill-store pseudo-op (target-blind, NO encoding). Payload = spill-slot index. Operand[0] = the physical reg being stored. Materialized into the target's real `store` (the STUR opcode below) by the ML7 callconv pass, only when a function spills / saves a callee-saved reg.

D-AS-REGALLOC-WIDE-CALL-OPERAND-COUNT (option E): outgoing-stack-arg store carrier (target-blind, NO encoding). Emitted by the PRE-REGALLOC wide-call lowering pass for every outgoing call argument beyond the cc's register-passed capacity (config: argGprs/argFprs = 8 GPR / 8 FPR on AAPCS64). Operand[0] = the arg VALUE vreg (regalloc assigns it; its live range ends HERE, not at the call). Payload = the arg's OVERFLOW SLOT INDEX (monotonic, source-order NSAA cursor). lir_callconv materializes it into `store operand, [sp + shadowSpaceBytes + payload*outgoingSlotSize]` (shadowSpaceBytes=0 on AAPCS64) via the STUR/scaled-STR chokepoint — byte-identical to the pre-existing placement-loop store. hasSideEffects=true so no pass reorders it off its call.

Memory LOAD — AArch64 LDUR Xt, [Xn, #simm9] (unscaled, signed 9-bit byte offset). Fixed word 0xF8400000 (size=11 64-bit, opc=01 load, unscaled mode bits 11..10 = 00). Operand layout (shared LIR load form): [base_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp)] + result. Wires: result→Rt (rd, bits 0..4), base_reg(index 0)→Rn (bits 5..9), MemOffset(index 2)→Imm9 (bits 12..20, signed). The MemBase(index 1) carries no AArch64 bits (scale must be 1; the walker validates it). The callconv materializes frame_load into this. Offset range -256..255; a wider frame fails loud (scaled LDR imm12 = future).

variants.$comment: width 64: LDUR Xt, [Xn, #simm9] (0xF8400000). width 8 (D-CSUBSET-CHAR-STRING-VALUE-CODEGEN): LDURB Wt, [Xn, #simm9] (0x38400000 — the LDUR word with size 11→00). Loads ONE byte, ZERO-extending it into Wt (and a W-write zeroes bits 63:32 of Xt) — a char/byte memory access MUST be byte-EXACT, a 64-bit LDUR of a 1-byte string/array element reads 7 bytes past it. ZERO-extend is the signedness-AGNOSTIC byte fetch (the x86_64 movzx peer); sign semantics live in the following SXTB cast (char→int), which re-reads the low byte. Same operand layout as the 64-bit form. Selected when the Load's result type is Char (width 8 via memAccessWidthFlags).

width 32 (D-LIR-INT-MEMORY-WIDTH-EXACT): LDUR Wt, [Xn, #simm9] (0xB8400000 — the LDUR word with size 11→10). Loads 4 bytes into Wt; a W-write zeroes bits 63:32 of Xt, so the int lands clean. A 4-byte int load MUST be width-exact — a 64-bit LDUR of a PACKED int element reads 4 bytes past it. Same operand layout as the 64-bit form. Selected when the Load's result type is a 4-byte integer (I32/U32, or `long` under LLP64) — width 32 via memAccessWidthFlags.

Loads 2 bytes, ZERO-extending into Wt (signedness-agnostic, the LDURB peer); the short→int promote (SXTH/UXTH = D-CSUBSET-SUBNATIVE-ALU-FORMS, not yet encoded ⇒ short VALUE use fails loud) re-reads the low half-word.
