opcodes.$comment: TLS C2 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): materialize the current thread's TLS base pointer (tp) into a GPR — the AArch64 form is `MRS Xd, TPIDR_EL0`, ONE self-contained fixed word 0xD53BD040 (3577466944 = MRS with op0=3 op1=3 CRn=13 CRm=0 op2=2, the EL0 software thread-ID register) | Rd at bits 0..4 (the standard `rd` slot — zero new slot vocabulary). ZERO-OPERAND shape, deliberately DIFFERENT from x86's 1-op `[memoffset]` row: the system-register read consumes NO memory operand and NO prefix byte, so the lowering's capability probe (lowerThreadLocalGlobalAddr) sees the `[]` variant and emits a bare `tlsbase %tp` — the format tlsAccess block's segmentPrefixByte/baseDisplacement are x86-template machinery this shape never reads (the arm64-ELF JSON declares them 0, inert). Pure read (no side effects); never a terminator. The paired tpoff ADD/ADD macro is the `lea` [reg, symbol] TLS variant below.

No-operation. ✔MEASURED (aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0, `-c` + aarch64-linux-gnu-objdump on a `.s` containing a bare `nop`): `d503201f` = 0xD503201F = 3573751839, one fixed word, no operands, no result — the canonical HINT #0 encoding.
★ `hasSideEffects: true` is load-bearing for the same reason as x86_64's `nop`: an instruction with no result and no declared effect is dead BY DEFINITION, and deleting it deletes the only thing it was ever for (alignment padding, a patch point, an `__asm__("nop")` written on purpose). ⚠ Honest scope: today's CSE/DCE/LICM read the MIR-tier flag (`src/opt/passes/{cse.cpp:84,dce.cpp:52,licm.cpp:93}`), so this is a correct declaration rather than a currently-live guard.

Read the Counter-timer Virtual Count register — AArch64's answer to x86's RDTSC, and the instruction sqlite's own `hwtime.h` uses on this CPU (`__asm__ volatile("mrs %0, cntvct_el0" : "=r"(cnt))`, the `"=r"` that the `asmConstraints` `r` row above binds).
✔MEASURED, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 + objdump, four destination registers assembled to separate the fixed word from the Rd field: `mrs x0` → d53be040, `x1` → d53be041, `x7` → d53be047, `x30` → d53be05e. ⇒ fixedWord = 0xD53BE040 = 3577471040, with Rd in bits 0..4 — the STANDARD `rd` slot, ZERO new slot vocabulary, structurally identical to the `tlsbase` row directly above (which measured d53bd040 for TPIDR_EL0 in the same run, confirming the two differ only in CRm: 13 vs 14).
★★ WHY THIS ROW IS NOT CALLED `mrs`, WHICH IS WHAT THE MACHINE MNEMONIC SAYS. `tlsbase` is ALSO an MRS (TPIDR_EL0). A row named `mrs` would therefore be the second MRS in this file and the FIRST one to claim the generic name, while encoding exactly one hardcoded system register and offering no slot in which to name another — `opcodeByMnemonic("mrs")` would resolve to something that can only ever read CNTVCT_EL0. This file names opcodes for the VALUE THEY PRODUCE (`tlsbase`, not `tpidr`), which keeps `mrs` free for a genuine general MRS if a system-register slot is ever justified by a consumer.
⚠ IT IS NOT A CYCLE COUNTER, and the name says so deliberately. CNTVCT_EL0 is a fixed-frequency system counter (typically ~24 MHz, scaled by CNTFRQ_EL0), NOT a per-cycle tick like the TSC. Calling it `cyclecounter` would have been the plausible wrong name; code that divides it by the CPU clock is wrong on this target.
★ `hasSideEffects: true`, and unlike `nop` this one guards a real silent miscompile: the counter is not a function of its (empty) operand list, so two reads must return two values. Declared pure, CSE folds the pair into one read and EVERY elapsed-time measurement becomes exactly zero, while LICM hoists the read out of the loop being timed. ⚠ NOTE THE CONTRAST WITH `tlsbase` ABOVE, which is correctly `false`: the TLS base is invariant for a thread, so folding two reads of it is a legitimate optimization. The two rows are otherwise the same instruction, and the flag is the only thing that distinguishes a value you may cache from one you may not.

Load-effective-address — AArch64 ADRP+ADD pair (D-AS4-3 multi-instruction macro-op materializing a module symbol's address into Xd). Mirrors x86_64's 1-operand RIP-relative `lea reg, [rip+sym]` so `lowerGlobalAddr` is target-blind: ONE SymbolRef operand wired into BOTH words. word0 = ADRP Xd, sym@PG (0x90000000=2415919104): Rd at bits 0..4; immlo[30:29]+immhi[23:5] left ZERO — the adr_prel_pg_hi21 reloc patches the ±4 GiB page delta. word1 = ADD Xd, Xd, #:lo12:sym (0x91000000=2432696320, the ADD-imm base shared with `add`'s imm variant): Rd at 0..4 AND Rn at 5..9 (BOTH = the result reg via extraResultSlots — ADD reads its own dest as the source base); imm12[21:10] left ZERO — the add_abs_lo12_nc reloc patches. Both relocs target the SAME symbol at byte offsets base+0 and base+4. The two `sym.patch` wires write NO immediate bits (the linker owns them); they carry only relocationKind + wordIndex.

variants.$commentResultRole: ★★★ THE TWO WORDS OF THIS MACRO READ ENCODING 31 DIFFERENTLY, WHICH IS WHY THE READING IS DECLARED PER PLACEMENT ([[D-ASM-ARM64-SP-AND-XZR-SHARE-ENCODING-31-SO-MOV-SP-SILENTLY-BECOMES-ZERO]]). Word 0 is ADRP, whose Rd is the ZERO register; word 1 is ADD (immediate), whose Rd and Rn are the STACK POINTER. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-03 before this key existed: `adr xzr, main` compiled rc=0 and emitted `adrp xzr, main` followed by **`add sp, sp, #:lo12:main`** — the stack pointer silently overwritten with a relocated address. ⓘ A destination must fit EVERY placement, so this macro now accepts only registers that carry no role at all — exactly the set for which the two readings name the same register. `adr x0, main` is untouched; `adr sp, main` was already refused, as it is by gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3.

variants.$comment: 2-op block-address form — ADRP+ADD of a SYNTHETIC per-block symbol (D-CSUBSET-COMPUTED-GOTO `&&label`). Byte-IDENTICAL to the 1-op `[symbol]` ADRP+ADD form above (same fixedWords, same Rd/Rn extraResultSlots, same two sym.patch wires emitting adr_prel_pg_hi21 on word0 + add_abs_lo12_nc on word1 against the SymbolRef at operand 0). The trailing BlockRef (operand 1) is METADATA, wired to NOTHING — it names the target LIR block so the assembler can bind the synthetic symbol to that block's byte offset (recorded as a BlockSymPatch; the linker assigns the interior-block VA). Distinct guard `[symbol, blockref]` so the variant matcher routes this 2-operand `lea` here instead of failing A_NoMatchingEncodingVariant.

FRAME-RELATIVE lea (single word) — `lea Xd, [base + #disp]` = AArch64 `ADD Xd, Xn, #imm12`. This is the form the ML7 callconv's `emitFrameAddr` materializes from `alloca` (a body-local's effective address): 3-op no-index shape [base_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp)] + result, MIRRORING x86_64's 3-op `lea` (so the callconv stays target-blind — it emits the same operand layout for both ISAs). Single fixed word 0x91000000 (2432696320, the ADD-imm base, shared with `add`'s imm variant + the SymbolRef lea's word1): base_reg→Rn (bits 5..9), result→Rd (bits 0..4), MemOffset→Imm12 (UNSIGNED, bits 10..21; frame offsets are non-negative). MemBase carries no AArch64 bits (scale must be 1; the walker validates it via membase.noscale). `immMax:4095` routes ONLY a frame offset ≤4095 here; a larger offset falls through to the 2-word shifted variant below (D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-IMM12).

FRAME-RELATIVE lea (shifted imm12 word-pair, D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-IMM12) — `lea Xd, [base + #disp]` with disp in (4095, 0xFFFFFF]. The GEP's array-element address (e.g. `int big[9000]; big[8999]` at sp+35996) under a >4095-byte frame. Emits TWO words reusing ADD's base: word0 = `ADD Xd, Xn, #(disp & 0xFFF)` (0x91000000, sh=0), word1 = `ADD Xd, Xd, #((disp>>12) & 0xFFF), LSL #12` (0x91400000, sh=1). SCRATCH-FREE: word0 reads the base (Xn) into Xd, word1 reads Xd→Xd (extraResultSlots thread the result reg into word1.Rd AND word1.Rn). The MemOffset (operand 2) is the VALUE-bearing operand the matcher keys on; its single imm12.hilo24 wire (word0) carries the displacement, split lo→word0 / hi→word1 by the encoder. MemBase (operand 1, scale==1) carries no bits (membase.noscale, word0). `immMin:4096`/`immMax:16777215`; a >16MiB offset stays fail-loud (D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-16MIB). width:64 (a frame address is Ptr-width); the disjoint imm-range makes it unambiguous against the single-word variant above regardless of width.

FRAME-RELATIVE lea (MOVZ/MOVK + EXTENDED-register 3-word form, D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-16MIB) — `lea Xd, [sp + #disp]` with disp in (0xFFFFFF, 0x7FFFFFFF] (>16 MiB, ≤2 GiB). The GEP's high-element address (e.g. `int big[5000000]; big[4999999]` at sp+~20MB) under a >16MiB frame. Emits THREE words, SCRATCH-FREE: the displacement materializes into the lea's DEST reg Xd, then an extended-register ADD off sp. word0 = `MOVZ Xd, #(disp & 0xFFFF)` (0xD2800000, Rd=Xd via resultSlot), word1 = `MOVK Xd, #((disp>>16) & 0xFFFF), LSL #16` (0xF2A00000, Rd=Xd via extraResultSlots word1.rd), word2 = `ADD Xd, sp, Xd` (the EXTENDED-register form 0x8B2063E0: option=011 UXTX, bit 21 set, Rn=sp=31 baked, Rd=Xd + Rm=Xd via extraResultSlots word2.rd/word2.rm). The dest reg threads through ALL THREE words (resultSlot=rd word0 + three extraResultSlots) — no separate scratch needed. The MemOffset (operand 2) is the VALUE-bearing operand the matcher keys on; its single imm32.movzmovk wire (word0) carries the displacement, split lo16→word0 / hi16→word1 by the encoder. Operand 0 (base=sp) → word2's `rn` (re-confirming the baked sp=31); operand 1 (membase, scale==1) → membase.noscale (word2, no bits). `immMin:16777216`/`immMax:2147483647`; a >2GiB offset goes negative through int32 → fail-loud (D-ASM-AARCH64-FRAME-OFFSET-BEYOND-2GIB).

NEGATIVE-DISP lea (single word, D-AS4-ARM64-NEGATIVE-DISP-LEA-NATIVE-SUB) — `lea Xd, [base + #disp]` with disp in [-4095, -1] = AArch64 `SUB Xd, Xn, #|disp|`. The `p[-1]`/`z[-1]` char-buffer lookback (a NEGATIVE const-disp GEP) that x86 encodes in one signed-disp32 `lea` but arm64's UNSIGNED imm12 ADD form could not — c94 gives it a NATIVE single-instruction SUB (replacing c93's materialize-into-a-fresh-GPR + base+index fold, which cost 5-7 instructions incl. a dead const). The negative MIRROR of the positive `ADD Xd,Xn,#imm12` variant above, op-bit SET: single fixed word 0xD1000000 (3506438144 = the ADD-imm base 0x91000000 | 0x40000000, sf=1 op=1 sub S=0 sh=0), shared with `sub`'s imm12 variant. base_reg→Rn (5..9), result→Rd (0..4), MemOffset→Imm12 (bits 10..21 — the encoder writes |disp| there; the SUB base makes it a subtract). MemBase carries no bits (scale must be 1, membase.noscale). `negValue:true` routes ONLY a NEGATIVE memoffset here (the sign matcher); `immMax:4095` bounds |disp|≤4095 (a larger magnitude falls through to the shifted / MOVZ-MOVK negative variants below). SUB imm encoding verified vs ARM ARM C6.2.* (add/subtract immediate: sf|op|S|100010|sh|imm12|Rn|Rd) + aarch64-gcc objdump.

NEGATIVE-DISP lea (shifted imm12 word-pair, D-AS4-ARM64-NEGATIVE-DISP-LEA-NATIVE-SUB) — `lea Xd, [base + #disp]` with |disp| in (4095, 0xFFFFFF]. The negative mirror of the positive shifted-imm12 ADD word-pair, op-bit SET: word0 = `SUB Xd, Xn, #(|disp| & 0xFFF)` (0xD1000000, sh=0), word1 = `SUB Xd, Xd, #((|disp|>>12) & 0xFFF), LSL #12` (0xD1400000 = 0xD1000000|0x400000, sh=1). SCRATCH-FREE: word1 reads its OWN dest (Xd) — extraResultSlots thread the result reg into word1.Rd AND word1.Rn. The MemOffset (operand 2) is the sign-matched value operand; its single imm12.hilo24 wire (word0) carries |disp|, split lo→word0 / hi→word1 by the encoder. `negValue:true` + `immMin:4096`/`immMax:16777215` (|disp| magnitude); a >16MiB magnitude falls through to the MOVZ/MOVK form below. Fixed words = the `sub` opcode's shifted word-pair.

NEGATIVE-DISP lea (MOVZ/MOVK + EXTENDED-register 3-word form, D-AS4-ARM64-NEGATIVE-DISP-LEA-NATIVE-SUB) — `lea Xd, [base + #disp]` with |disp| in (0xFFFFFF, 0x7FFFFFFF]. The negative mirror of the positive MOVZ/MOVK 3-word form, op-bit SET on the operation word. SCRATCH-FREE: |disp| materializes into the lea's DEST reg Xd, then an EXTENDED-register SUB off the base. word0 = `MOVZ Xd, #(|disp| & 0xFFFF)` (0xD2800000, Rd=Xd via resultSlot), word1 = `MOVK Xd, #((|disp|>>16) & 0xFFFF), LSL #16` (0xF2A00000, Rd=Xd via extraResultSlots word1.rd), word2 = `SUB Xd, Xn, Xd` (the EXTENDED-register form 0xCB206000: sf=1 op=1 sub, option=011 UXTX bits 15:13, bit 21 set, Rn=base wired 5..9, Rd=Xd + Rm=Xd via extraResultSlots word2.rd/word2.rm). Unlike the POSITIVE 3-word form (which bakes Rn=sp=31), the NEGATIVE form WIRES Rn to the base register (operand 0, word2) — a derived-pointer `p[-N]` base, not sp. The dest reg threads through all three words. MemOffset (operand 2) sign-matched; its imm32.movzmovk wire (word0) carries |disp|, split lo16→word0 / hi16→word1. `negValue:true` + `immMin:16777216`/`immMax:2147483647`; a magnitude > 2 GiB flows through int32 as a value whose |x| is unrepresentable → no variant → fail-loud (the residual, mirrors the positive >2GiB gap). SUB-extended base 0xCB206000 = the positive lea word2 0x8B2063E0 minus the baked Rn=sp (0x3E0) with the ADD op-bit flipped to SUB (0x8B→0xCB), verified by bit-decode.

BASE+INDEX lea (D-AS4-ARM64-BASE-INDEX-LEA) — `lea Xd, [base + index*1 + 0]` = AArch64 `ADD Xd, Xn, Xm` (shifted-register add, LSL #0). The 4-op form `lowerGep` emits for an indexed pointer access `p[n]` ([base_reg, index_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp=0)]), MIRRORING x86_64's 4-op SIB lea so the GEP stays target-blind (closing the gap that made `p[n]` fail loud on arm64 for int AND char alike). The GEP emits scale=1 + disp=0 ALWAYS today, so this single ADD is the complete realization: base→Rn (5..9), index→Rm (16..20), result→Rd (0..4); MemBase→membase.noscale (scale MUST be 1, fail-loud) and MemOffset→memoffset.zero (disp MUST be 0 — the register-add form has NO displacement field, and bits 10..21 overlap Rm so an Imm12 wiring would corrupt it; fail-loud on nonzero). Fixed word 0x8B000000 (the ADD reg-reg base, shared with `add`'s reg-reg variant). A scale!=1 (typed-array Gep scaling by sizeof(T)) needs the shifted form `ADD Xd,Xn,Xm,LSL #log2(scale)` — a FUTURE consumer (D-AS4-ARM64-INDEXED-LEA-SCALE, co-design with ML6 address-mode synthesis), NOT built speculatively.

TLS C2 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): 2-op thread-pointer-offset form — `lea Xd, [tp + tpoff(sym)]` = the AArch64 local-exec ADD/ADD hi12/lo12 word-pair (gcc -ftls-model=local-exec parity): word0 = `ADD Xd, Xn(tp), #hi12, LSL #12` (0x91400000 = ADD-imm sh=1, imm12 field ZERO — reloc tls-tprel-hi12 patches (S+A)>>12 in, range-checked [0, 0xFFFFFF]), word1 = `ADD Xd, Xd, #lo12` (0x91000000 = ADD-imm sh=0, imm12 ZERO — reloc tls-tprel-lo12 patches (S+A)&0xFFF in, magnitude-free). S = the POSITIVE Variant-I tpoff the walker bit-cast into symbolVa (addTlsSymbolOffsets). SCRATCH-FREE via the SAME extraResultSlots threading the ADRP+ADD [symbol] variant above uses: word1 reads its own dest (Xd → word1.Rd AND word1.Rn). Operand 0 (the `tlsbase`-produced tp reg) → word0.Rn; operand 1 (the SymbolRef) emits BOTH relocations through the generic sym.patch marker — at word offsets 0 and 4 of the macro, both against the same symbol. Distinct guard [reg, symbol] — no other lea variant carries that shape. The x86 twin is the [reg, symbol] memreloc.disp32 lea in x86_64.target.json; the LIR the lowering emits is IDENTICAL (tlsbase reg + lea [reg, sym]) — only the declared encodings differ.

opcodes.$comment: D-LK-ARM64-EXTERN-DATA-ADDR-PIE-GOT (TF-C52): GOT-address materialization macro -- `adrp Xd,:got:sym` + `ldr Xd,[Xd,:got_lo12:sym]`. Loads the RUN-TIME address of an undefined/preemptible extern (function OR data) OUT of a GOT slot the FINAL (foreign) linker synthesizes, so a foreign default-PIE link of the emitted relocatable `.o`/`.a` accepts it (an absolute ADRP+ADD page-pair against a symbol that may bind externally is rejected 'when making a shared object'). A DISTINCT MnemonicSlot (the `tlsbase` precedent), NOT a new `lea` variant -- a `lea` `[symbol]` variant would COLLIDE with the existing absolute ADRP+ADD `[symbol]` lea (ambiguous encoder match); MIR->LIR `lowerGlobalAddr`'s value-form arm emits THIS mnemonic explicitly (keyed on the capability-derived `externAddrGotSymbols_` set) for an `&extern` VALUE. word0 = ADRP Xd, sym@GOTPAGE (0x90000000=2415919104): Rd at bits 0..4 via resultSlot; immlo[30:29]+immhi[23:5] left ZERO -- the adr_got_page reloc (R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE) patches the GOT-page delta. word1 = LDR Xd, [Xd, #:got_lo12:sym] (0xF9400000=4181721088, the 64-bit unsigned-offset LDR base shared with `load_u`'s width-64 word): Rt at 0..4 AND Rn at 5..9 (BOTH = the result reg via extraResultSlots -- the LDR reads the ADRP page-base register into itself); imm12[21:10] left ZERO -- the ld64_got_lo12 reloc (R_AARCH64_LD64_GOT_LO12_NC) patches the scaled slot offset. BYTE-STRUCTURE-IDENTICAL to the ADRP+ADD `lea` `[symbol]` variant (same resultSlot/extraResultSlots threading) except the 2nd word is an LDR (a load, not an add) and the two sym.patch wires carry the GOT relocs. DSS never APPLIES these relocs (the exec_reloc_apply kernel arm fail-loud-refuses); the foreign linker resolves the GOT slot.

D-AS3-BLOCK-REL-IMM19/26 (ARM64 conditional control-flow): integer compare writing the NZCV flags, no GPR result. AArch64 `CMP Xn, Xm` is an alias for `SUBS XZR, Xn, Xm` (subtract-and-set-flags discarding the result into the zero register). Fixed word 0xEB00001F = SUBS (sf=1, op=1, S=1) with Rd=31 (XZR) baked in; Rn at bits 5..9, Rm at bits 16..20. Mirrors x86's `cmp` LIR shape (InvalidLirReg result, 2 reg operands) — ML5 lowerICmp + lowerCondBr emit it before the conditional branch. NO resultSlot (the flags are the implicit output). Reuses the Rn/Rm slots already exercised by the add/sub reg-reg variants.

variants.$comment: FC3 c2: CMP Wn, Wm = SUBS WZR, Wn, Wm — 0x6B00001F (the X-form 0xEB00001F with sf=0). A U32 compare MUST read 32 bits — a bitcast-from-negative operand carries sign-extended upper bits the X-form would misread.

FC3.5 sweep-c1: CMP Xn, #imm12 = SUBS XZR, Xn, #imm12 — add/subtract (immediate), ARM ARM C6.2.395: sf=1 [31] | op=1 sub [30] | S=1 [29] | 100010 [28:23] | sh=0 [22] | imm12 [21:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd=XZR=31 [4:0] = 0xF100001F. FIRST consumer: the MIR->LIR non-fused CondBr arm's `cmp cond, #0` over a PHI-produced Bool (a short-circuit `&&`/`||` result used as an if/while condition cannot fuse with its compare). x86's cmp had its reg-imm form from the start; this arm64 gap was masked until the S2 marker fix let logical-op conditions reach codegen. Reuses the Imm12 slot (bits 10..21) the callconv's sub-sp frame adjust already exercises; the walker range-checks 0..4095 fail-loud.
FC3.5 sweep-c1: CMP Wn, #imm12 — the X-form with sf=0: 0x7100001F. The 32-bit sibling per the FC3-c2 width axis (a U32-typed Bool-ish compare reads 32 bits).

opcodes.$comment: D-AS3-BLOCK-REL-IMM19/26: unconditional intra-function jump. AArch64 `B <label>` (encoding 0x14000000, opcode bits 26..31 = 0b000101). The 26-bit imm field (bits 0..25, SCALED by 4) is the SIGNED word displacement to the target block — resolved at ASSEMBLE time via the Imm26 slot + per-function patch list (NOT a linker relocation; the same Imm26 slot is symbol-bearing for the BL/`call` form, but a BlockRef operand here selects the intra-function path). Operand[0] is a BlockRef naming the target basic block. Mirrors x86's `jmp` (E9 rel32). Imm26's ±128 MiB reach covers any single function.

D-CSUBSET-COMPUTED-GOTO: indirect branch `BR Xn` — 0xD61F0000 | Rn<<5 (unconditional branch to a register, NO link/return-address — the BLR sibling captures one). fixedWord 3592355840 = 0xD61F0000; mirrors the BLR row (0xD63F0000, same D6 family — BR clears bit 21). Rn at bits 5..9 via the `rn` slot. The MIR IndirectBr lowers to this; the target-address register is materialized by a preceding adrp+add `lea` of the target block's synthetic symbol (BlockAddress). terminatorKind indirect-br → variadic address-taken successors.

D-AS3-BLOCK-REL-IMM19/26: conditional intra-function jump with mandatory fallthrough. 2-WORD macro: `B.cond <ifTrue>` (word 0) then `B <ifFalse>` (word 1) — the AArch64 analog of x86's `0F 8x rel32; E9 rel32` compound. word0 = B.cond base 0x54000000 (opcode bits 24..31 = 0b01010100, bit 4 = 0); the cond nibble (bits 0..3) comes from the inst's payload (TargetCondCode) via `condCodeFromPayload` + the schema's `condCodeEncoding` table; the 19-bit signed PC-relative offset (bits 5..23, scaled by 4) goes to the Imm19 slot → ifTrue block. word1 = B base 0x14000000 with the Imm26 slot → ifFalse (fallthrough) block. Both displacements resolve at assemble time (BlockRef operands, no relocation). operand[0]=ifTrue (taken when cond holds), operand[1]=ifFalse. D-OPT-JCC-FALLTHROUGH: the SECOND variant is the FALLTHROUGH FORM — word0 alone, 4 bytes instead of 8 — selected by OPERAND COUNT when `lir_peephole`'s rule R2 drops the trailing BlockRef operand because ifFalse IS the next-laid-out block, both successors staying on the block. `lir_verifier`'s Rule 1b refuses the shortened operand list wherever that unnamed successor is not the block laid out next. Mirrors the x86 jcc wiring + the lea multi-word fixedWords+wordIndex shape.

variants.$comment: D-OPT-JCC-FALLTHROUGH: the FALLTHROUGH FORM. Word 0 alone — `B.cond <ifTrue>` (base 0x54000000 + the payload cond nibble, Imm19 → ifTrue) — WITHOUT the trailing `B <ifFalse>` word: 4 bytes instead of 8. Note `fixedWord` (singular) rather than `fixedWords`: a one-word macro is a one-word template, and the Imm19 wire drops its `wordIndex` with it. Selected when the instruction carries ONE BlockRef operand instead of two, which `lir_peephole`'s rule R2 produces by dropping the trailing operand once the ifFalse successor IS the next-laid-out block.

opcodes.$comment: c78 (D-CSUBSET-FLOAT-NEG-ENCODING): FNEG Dd, Dn — scalar double floating-point NEGATE, FP data-processing (1 source). arm64 has a NATIVE fp-negate (unlike x86, which has no fneg instruction and takes the sign-mask XORPD fallback in mir_to_lir — the two realizations diverge by CAPABILITY, probed via this opcode's declared-encoding presence). IEEE-exact by construction: FNEG flips ONLY the sign bit (bit 63), so -(+0.0)=-0.0, -(-0.0)=+0.0, and -NaN preserves the payload while flipping the sign — the signed-zero + NaN-sign semantics C requires. Base 0x1E614000 = 000 11110 [31:24] | ftype=01 double [23:22] | 1 [21] | opcode=000010 FNEG [20:15] | 10000 [14:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] (ARM ARM C7.2 FNEG scalar; opcode 000001 would be FABS, 000000 FMOV). 1-source NATIVE — Rd (result), Rn (wire 0 = the value negated). NO requires2Address (Rd and Rn are independent, like neg/not). F32 sibling FNEG Sd, Sn = ftype=00 -> base 0x1E214000 rides the width axis (D-form keyed 64, S-form keyed 32).

opcodes.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2 (FCmp LIR lowering): FCMP Dn, Dm — floating-point compare writing NZCV, no register result (the float sibling of `cmp`). Base 0x1E602000 = 000 11110 [31:24] | ftype=01 [23:22] | 1 [21] | Rm [20:16] | op=00 [15:14] | 1000 [13:10] | Rn [9:5] | opcode2=00000 [4:0] (ARM ARM C7.2 FCMP; opcode2 bit4=1 is FCMPE, the signaling form — DSS does not model the FP environment, so the quiet FCMP serves all predicates in the compiler's OWN lowering; the NZCV comparison RESULTS are identical). ⓘ *would be* BECAME *is* ON 2026-09-02: FCMPE is now a declared opcode of its own (`fcmpe`, lane av, D-ASM-ARM64-GAS-SPELLS-NO-ROUNDING-MODE-OR-VECTOR-MOVE), reachable only from an assembly TEXT surface because both references assemble the spelling. Nothing about THIS opcode or about which form a C comparison lowers to has changed. F32 sibling FCMP Sn, Sm = 0x1E202000 (ftype=00). NZCV outcomes: equal → Z=1(C=1); less → N=1; greater → C=1; unordered → C=1,V=1 — the truth table the float condCodeEncoding arms below realize (full derivation at mir_to_lir floatCmpPlan).

FC3.5 sweep-c2: float↔float precision change for MIR FPTrunc/FPExt — FCVT (scalar): 000 11110 [31:24] | type [23:22] = SOURCE type | 1 [21] | 0001 [20:17] | opc [16:15] = DEST type | 10000 [14:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] (ARM ARM C7.2 FCVT). The width axis keys on the SOURCE (the MIR→LIR FPTrunc/FPExt arm threads a widthOverride from the source operand's type — the result-width default would select exactly the WRONG direction): F32 source → FCVT Dd, Sn (type=00, opc=01 → 0x1E22C000, the FPExt widen); F64 source → FCVT Sd, Dn (type=01, opc=00 → 0x1E624000, the FPTrunc narrow).
★★★ A **THIRD** ARM SINCE 2026-09-02 (cycle P55, lane fp, [[D-TARGET-ARM64-FP16-CONVERSION-FORMS-UNDECLARED]]), AND THE SENTENCE ABOVE THAT ENUMERATED **TWO** IS NOW AN ENUMERATION OF THE TWO A C PROGRAM REACHES RATHER THAN OF EVERY ARM. `fcvt` is SIX machine instructions on this ISA, not two: the H view is a third `type`/`opc` value (11) and both references assemble every one of the six at the DEFAULT -march. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02, GNU as 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 probed SEPARATELY and agreeing on all 37 probes of that run: `fcvt h0, s1` = 0x1E23C020 · `fcvt h0, d1` = 0x1E63C020 · `fcvt s0, h1` = 0x1EE24020 · `fcvt d0, h1` = 0x1EE2C020, each base re-derived from THREE independent (Rd,Rn) placements (`h3, s7` = 0x1E23C0E3, `h29, s16` = 0x1E23C21D; `h3, d7` = 0x1E63C0E3, `h16, d29` = 0x1E63C3B0; `s3, h7` = 0x1EE240E3, `s29, h16` = 0x1EE2421D; `d3, h7` = 0x1EE2C0E3, `d16, h29` = 0x1EE2C3B0).
★★★ WHY SIX FORMS NEED **TWO** OPCODES, AND WHY THE SPLIT IS FORCED RATHER THAN CHOSEN. An arm is selected by `guard.width`, which for this spelling is the SOURCE width, and `validate()`'s overlapping-guard rule refuses two `["reg"]` variants of ONE opcode that share a width — so an opcode holds AT MOST ONE arm per source width, i.e. at most three of the six. That rule is the fail-loud form of a deeper fact rather than a policy: `selectEncodingVariant` is FIRST-MATCH on (operandKinds, width, imm, memory-direction) and the ENCODER re-runs it post-regalloc off a LIR instruction that carries exactly ONE width, so a second same-width arm distinguished only by `destWidth` would be unreachable — the elector's `variantAcceptsRegisterProfile` eliminates the whole OPCODE when the first-matched variant's destination disagrees, never a second variant of it. ⇒ the source widths 32 and 64 are SPENT here on the two float↔double arms MIR produces, the source-width-16 slot was free, and the remaining three forms live on `fpcvt_h` below.
⚠ WHICH ARM LANDED HERE IS THE ONE FREE CHOICE, AND IT IS `fcvt s, h`: an `_Float16` front end promotes to `float` far more often than to `double`, so the arm a future MIR FPExt would reach is the one on the opcode `mir_to_lir` already names. ⚠⚠ AND THAT IS A DECLARATION, NOT A CODEGEN PATH — ✔MEASURED, no shipped language forms an F16 value, so `mir_to_lir` never threads a width-16 override and this arm is TEXT-REACHABLE ONLY. Whoever adds `_Float16` must pick the opcode whose arm AT THAT SOURCE WIDTH declares the destination width they want: `mir_to_lir` calls `addInst` directly and the encoder selects on width alone, so naming `fpcvt` for an F32→F16 truncation would silently encode `fcvt d0, s1` — the text tier's `variantHonorsDeclaredDestWidth` gate does not stand between a lowering pass and the encoder.

variants.$comment: F64 source → FCVT Sd, Dn (narrow to single). ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing: `fcvt s0, d1` = 0x1E624020, `fcvt s3, d7` = 0x1E6240E3. ★ `destWidth` 32 is the DECLARATION this variant's two ends disagree, added 2026-09-02 (D-ASM-DIALECTS-DECLARE-A-REGISTER-CLASS-NO-INSTRUCTION-CAN-NAME): it is what lets the dialect spell `fcvt` ONCE and lets the written destination decide which arm was meant. It is NOT a guard — no LIR instruction carries a second width — so the encoder still selects on `guard.width` alone and cannot disagree with the election.

F32 source → FCVT Dd, Sn (widen to double). ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3: `fcvt d0, s1` = 0x1E22C020. ⓘ BOTH REFERENCES REFUSE the same-width spellings `fcvt s0, s1` and `fcvt d0, d1` (✔MEASURED) — and so does DSS, because no variant declares a destination width equal to its source width, so the election eliminates every candidate and refuses by name. ⚠ THAT CLAUSE SAID *no `fpcvt` variant* UNTIL 2026-09-02 (cycle P55, lane fp) AND THE NARROWER FORM WOULD HAVE GONE FALSE THE MOMENT A SECOND OPCODE JOINED THE SPELLING: the property that refuses a same-width `fcvt` is now a property of BOTH `fpcvt` and `fpcvt_h`, and the third same-width spelling `fcvt h0, h1` — which both references also refuse, ✔MEASURED — is refused by exactly the same elimination.

F16 source → FCVT Sd, Hn (widen half to single). ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, probed separately and agreeing: `fcvt s0, h1` = 0x1EE24020, `fcvt s3, h7` = 0x1EE240E3, `fcvt s29, h16` = 0x1EE2421D ⇒ base 0x1EE24000 (type=11 half source, opc=00 single dest). ★ THE SOURCE-WIDTH-16 SLOT WAS THE ONLY ONE FREE ON THIS OPCODE, which is the whole reason three of the four half forms live on `fpcvt_h` instead; the opcode `$comment` above carries the derivation. ⚠ BASE ARMv8-A, NOT `FEAT_FP16`: the fp16 posture splits by INSTRUCTION and not by width, and this variant is the half of that split DSS was BELOW the union on.

opcodes.$comment:
★★★ THE HALF-PRECISION HALF OF `fcvt`, DECLARED 2026-09-02 (cycle P55, lane fp) TO CLOSE [[D-TARGET-ARM64-FP16-CONVERSION-FORMS-UNDECLARED]] — DSS refused all four `h`-view conversion forms and BOTH references assemble all four at the DEFAULT -march, so it was BELOW the union.
★★★ WHY THE NAME CARRIES NO WIDTH, AND WHY THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER RATHER THAN A CONCESSION. Everywhere else on this target a suffixed conversion opcode names its DESTINATION width and every arm of it writes that width — `fp_to_si32` writes 32 on both arms, `fp_to_si` 64 on both, exactly as x86_64's `zext32`/`zext16` do. That convention is UNAVAILABLE here and the arithmetic says so: the six `fcvt` forms carry destination widths {32, 64, 16, 16, 32, 64} while an opcode may hold at most one arm per SOURCE width (see `fpcvt`'s `$comment`), so any two-opcode partition leaves this opcode holding two 16-bit destinations and one that is not — a `fpcvt16` would be a name that LIES about its third arm. The `_h` suffix names the register VIEW every arm here touches (`h0..h31`, the view letter this target already declares), which is true of all three without claiming exclusivity: `fpcvt` carries the fourth H form, `fcvt s, h`, because its source-width-16 slot was free and this opcode's is not.
★★ THREE OPCODES WOULD HAVE BOUGHT THE UNIFORM NAME AND WAS REJECTED. `fpcvt16` = {h←s, h←d} plus a single-arm `fpcvt32` = {s←h} makes every suffix honest — but it is half of a scheme whose finished form is `fpcvt16`/`fpcvt32`/`fpcvt64` with `fpcvt` retired, and `fpcvt` is the mnemonic `mir_to_lir` names for FPTrunc/FPExt. A half-migration that leaves `fcvt s0, d1` on `fpcvt` while `fpcvt32` exists beside it is a worse thing to read than one unsuffixed sibling, and completing the migration is a lowering-tier change this row does not reach.
★★ EVERY WORD ✔BYTE-VERIFIED AGAINST GNU as 2.42 **AND** clang 18.1.3, PROBED SEPARATELY — 37 probes, ZERO disagreements — each read back out of an assembled object with `aarch64-linux-gnu-objdump`, none derived from a neighbouring form and none read out of a manual. Every base is re-derived from THREE independent (Rd,Rn) placements, so a field-placement error cannot hide behind a single low-register probe.
⚠⚠ THE fp16 STORY SPLITS BY INSTRUCTION FAMILY AND THE SPLIT IS FINER THAN 'CONVERSION': FP16 ARITHMETIC is `FEAT_FP16` and both references REFUSE it at the default -march (✔RE-MEASURED here: `fmov h0,h1`, `fmov h0,w1`, `fadd`, `fsub`, `fmul`, `fdiv`, `fabs`, `fneg`, `fsqrt`, `fcmp`, `fmax`, `fmin` over `h` registers, all rejected by BOTH) — and so are the fp16 **INTEGER** conversions (✔MEASURED 2026-09-02, cycle P55: `fcvtzs w0, h1`, `fcvtzs x0, h1`, `scvtf h0, w1`, `scvtf h0, x1`, `fcvtns w0, h1`, `fcvtas w0, h1` are ALL rejected by BOTH at the default -march). Only FCVT — the float↔float precision change — has half-precision arms in base ARMv8-A. ⇒ this opcode declares the H forms of FCVT and NOTHING ELSE; declaring an `h` arm on `fp_to_si*`/`si_to_fp*` or on any arithmetic opcode would put DSS ABOVE the union.
⚠ NO C PATH PRODUCES THESE. There is no `_Float16` in this front end, so `mir_to_lir` never forms a width-16 float and this opcode is TEXT-REACHABLE ONLY — the same declared-but-unproduced posture `fp_to_si32` has, and the reason `tests/asm/test_asm_arm64_conversion_dialect_rows.cpp` pins all four words through the real lowering: an unproduced declaration is exactly how the `fmov` S- and H-form byte divergence survived unnoticed until P54.

opcodes.$comment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): FCVTZS Xd, Dn — double to signed 64-bit integer, round toward zero (FP→integer conversion). Base 0x9E780000 = sf=1 [31] | 00 | 11110 [28:24] | ftype=01 double [23:22] | 1 [21] | rmode=11 toward-zero [20:19] | opcode=000 FCVTZS [18:16] | 000000 [15:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0]. The result is GPR-class via the MIR integer type (regClassFor) — rd carries the X destination, the rn wire the D source; the 5-bit slots are class-blind hwEncodings, exactly the GPR-dest/FPR-src split x86's cvttsd2si makes through modrm.reg/modrm.rm. MIR FPToSI is the producer. FC3.5 sweep-c2: the F32-source sibling FCVTZS Xd, Sn (ftype=00 → 0x9E380000) rides the SOURCE-width axis (the FPToSI arm threads the source's width — the X destination is unchanged).

FC3.5: FCVTZS Xd, Sn — ftype=00 single source, base 0x9E380000. ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3: `fcvtzs x0, s1` = 0x9E380020.

opcodes.$comment: c92 (D-CSUBSET-FP-TO-UI-CODEGEN, the c78 arm64 residual): FCVTZU — float to UNSIGNED integer, round toward zero. The EXACT MIRROR of fp_to_si above: same 'Conversion between FP and integer' group, same field layout (sf [31] | 00 | 11110 [28:24] | ftype [23:22] | 1 [21] | rmode=11 toward-zero [20:19] | opcode [18:16] | 000000 [15:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0]), opcode=001 FCVTZU where FCVTZS is 000 (+0x00010000). Same SOURCE-float-width axis (the mir_to_lir FPToUI arm threads the source's width, c78) and the same FIXED X destination as fp_to_si — a U32 result reads the low 32 bits of the Xd result, VALUE-CORRECT for any double/float in [0, 2^32) (the arm64 analog of x86 fp_to_ui's CVTTSD2SI r64 low-32 convention; gcc's `fcvtzu w0, d0` agrees on every in-range value, out-of-range is C 6.3.1.4p1 UB). ★ UNLIKE x86 (whose signed CVTTSD2SI needs the deferred >2^63 conditional-subtract, D-CSUBSET-UI-FROM-FP-UNSIGNED-I64), FCVTZU Xd covers the FULL unsigned-i64 range NATIVELY — that anchor is x86-ONLY; the arm64 leg has NO >2^63 residual (gcc emits the identical `fcvtzu x0, d0`). MIR FPToUI is the producer. FCVTZU Xd,Dn = 0x9E790000 = FCVTZS Xd,Dn[0x9E780000] | opcode bit [0x00010000]; FCVTZU Xd,Sn = 0x9E390000 = FCVTZS Xd,Sn[0x9E380000] | 0x00010000 (both cross-checked against the ARM ARM field decode above + aarch64-gcc objdump).

lowering.$comment: D-TARGET-ENCODING-TABLE-EXPRESSES-ONLY-THE-DEGENERATE-SEQUENCE. ★ THIS IS NOT A SPECIAL CASE AND NOT A `native` FLAG — it is the same kind of row x86-64's seven-step fp_to_ui carries, ONE ENTRY LONG, because on this machine the operation genuinely IS one instruction. Declaring it makes the statement uniform: every target STATES how the operation is realized, and the shared substrate reads one thing and emits what it was told. ✔MEASURED under qemu-aarch64 on all ten conversion probes (both directions, both source float widths, u32 and u64, at and above 2^31/2^63): 10/10 agree with gcc-13 and clang-19 — FCVTZU Xd is genuinely full-range from BOTH a Dn and an Sn source, so the one-step declaration is TRUE and not a half-truth. The step names this very opcode; that is well-founded, not circular, because a step is emitted as a MACHINE instruction and never re-expanded (the loader enforces it by requiring every step's opcode to declare an encoding).

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-INT-FLOAT-CONVERSION (int→float): SCVTF — Scalar Convert Signed integer to Floating-point. The REVERSE of FCVTZS above. 'Conversion between FP and integer' group: sf [31] | 00 [30:29] | 11110 [28:24] | ftype [23:22] | 1 [21] | rmode=00 [20:19] | opcode=010 SCVTF [18:16] | 000000 [15:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0]. The result is FPR-class (regClassFor sees the F64 MIR result) — rd carries the D destination, the rn wire the X/W integer source; the 5-bit slots are class-blind hwEncodings, exactly the GPR-src/FPR-dest split x86's cvtsi2sd makes through modrm.rm/modrm.reg. MIR SIToFP is the producer. The width axis keys on the SOURCE INTEGER width (the mir_to_lir SIToFP arm threads the source's int width): a 64-bit source -> SCVTF Dd, Xn (sf=1, width=64), a 32-bit source -> SCVTF Dd, Wn (sf=0, width=32). UNLIKE x86's single REX.W bit, arm64 sf+ftype are INDEPENDENT, so BOTH source-int widths keep ftype=01 (the F64 DESTINATION, Dd) — `Dd,Wn` is the i32->f64 form, the arm64 analog of cvtsi2sd xmm,r32. DESIGN NOTE (audit + qemu-arm64 scrutiny — verify these fixedWords on real hardware): dest fixed at F64/Dd this cycle (the dominant + sqlite-blocking i64->double case); int->F32 (ftype=00, Sd) is FAIL-LOUD at the mir_to_lir SIToFP arm (a deferred narrow gap, D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN). SCVTF Dd,Xn = 0x9E620000 = sf=1[0x80000000] | 11110[0x1E000000] | ftype=01[0x00400000] | bit21[0x00200000] | opcode=010[0x00020000]; SCVTF Dd,Wn = 0x1E620000 (same MINUS the sf bit). Cross-checked against the config's FCVTZS Dn base 0x9E780000 (opcode=000, rmode=11) — same field decode.

variants.$comment: SCVTF Dd, Xn — sf=1 64-bit signed source -> double. base 0x9E620000. The sqlite i64 -> volatile double blocker. ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3: `scvtf d0, x1` = 0x9E620020, `scvtf d3, x7` = 0x9E6200E3.
SCVTF Dd, Wn — sf=0 32-bit signed source -> double. base 0x1E620000 (the arm64 analog of cvtsi2sd xmm,r32; an I32 fits the F64 result exactly). ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3: `scvtf d0, w1` = 0x1E620020.

opcodes.$comment: D-CSUBSET-INT-FLOAT-CONVERSION (int→float, unsigned): UCVTF — Scalar Convert Unsigned integer to Floating-point. Same 'Conversion between FP and integer' group as SCVTF but opcode=011 [18:16] (the unsigned sibling). MIR UIToFP is the producer; the SOURCE-int-width axis matches si_to_fp (width=64 -> UCVTF Dd,Xn, width=32 -> UCVTF Dd,Wn). Dest fixed F64/Dd (U->F32 deferred D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN). Unlike x86 SSE2 (which has no unsigned cvt and must fall back to cvtsi2sd), arm64 UCVTF handles the FULL unsigned i64 range natively — so the arm64 ui_to_fp is value-correct where x86's signed-cvt fallback is not (the deferred D-CSUBSET-UI-TO-FP-UNSIGNED-I64 is an x86-only gap; sqlite does not hit it on either target). UCVTF Dd,Xn = 0x9E630000 = SCVTF Dd,Xn[0x9E620000] | opcode bit [0x00010000]; UCVTF Dd,Wn = 0x1E630000.

lowering.$comment: D-TARGET-ENCODING-TABLE-EXPRESSES-ONLY-THE-DEGENERATE-SEQUENCE — the one-entry form of the same row x86-64 needs seven steps for. UCVTF Dd,Xn is full-range over the whole u64 and UCVTF Dd,Wn over the whole u32, so BOTH declarations are true at their declared width; the destination stays fixed at F64/Dd on this target, and an F32 destination still has no realization at all and fails loud upstream (D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN) rather than being half-declared here.

★★★ THE NARROW-DESTINATION HALF OF THE CONVERSION FAMILY — FOUR OPCODES, DECLARED 2026-09-02 (cycle P54, lane el, D-ASM-DIALECTS-DECLARE-A-REGISTER-CLASS-NO-INSTRUCTION-CAN-NAME).
★★★ WHY THEY ARE SEPARATE OPCODES AND NOT MORE VARIANTS. `fcvtzs` is FOUR machine instructions (Wd|Xd × Sn|Dn) that gas and clang spell identically — ✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 agree on all four. The SOURCE width already rides `guard.width`, so the destination width has to separate the other pair, and a LIR instruction carries exactly ONE width: a second guard axis would be one the ENCODER could not read post-regalloc, and the two tiers would silently pick different variants. Making it a different OPCODE puts the answer in the one field the instruction DOES carry. ⇒ this is the same shape x86_64 has declared since D-ASM-X86-WIDTH-EXTENDING-MOVES-UNSPELLABLE, where `zext`/`zext32`/`zext16` are three opcodes over one machine idea, and `AsmInstructionSpelling::destWidth` states it in words: *an instruction that writes a different width is a different opcode in `opcodeNames`*.
★★ THE DIALECT STILL SPELLS EACH MNEMONIC ONCE: its row names BOTH opcodes as candidates and declares `destWidthFromOperands`, so the WRITTEN destination register elects between them through the `destWidth` declarations below. A destination width no candidate declares elects nothing and refuses by name — which is what makes the old silent `fcvtzs x16, s29` unsayable rather than unlikely.
⚠ NO C PATH PRODUCES THESE. `mir_to_lir` converts to a 64-bit integer and truncates, so these four are text-reachable only — the same declared-but-unproduced posture `movsd_reg` has on x86_64, and the reason `tests/asm/test_asm_arm64_conversion_dialect_rows.cpp` pins every one of their words: an unproduced declaration is exactly how the `fmov` S- and H-form divergence survived unnoticed until P54.
★ FCVTZS Wd,*: same 'Conversion between FP and integer' group as `fp_to_si`, sf=0. ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing: `fcvtzs w0, s1` = 0x1E380020 ⇒ base 0x1E380000; `fcvtzs w0, d1` = 0x1E780020 ⇒ base 0x1E780000; `fcvtzs w3, s7` = 0x1E3800E3 (the field-placement pin).

★★★ WHY EVERY ROUNDING MODE GETS ITS OWN OPCODE, AND IT IS THE REASON THE FAMILY EXISTS RATHER THAN A FILING CONVENTION. FCVTAS/FCVTMS/FCVTNS/FCVTPS differ from the already-declared FCVTZS in NOTHING BUT `rmode`. Bind `fcvtms` to `fp_to_si` and the program still compiles, still links, still runs, and rounds toward ZERO where the author wrote toward MINUS INFINITY: a working program with the wrong numbers and an empty build log. That is the one failure class this project vetoes outright, and it is why `fcvtzs`'s own two opcodes were never widened to carry a fifth axis. ⓘ Lane `el` named this hazard when it left the mnemonics undeclared with their bytes measured; this is that warning honoured rather than worked around.

★★★ THE SAME SILENT HAZARD AS THE FCVT FAMILY ABOVE, ONE STEP SHORTER. FRINTN/FRINTP/FRINTM/FRINTZ/FRINTA/FRINTX/FRINTI are ONE instruction group differing only in `opcode` [17:15]; every one of them assembles, runs and returns a NUMBER, so binding two of them together is invisible everywhere except in the answer. They therefore get seven opcodes and never a shared one with a mode parameter.
★★ WHAT EACH MODE IS, because the mnemonic letters are not self-evident and picking the wrong one is the defect: N = nearest, ties to EVEN · P = toward +∞ (`ceil`) · M = toward −∞ (`floor`) · Z = toward ZERO (`trunc`) · A = nearest, ties AWAY from zero (`round`) · I = whatever mode FPCR currently selects · X = the same FPCR mode as I, but SIGNALLING Inexact. ⚠ `I` AND `X` ARE NOT ALIASES: they differ in the exception they raise, which is the whole reason C has both `nearbyint` (X's quiet sibling) and `rint`. Their words differ in bit 15 and both are declared.
★★ ✔MEASURED against GNU as 2.42 AND clang 18.1.3 SEPARATELY, agreeing on all fourteen; each base derived by clearing Rd [4:0] and Rn [9:5] from the measured word and re-inserting the registers to reproduce it.

★★★ THE 2-SOURCE FP FAMILY THAT WAS MISSING — FMAX / FMIN / FMAXNM / FMINNM / FNMUL, five opcodes sharing `fadd`'s exact word shape and differing only in `opcode` [15:12] (cycle P54, lane av). ONE banner; each row carries its own pair.
★★★ `fmax` AND `fmaxnm` ARE **NOT** THE SAME INSTRUCTION AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ONLY VISIBLE ON NaN — which is precisely the shape of defect this whole lane is about. FMAX propagates a NaN operand; FMAXNM returns the OTHER operand when exactly one is a NaN (IEEE-754 `maxNum`, the one C's `fmax()` is specified as). Two instructions that agree on every ordinary input and disagree on the input a test is least likely to feed. They are separate opcodes for that reason and must never be folded.
✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 agreeing on all ten. FMAX: `fmax d0, d1, d2` = 0x1E624820 ⇒ base 0x1E604800; `fmax s0, s1, s2` = 0x1E224820 ⇒ base 0x1E204800.

★★★ THE FUSED MULTIPLY-ADD FAMILY — FMADD / FMSUB / FNMADD / FNMSUB, four opcodes over THREE source registers (cycle P54, lane av). ONE banner; each row carries its own pair.
★★★ THE THIRD SOURCE RIDES `Ra` [14:10], WHICH IS THE SLOT THE INTEGER `msub` ALREADY USES — so a 3-source FP opcode needed no new encoding vocabulary at all, only the declaration. That reuse is the finding worth recording: the `fixed32` walker's slot set was general enough for a family nothing had exercised on the FP side.
★★★ FUSED IS NOT THE SAME AS MULTIPLY-THEN-ADD, and it is why these cannot be synthesized: FMADD rounds ONCE, at the end, so it is `fma()` and not `a*b+c`. A program that spells `fmadd` and gets two roundings has a different answer, quietly.
⚠ THE OPERAND ORDER IS Rd, Rn, Rm, Ra — the ADDEND IS LAST, so `fmadd d0, d1, d2, d3` is d0 = d1×d2 + d3. Wires 0/1/2 map to rn/rm/ra in that order.
✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 agreeing on all eight. FMADD: `fmadd d0, d1, d2, d3` = 0x1F420C20 ⇒ base 0x1F400000; `fmadd s0, s1, s2, s3` = 0x1F020C20 ⇒ base 0x1F000000.

opcodes.$comment:
★★ FCMPE Dn, Dm — the SIGNALLING floating-point compare, `fcmp`'s sibling and the form `fcmp`'s own comment named without declaring (*opcode2 bit4=1 would be FCMPE*). It writes NZCV and no register, exactly like `fcmp`; it differs by raising Invalid for a QUIET NaN as well as a signalling one, which is what C's `<`/`>` on possibly-NaN operands are specified to do.
★★★ Rd [4:0] IS **NOT A REGISTER SLOT** ON THIS OPCODE — it is `opcode2`, and BIT 4 IS THE E BIT. That is why the base word below ends in 0x10 and why the variant declares NO `resultSlot`: wiring one here would overwrite the flag that makes it the signalling form and silently emit a quiet FCMP. The two operands wire to Rn and Rm, and nothing else moves.
⚠ DSS's own codegen still emits the QUIET `fcmp` for every C comparison — this opcode is TEXT-REACHABLE ONLY, and `fcmp`'s adjudication (*DSS does not model the FP environment, so the quiet FCMP serves all predicates*) is unchanged for the compiler's own lowering.
✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 agreeing: `fcmpe d0, d1` = 0x1E612010 ⇒ base 0x1E602010; `fcmpe s0, s1` = 0x1E212010 ⇒ base 0x1E202010.

variants.$comment: FCMPE Dn, Dm — ftype=01 double, opcode2=10000. base 0x1E602010.
FCMPE Sn, Sm — ftype=00 single, opcode2=10000. base 0x1E202010.

opcodes.$comment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): FMOV — FP register-register move. Word shape: 0 0 0 11110 [31:24] | ftype [23:22] | 1 [21] | opc=000000 FMOV [20:15] | 10000 [14:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] (FP data-processing 1 source — the single source rides Rn, NOT Rm; contrast the GPR mov's ORR alias whose source is Rm). Bound to the fpr class's `move` slot in registerClassOps[] — consumed by MIR value/phi copies and the callconv arg/return moves whenever the register class is FPR (the arm64 analog of x86's movaps role), and SPELLED `fmov` by the aarch64 gas dialect since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE OLD FC3.5 sweep-c2 ADJUDICATION RECORDED HERE — *register COPIES stay width-BLIND (variant deliberately width-absent, match-any)* — IS FALSE TWICE OVER AND IS KEPT ONLY AS THE CLAIM THAT WAS REFUTED: R2 (P47) gave the arms a `width` guard, and P54 gave each width its OWN ftype word after ✔measuring that the shared D-form word diverged from gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 on every S- and H-form spelling. Its premise (an F32 value lives in the low 4 bytes, so a D-form copy preserves it) was about the VALUE and was never about the BYTES. See `$variantsComment` for the measurement. Memory accesses (fldur/fstur) were always width-exact.

encoding.$variantsComment: ★★★ **TWO** DECLARED WIDTHS, TWO DIFFERENT WORDS, AND NO WIDTH-128 ARM — AND THE COUNT SAID **THREE** UNTIL 2026-09-02 (cycle P54, lane ae), WHEN THE WIDTH-16 ARM WAS DELETED FOR BEING **ABOVE THE UNION**. ✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 AND clang 18.1.3 probed separately and agreeing: `fmov h0, h1` is REJECTED by both at the default -march, as are `fmov h0, w1`, `fadd h0, h1, h2`, `fabs`/`fsqrt`/`fneg`/`fmul`/`fdiv`/`fsub`/`fcmp`/`fmax`/`fmin` over `h` registers — FP16 ARITHMETIC IS `FEAT_FP16`, an architecture feature this descriptor carries no vocabulary for. The arm was reachable and ✔MEASURED to compile: `fmov h0, h1` assembled rc=0 to 0x1EE04020 through the `.s` surface at the P54 base, so DSS accepted a program NEITHER reference accepts. ⚠⚠ AND IT WAS NOT INTRODUCED BY THE CYCLE THAT MADE IT WRONG-LOOKING — ✔MEASURED with `git show 30cfe32c` (P54's own base commit): this opcode already carried THREE width arms there, 64 / 32 / 16, ALL THREE with the same D-form word 0x1E604000. P54 gave each arm its own `ftype`, which made the `h` arm byte-CORRECT and left it above the union, and the dialect's first `fmov` row made it reachable from TEXT for the first time. Nobody declared it this cycle; it was corrected without anyone asking whether it should exist, which is why the deletion is recorded here rather than in a lane's diff. The paragraph below that reasoned *this descriptor carries no CPU-feature vocabulary, so the union's spelling is the one declared* had the rule EXACTLY BACKWARDS: the disjunction makes a construct required when SOME reference accepts it, and forbidden when NONE does. Its byte measurement is correct and is kept. ⓘ AND THE fp16 STORY IS NOT UNIFORM, which is why this is a per-instruction deletion rather than a per-width one: ✔MEASURED in the same run, the fp16 CONVERSIONS are base ARMv8-A and BOTH references assemble them — `fcvt h0, s1` = 0x1E23C020, `fcvt h0, d1` = 0x1E63C020, `fcvt s0, h1` = 0x1EE24020, `fcvt d0, h1` = 0x1EE2C020, `fcvt h3, s7` = 0x1E23C0E3, `fcvt s3, h7` = 0x1EE240E3 — so DSS **was** BELOW the union on those four forms, which `fpcvt` cannot hold as extra variants (two variants of one opcode may not share an operand shape at one width) and which therefore needed their own opcode: [[D-TARGET-ARM64-FP16-CONVERSION-FORMS-UNDECLARED]], CLOSED 2026-09-02 (cycle P55, lane fp) by declaring `fpcvt_h` beside `fpcvt` — three of the four forms there, `fcvt s, h` on `fpcvt`'s free source-width-16 slot. ⚠ THE MEASUREMENT ABOVE IS UNCHANGED AND THE DELETION HERE STANDS: the split is per-INSTRUCTION, and `fmov` at width 16 is on the `FEAT_FP16` side of it in both references. ⚠ THE PHRASE *the fp16 CONVERSIONS* IS WIDER THAN WHAT WAS MEASURED, ✔RE-MEASURED in P55: only FCVT (float↔float) has half arms at the default -march — `fcvtzs w0, h1`, `fcvtzs x0, h1`, `scvtf h0, w1`, `scvtf h0, x1`, `fcvtns w0, h1` and `fcvtas w0, h1` are ALL refused by BOTH references, so the fp16 INTEGER conversions stay undeclared for the same reason this `fmov` arm was deleted. ⚠ REMOVING THE ARM DOES NOT REMOVE A CODEGEN PATH. `registerClassOps.fpr.move` names this opcode and takes its widths from these arms, so a width-16 class-internal FPR copy now elects NOTHING and fails loud at the emitting site — which is exactly what width 128 already does, and ✔MEASURED nothing can produce one: no shipped language forms an F16 value (there is no `_Float16` in this front end). The old note that called this arm *stated rather than deleted* was written before its spelling was reachable from text; it is reachable now, and a declared spelling both references refuse is not a statement, it is an acceptance defect. ⚠⚠ THE THREE ARMS USED TO CARRY THE **SAME** fixedWord (0x1E604000 = FMOV Dd,Dn) AND THAT WAS A BYTE DIVERGENCE FROM BOTH REFERENCES, CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (cycle P54, lane ad, D-ASM-DIALECTS-DECLARE-A-REGISTER-CLASS-NO-INSTRUCTION-CAN-NAME). The argument it rested on — 'FMOV Dd,Dn copies the low 64 bits and zeroes 127:64, which is value-preserving for every float width this pipeline puts in a register' — is TRUE ABOUT THE VALUE and says nothing about the BYTES, and the bytes are what a target descriptor declares. ✔MEASURED at the CLI before the fix: a `float` class-internal move at `--config=release` on `arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-exec` disassembled to `fmov d28, d0` / `fmov d27, d28` where gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both emit the S-form. ⇒ ftype [23:22] IS the width axis here exactly as it is on `fadd`/`fneg`/`fcmp`, and the arms now say so: ✔BYTE-VERIFIED against GNU as 2.42 AND clang 18.1.3, agreeing on every probe — width 64 `fmov d0, d1` = 0x1E604020 ⇒ base **0x1E604000** (ftype=01); width 32 `fmov s0, s1` = 0x1E204020 ⇒ base **0x1E204000** (ftype=00); width 16 `fmov h0, h1` = 0x1EE04020 ⇒ base **0x1EE04000** (ftype=11), which BOTH references refuse at the default -march and BOTH accept under `.arch armv8.2-a+fp16` — this descriptor carries no CPU-feature vocabulary, so the union's spelling is the one declared. High-register forms pin the Rn/Rd field placement: `fmov d31, d30` = 0x1E6043DF and `fmov s31, s30` = 0x1E2043DF. ⓘ THE WIDTH-64 WORD IS UNCHANGED, so every existing F64 byte pin still reads what it always read; only the F32 and F16 arms move. ⚠⚠ NEITHER ARM HAD A REACHABLE TEXT SPELLING WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN — the aarch64 gas dialect spelled no FP mnemonic at all, so the only consumer was the compiler's own `registerClassOps.fpr.move`, and a wrong word there produces a working program with the wrong instruction in it. It is reachable from text now. ★ THE FAIL-LOUD HALF OF R2 (design A′, 2026-08-28) IS UNTOUCHED: the arms carry a `width` GUARD, which the pre-R1 single variant did not, and `variantMatchesInst` treats an absent width as MATCHING ANY WIDTH — so an unguarded row would silently encode a 64-bit FMOV for the 128-bit move R1 made formable (`"w"` binds `fpr`, so a `long double` operand is an FPR-class value) and drop the top half. Width 128 elects nothing and fails loud at the emitting site. ★ What a width-128 register-to-register SIMD move needs is ORR (`mov v_d.16b, v_n.16b`), a DIFFERENT AArch64 instruction with different bytes. ⚠ THE CLAUSE THAT FOLLOWED — *undeclared here on trigger discipline, because ✔MEASURED nothing consumes one* — WENT FALSE THE SAME DAY: it is declared, as the separate opcode `move_bytes` (2026-09-02, lane av, D-ASM-ARM64-GAS-SPELLS-NO-ROUNDING-MODE-OR-VECTOR-MOVE), because a TEXT consumer appeared that codegen never had — the dialect's `mov` row. The measurement it rested on is UNCHANGED and still true (F80 and F128 are the two memory-resident kinds, per `LirVerifier`'s store rule and `lowerF128Store`'s GPR word stores), which is exactly why `fmov` still has no width-128 arm and `registerClassOps.fpr.move` still elects nothing at 128: the new opcode serves the assembler surface, not the copy path.

opcodes.$comment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): FPR memory LOAD — LDUR Dt, [Xn, #simm9] (SIMD&FP 64-bit, unscaled). Fixed word 0xFC400000 = the GPR LDUR 0xF8400000 with V=1 (bit 26): size=11 [31:30] | 111 [29:27] | V=1 [26] | 00 [25:24] | opc=01 load [23:22] | 0 [21] | imm9 [20:12] | 00 [11:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rt [4:0]. Operand layout mirrors the GPR `load` row exactly (shared LIR load form [base_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp)] + result): result→Rt (rd), base→Rn, MemOffset→Imm9 (signed -256..255), MemBase carries no bits (membase.noscale). Bound to the fpr class's `load` slot in registerClassOps[] — the callconv epilogue saved-d-reg reload, stack-resident F64 args, and MIR Load of an F64 rodata global (the literal-materialization path) all resolve here. F64-only: the F32 S-form (size=10, 0xBC400000) lands with an F32 consumer.

encoding.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2 (D-CSUBSET-F32-CODEGEN): width-keyed pair — LDUR Dt (8-byte, 0xFC400000, width 64) vs LDUR St (4-byte, size=10 → 0xBC400000, width 32; ARM ARM C7.2 LDUR SIMD&FP). lowerLoad threads the loaded type's width for FPR-class results: an 8-byte D-load of a 4-byte F32 rodata item would read past the item.

variants.$comment: FC3.5: LDUR St, [Xn, #simm9] — size=10 single, base 0xBC400000 (4-byte load).

R2 (design A′, 2026-08-28): LDUR Qt, [Xn, #simm9] — the Q form, size=00 opc=11, base 0x3CC00000. ★ THE fixedWord IS THE ONE THE DELETED `fldur_q` OPCODE CARRIED, VERBATIM, and that opcode was byte-pinned against aarch64-linux-gnu-as; folding it onto this row's width axis moved no byte. ⚠ WHY IT IS A WIDTH AND NOT A SECOND MNEMONIC: `fldur_q` existed only because the SIMD&FP file was declared TWICE, so the 16-byte access looked like a different register CLASS's load rather than a wider one of the same class's. With the file declared once (R1) the class is `fpr` at every width and the access width is what varies — the same axis that already picks LDUR Dt (64) from LDUR St (32) three lines up.

LDUR Ht, [Xn, #simm9] — size=01 V=1 opc=01, base 0x7C400000. ✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 probed SEPARATELY and agreeing: `ldur h0,[x1]` = 0x7C400020 · `ldur h0,[x1,#-2]` = 0x7C5FE020 · `ldur h7,[x3,#5]` = 0x7C405067 · `ldur h29,[x16,#-1]` = 0x7C5FF21D. ⚠ THE UNSCALED FORM DOES NOT SCALE, so this arm's reach is the SAME ±256 every other width has — that is the discriminator against the scaled twin, and it is pinned: `ldur h0,[x1,#-2]` = 0x7C5FE020 encodes a NEGATIVE displacement no `imm12.scaled` arm can express at all.

LDUR Bt, [Xn, #simm9] — size=00 V=1 opc=01, base 0x3C400000. ✔MEASURED (gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing): `ldur b0,[x1]` = 0x3C400020 · `ldur b0,[x1,#-1]` = 0x3C5FF020 · `ldur b7,[x3,#3]` = 0x3C403067 · `ldur b29,[x16,#-7]` = 0x3C5F921D. ⚠ THE B AND Q FORMS SHARE size=00 AND ARE SEPARATED BY opc — 0x3C400000 (B) against 0x3CC00000 (Q) — so a B arm copied from the Q word would be a 16-byte access spelled as a 1-byte one.

Fixed word 0xFC000000 = the GPR STUR 0xF8000000 with V=1 (bit 26); opc=00 store. Operand layout mirrors the GPR `store` row exactly (shared LIR store form [value_reg, base_reg, MemBase(scale=1), MemOffset(disp)], no result): value→Rt (rd wire), base→Rn, MemOffset→Imm9 (signed). Bound to the fpr class's `store` slot in registerClassOps[] — the callconv prologue saved-d-reg spill is the first consumer (AAPCS64 declares d8-d15 callee-saved + regalloc prefers callee-saved, so the FIRST FPR vreg in any function needs this store — the exact shape that surfaced x86's movsd_store on ms_x64).

encoding.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c2: width-keyed pair — STUR Dt (8-byte, width 64) vs STUR St (4-byte, 0xBC000000, width 32). lowerStore threads the stored VALUE's type width for FPR-class stores; the regalloc spill path stays width-default 64 over 8-byte slots (value-preserving for both float widths).

variants.$comment: FC3.5: STUR St, [Xn, #simm9] — size=10 single, base 0xBC000000 (4-byte store).

Its consumer is the AAPCS64 variadic register-save area, which stores q0..q7 sixteen bytes each; that site now threads width 128 instead of naming a second mnemonic. See the load's twin for why this is a WIDTH rather than a class.

STUR Ht, [Xn, #simm9] — base 0x7C000000. ✔MEASURED (gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing): `stur h0,[x1]` = 0x7C000020 · `stur h0,[x1,#-2]` = 0x7C1FE020 · `stur h7,[x3,#5]` = 0x7C005067 · `stur h29,[x16,#-1]` = 0x7C1FF21D. ⚠ THE UNSCALED FORM DOES NOT SCALE, so this arm's reach is the SAME ±256 every other width has — that is the discriminator against the scaled twin, and it is pinned: `ldur h0,[x1,#-2]` = 0x7C5FE020 encodes a NEGATIVE displacement no `imm12.scaled` arm can express at all.
