opcodes.$comment: ★★★ D-TARGET-REGISTER-CLASS-OPS-HAVE-NO-LONG-REACH-MEMORY-FORM: the SIMD&FP SCALED unsigned-offset LOAD — LDR St/Dt/Qt, [Xn, #pimm]. `fldur`'s long-reach twin, bound to the fpr class's NEW `loadScaled` slot in registerClassOps[], exactly as `load_u` is the integer file's twin of `load`. ⚠⚠ WHY THIS ROW HAD TO EXIST: the frame load/store chokepoint (`selectFrameMemOp`) has swapped an out-of-imm9 offset onto the scaled form since D-ASM-AARCH64-LARGE-FRAME-IMM12 — but it could only ever swap the INTEGER file's op, because the integer file was the only one with a twin declared. An FP frame access past ±256 therefore kept `fldur` and fail-louded A_ImmediateOperandOutOfRange at the encoder's Imm12Scaled handler with nothing to select. ✔MEASURED: `examples/c/varargs_aapcs64_struct` on arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-exec produced eight such refusals at offsets 256/272/288/320 once the SIMD&FP file was declared once and the frame slot stride became 16. ★ THE ENCODING IS `fldur`'s WITH BIT 24 SET — the unsigned-offset mode bit — and the imm9 slot replaced by imm12.scaled, whose field is byteOffset/accessSize (so a Q-form access at [sp,#256] encodes 16, a D-form 32, an S-form 64). Reach: 0..16380 (S), 0..32760 (D), 0..65520 (Q). ✔MEASURED byte-for-byte against BOTH `aarch64-linux-gnu-as` 13.3.0 AND `clang 18.1.3 --target=aarch64-linux-gnu`, which agree exactly: `ldr s0,[x1]`=0xBD400020, `ldr d0,[x1]`=0xFD400020, `ldr q0,[x1]`=0x3DC00020.

encoding.$comment: The SAME width axis `fldur` keys on, so the chokepoint's swap is width-preserving BY CONSTRUCTION: whatever width elected an `fldur` variant elects the matching `fldr_u` variant, and the encoder scales the displacement by that same width. A width declared on one and not the other would be a silent half-register access on exactly the frames that are too big to reach with the short form.

variants.$comment: width 64: LDR Dt, [Xn, #pimm] — size=11 V=1 opc=01, base 0xFD400000 (LDUR Dt 0xFC400000 with bit 24 set). accessSize 8 ⇒ imm12 = byteOffset/8.
width 32: LDR St, [Xn, #pimm] — size=10, base 0xBD400000. accessSize 4 ⇒ imm12 = byteOffset/4.

width 128: LDR Qt, [Xn, #pimm] — size=00 opc=11, base 0x3DC00000. accessSize 16 ⇒ imm12 = byteOffset/16. THIS is the variant the failing corpus needs: an AAPCS64 variadic callee's VR save block and the 16-byte-stride FP frame slots sit past ±256 on any function that also carries a GR save block.

width 16: LDR Ht, [Xn, #pimm] — base 0x7D400000 (LDUR Ht 0x7C400000 with bit 24 set). accessSize 2 ⇒ imm12 = byteOffset/2, reach 0..8190. ✔MEASURED (gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing): `ldr h0,[x1]` = 0x7D400020 · `ldr h0,[x1,#2]` = 0x7D400420 · `ldr h7,[x3,#4]` = 0x7D400867 · `ldr h29,[x16,#8]` = 0x7D40121D · `ldr h0,[x1,#8190]` = 0x7D7FFC20 (imm12 = 4095, the maximum) and `#8192` REFUSED by both. ★★ THE SCALE COMES OFF THIS VERY WIDTH and nowhere else (`fixed32.cpp`'s Imm12Scaled handler derives accessSizeBytes = width/8), which is the whole silent-wrong-answer fence on this row: ONE byte offset encodes a DIFFERENT imm12 at every width, so an arm that borrowed a neighbour's scale would address the wrong memory rather than refuse.

width 8: LDR Bt, [Xn, #pimm] — base 0x3D400000. accessSize 1 ⇒ imm12 = byteOffset, reach 0..4095 — the ONE width at which the field and the byte offset coincide, which is exactly why a scale bug is invisible here and visible everywhere else. ✔MEASURED (gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing): `ldr b0,[x1]` = 0x3D400020 · `ldr b0,[x1,#1]` = 0x3D400420 · `ldr b7,[x3,#2]` = 0x3D400867 · `ldr b29,[x16,#3]` = 0x3D400E1D · `ldr b0,[x1,#4095]` = 0x3D7FFC20 and `#4096` REFUSED by both.

opcodes.$comment: ★★★ D-TARGET-REGISTER-CLASS-OPS-HAVE-NO-LONG-REACH-MEMORY-FORM: the SIMD&FP SCALED unsigned-offset STORE — STR St/Dt/Qt, [Xn, #pimm]. `fstur`'s long-reach twin, bound to the fpr class's NEW `storeScaled` slot. It is declared TOGETHER with `fldr_u` and the loader refuses one without the other: half a pair is a frame whose FP spill RELOADS encode and whose FP spill STORES fail loud on the same slot. ★ Encoding = `fstur` with bit 24 set, imm12.scaled in place of imm9. ✔MEASURED against `aarch64-linux-gnu-as` AND clang (identical): `str s0,[x1]`=0xBD000020, `str d0,[x1]`=0xFD000020, `str q0,[x1]`=0x3D800020; and the concrete failing shape `str d8,[sp,#256]`=0xFD0083E8 (imm12=32), `str q0,[sp,#256]`=0x3D8043E0 (imm12=16), `str s3,[sp,#256]`=0xBD0103E3 (imm12=64) — three different fields for ONE byte offset, which is why the scale must come off the instruction's own width and never off a constant.

encoding.$comment: Width axis identical to `fstur`'s — see `fldr_u`'s encoding comment for why the two mnemonics must declare the same set.

variants.$comment: width 64: STR Dt, [Xn, #pimm] — base 0xFD000000 (STUR Dt 0xFC000000 with bit 24 set).
width 32: STR St, [Xn, #pimm] — base 0xBD000000.
width 128: STR Qt, [Xn, #pimm] — base 0x3D800000. The AAPCS64 variadic VR save block's store, once the save area sits past the short form's reach.

width 16: STR Ht, [Xn, #pimm] — base 0x7D000000, accessSize 2. ✔MEASURED (gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing): `str h0,[x1]` = 0x7D000020 · `str h0,[x1,#2]` = 0x7D000420 · `str h7,[x3,#4]` = 0x7D000867 · `str h29,[x16,#8]` = 0x7D00121D. ★★ THE SCALE COMES OFF THIS VERY WIDTH and nowhere else (`fixed32.cpp`'s Imm12Scaled handler derives accessSizeBytes = width/8), which is the whole silent-wrong-answer fence on this row: ONE byte offset encodes a DIFFERENT imm12 at every width, so an arm that borrowed a neighbour's scale would address the wrong memory rather than refuse.

width 8: STR Bt, [Xn, #pimm] — base 0x3D000000, accessSize 1. ✔MEASURED (gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing): `str b0,[x1]` = 0x3D000020 · `str b0,[x1,#1]` = 0x3D000420 · `str b7,[x3,#2]` = 0x3D000867 · `str b29,[x16,#3]` = 0x3D000E1D. ⚠ DECLARED IN LOCKSTEP WITH `fldr_u`'s arms: the loader refuses the scaled pair half-declared, and a width on the load without its store is a frame whose spill RELOADS encode and whose spill STORES fail loud on the same slot.

opcodes.$comment: D-FULLC-STDBIT-ARM64-CNT-POPCOUNT: cross-class bit-copy GPR -> SIMD&FP register. The arm64 declaration of the SAME shared verb x86_64 declares as MOVQ xmm, r/m64 — the vocabulary is `movq_gpr_to_xmm` on BOTH targets and the bytes differ, which is the whole point of a target descriptor. FMOV (general), 'Conversion between FP and integer' group: sf [31] | 00 [30:29] | 11110 [28:24] | ftype [23:22] | 1 [21] | rmode=00 [20:19] | opcode=111 [18:16] | 000000 [15:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0]. WIDTH AXIS = the SOURCE INTEGER width, the same axis si_to_fp/ui_to_fp above key on: width 64 -> FMOV Dd, Xn (sf=1, ftype=01, base 0x9E670000 = 2657550336); width 32 -> FMOV Sd, Wn (sf=0, ftype=00, base 0x1E270000 = 505872384). ★ THE UPPER-LANE ZEROING IS LOAD-BEARING AND IT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: a write to the D or S view of a SIMD&FP register zeroes every bit above it, so after the width-32 form bytes 4..7 of the register read ZERO and a following byte-lane count over 8 bytes still answers the 32-bit population count. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-26 by EXECUTION under qemu-aarch64 with the destination register pre-dirtied to all-ones via `movi v0.16b, #0xFF` — had the zeroing not happened the probe would have reported 32 extra bits. `registerClass: gpr` is the SOURCE bank (Rn); `resultRegClass: fpr` is the DESTINATION bank (Rd) — the identical split si_to_fp declares, and the reason the encoder cannot silently write a GPR ordinal into an FP field (D-OPT-LIR-ARG-REGISTER-CLASS-MISMATCH-FAILLOUD). Byte-pins verified against aarch64-linux-gnu-as: `fmov s3, w7` = 0x1E2700E3, `fmov d3, x7` = 0x9E6700E3.

variants.$comment: FMOV Dd, Xn — 64-bit source integer into the D view. base 0x9E670000.
FMOV Sd, Wn — 32-bit source integer into the S view; bits 32..127 of the destination are zeroed by the write.

opcodes.$comment: D-FULLC-STDBIT-ARM64-CNT-POPCOUNT: cross-class bit-copy SIMD&FP register -> GPR — the EXACT MIRROR of `movq_gpr_to_xmm` above, and a SEPARATE opcode for the reason x86_64's twin rows state verbatim: the variant guard keys only on (operandKinds, width) and BOTH directions are `reg` at the same width, so one opcode carrying both would silently pick a direction. Same FMOV (general) group with opcode=110 [18:16] instead of 111: width 64 -> FMOV Xd, Dn (sf=1, ftype=01, base 0x9E660000 = 2657484800); width 32 -> FMOV Wd, Sn (sf=0, ftype=00, base 0x1E260000 = 505806848). `registerClass: fpr` is the SOURCE bank (Rn), `resultRegClass: gpr` the DESTINATION bank (Rd) — the reverse of the row above, exactly as fp_to_si is the reverse of si_to_fp. ★★ D-TARGET-NO-CROSS-CLASS-MOVE-VERB CLOSED THIS: the row's old text SAID a cross-class Bitcast FAILED loud here — *"a different row's work, not this one's"* — and SAID arm64 DECLARED no `movq_xclass`. ⚠ Both claims are PAST TENSE on purpose, with the governor against the claim rather than two clauses upstream: `stale_refusal_citations_guard` looks BACK exactly 48 characters, which is one clause, and it refused the longer phrasing — correctly. That row landed. `movq_xclass` is DELETED from the tree — a bidirectional opcode was never the shape, because the variant guard cannot disambiguate two `reg` operands at one width — and this opcode is now the `fpr` -> `gpr` cell of the class×class `registerClassOps` table, with `movq_gpr_to_xmm` as its mirror. A cross-class Bitcast and a `"r"`-bound floating inline-asm operand both WORK here now, on the bytes below, which shipped before the slot to name them did. Byte-pins re-verified against aarch64-linux-gnu-as 2026-08-31: `fmov w7, s3` = 0x1E260067, `fmov x7, d3` = 0x9E660067.

variants.$comment: FMOV Xd, Dn — the D view's 64 bits into a 64-bit GPR. base 0x9E660000.
FMOV Wd, Sn — the S view's 32 bits into a 32-bit GPR (a W write zeroes bits 63:32 of the X view).

opcodes.$comment: D-FULLC-STDBIT-ARM64-CNT-POPCOUNT: PER-LANE population count over the register's EIGHT BYTE LANES — each byte of the operand is replaced by the number of set bits in that byte (0..8). The DSS verb is `popcount_bytes` and it names the OPERATION and the lane element, never the ISA: an x86_64 target with AVX-512 VPOPCNTB would declare this same row with its own bytes and inherit the sequence below unchanged. AArch64 realization CNT Vd.8B, Vn.8B (AdvSIMD two-register misc): 0 [31] | Q=0 8B [30] | U=0 [29] | 01110 [28:24] | size=00 [23:22] | 10000 [21:17] | opcode=00101 [16:12] | 10 [11:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] = 0x0E205800 = 237000704. Q=0 selects the 8-BYTE arrangement, which reads and writes only the low 64 bits and zeroes bits 64..127 — so this row is honestly a 64-bit operation on the `fpr` (D-view) bank and needs no allocatable `vr` register. The guard is keyed at width 64 for that reason: the instruction always processes eight bytes regardless of how wide the VALUE that reached it was, and a caller emitting it at any other width gets A_NoMatchingEncodingVariant rather than a lane count it did not ask for. Byte-pin verified against aarch64-linux-gnu-as: `cnt v3.8b, v7.8b` = 0x0E2058E3.

variants.$comment: CNT Vd.8B, Vn.8B — Q=0, eight byte lanes, 64 bits. ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3: `cnt v0.8b, v1.8b` = 0x0E205820, `cnt v3.8b, v7.8b` = 0x0E2058E3.

★ CNT Vd.16B, Vn.16B — Q=1, SIXTEEN byte lanes, 128 bits. base 0x4E205800 = the Q=0 word | bit 30. ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing: `cnt v0.16b, v1.16b` = 0x4E205820.
⚠ DECLARED 2026-09-02 (cycle P54, lane el) BECAUSE THE SPELLING BECAME REACHABLE, not because a producer appeared. Until the aarch64 gas dialect could parse a lane arrangement (D-ASM-DIALECTS-DECLARE-A-REGISTER-CLASS-NO-INSTRUCTION-CAN-NAME, gap 3) nothing could write either form, and the C path's `popcount` sequence emits only the Q=0 one. With the arrangement parsable, `cnt v0.16b, v1.16b` is a program BOTH references assemble, so refusing it would put DSS below the union on a form this very opcode already encodes — the whole width axis being one bit.
ⓘ THE OLD TEXT ABOVE — *'a caller emitting it at any other width gets A_NoMatchingEncodingVariant rather than a lane count it did not ask for'* — IS STILL TRUE AND IS NOW TRUE OF A SMALLER SET: widths 8, 16 and 32 still elect nothing. What changed is that 128 is no longer among them, because at 128 the instruction genuinely does count sixteen lanes.

opcodes.$comment: D-FULLC-STDBIT-ARM64-CNT-POPCOUNT: HORIZONTAL ADD of the register's eight byte lanes into the lowest lane — the reduction that turns eight per-byte counts into one total. The DSS verb is `addlanes_bytes`; it is the necessary partner of `popcount_bytes` and the reason this row's registry entry could NOT be closed by 'declare arm64 popcount as CNT', which was the closing work the row carried from 2026-07-15 until it was measured: CNT ALONE answers eight separate per-byte counts sitting in eight lanes, not a population count, so a single-opcode declaration on the `popcount` slot would have been a silent miscompile. AArch64 realization ADDV Bd, Vn.8B (AdvSIMD across lanes): 0 [31] | Q=0 8B [30] | U=0 [29] | 01110 [28:24] | size=00 [23:22] | 11000 [21:17] | opcode=11011 [16:12] | 10 [11:10] | Rn [9:5] | Rd [4:0] = 0x0E31B800 = 238139392. The destination is the B (8-bit) view, which is sufficient WITHOUT SATURATION: eight lanes of at most 8 sum to at most 64, and 64 fits an unsigned byte. Writing the B view zeroes bits 8..127, so the following cross-class move reads the total with no masking step. Guard keyed at width 64 for the same reason as `popcount_bytes` — the instruction always reduces eight bytes. Byte-pin verified against aarch64-linux-gnu-as: `addv b3, v7.8b` = 0x0E31B8E3.

variants.$comment: ADDV Bd, Vn.8B — Q=0, reduces eight byte lanes into the B (8-bit) view. ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3: `addv b0, v1.8b` = 0x0E31B820, `addv b3, v7.8b` = 0x0E31B8E3. ★ `destWidth` 8 is the DECLARATION that this instruction's two ends disagree — a 64-bit source reduced into an 8-bit destination — which is exactly what the dialect's `addv` row says with `destWidthFromOperands`, and what makes `addv b0, v1.8b` electable at all: without it the written `b0` and the written `v1.8b` disagree and the single-width model refuses the line.

★ ADDV Bd, Vn.16B — Q=1, reduces SIXTEEN byte lanes. base 0x4E31B800 = the Q=0 word | bit 30. ✔gas 2.42 + clang 18.1.3, agreeing: `addv b0, v1.16b` = 0x4E31B820. Still WITHOUT SATURATION: sixteen lanes of at most 8 sum to at most 128, and 128 fits an unsigned byte. Declared for the same reason as `popcount_bytes`' Q=1 arm — the spelling became writable, both references assemble it, and the bytes are one bit away from the form already shipped.

opcodes.$comment:
★★★ THE SIMD REGISTER-TO-REGISTER MOVE — `mov Vd.16b, Vn.16b`, WHICH IS **ORR** (cycle P54, lane av, D-ASM-ARM64-GAS-SPELLS-NO-ROUNDING-MODE-OR-VECTOR-MOVE). Lane `el` measured this word and left it undeclared; the operator ruled it in.
★★★ ONE WRITTEN SOURCE, TWO ENCODED FIELDS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE INSTRUCTION. AArch64 has no vector MOV: the assembler's `mov Vd.<T>, Vn.<T>` is an ALIAS for `orr Vd.<T>, Vn.<T>, Vn.<T>` — the source appears TWICE, in Rn [9:5] and Rm [20:16], and ORing a register with itself is the identity. So this opcode declares ONE operand and TWO wires from index 0. ✔MEASURED that the alias really is that instruction: `orr v0.16b, v1.16b, v1.16b` and `mov v0.16b, v1.16b` both assemble to 0x4EA11C20 on gas 2.42 AND clang 18.1.3, byte for byte.
★★ WHY IT IS NOT `fmov`'S WIDTH-128 ARM, and `registerClassOps`'s own note says the same thing from the other side: a 128-bit register move is a DIFFERENT INSTRUCTION with different bytes, not a wider FMOV. Declaring it here leaves the `fpr` class's `move` verb (`fmov`, widths 16/32/64) exactly as it was — 128 still elects nothing there and still fails loud at the emitting site, because no F128 value ever reaches a class-internal register copy on this pipeline.
⚠⚠ ONE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED: because a lane ARRANGEMENT is erased to a WIDTH before variant election, declaring these two arms also makes `mov %q0, %q1` and `mov %d0, %d1` electable — spellings GNU as 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 BOTH REJECT (✔MEASURED). That is not new with this opcode: `cnt %q0, %q1`, `cnt %d0, %d1` and `addv %b0, %d1` are ALREADY accepted at this base for the same reason, and all three are equally refused by both references. The whole class is anchored at [[D-ASM-ARRANGEMENT-ERASED-TO-A-WIDTH-BEFORE-ELECTION]], and ⚠⚠ IT IS CLOSED AS OF 2026-09-02 (cycle P54, lane `ae`) — SO THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE DESCRIBES THIS OPCODE'S PAST AND NOT ITS PRESENT. `mov q0, q1` and `mov d0, d1` are REFUSED now, and so are `cnt d0, d1` and `addv b0, d1`. ⚠ THE PREDICTION IN THE NEXT CLAUSE WAS HALF RIGHT: it took an engine + schema change AND a target-document one. The engine carries the lane WIDTH into election; the schema grew `wires[].lanes`/`laneBits` and `destLanes`/`destLaneBits`; and THIS OPCODE had to say which of the three readings each of its fields takes — `lanes` with NO `laneBits` on both wires and on the result, because the ORR it encodes is BITWISE and its lane size reaches no bit. That is also what makes `mov v0.4h, v1.4h` and `mov v0.2s, v1.2s` electable, which clang 18.1.3 assembles (both 0x0EA11C20) and gas 2.42 refuses — the one gas-vs-clang disagreement in this family, and a spelling DSS was BELOW the union on until the lane vocabulary landed. Refusing to declare the move would not have closed that leak — it would only have kept DSS BELOW the union on `mov v0.16b, v1.16b`, which both references assemble.
✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 agreeing: `mov v0.16b, v1.16b` = 0x4EA11C20 ⇒ base 0x4EA01C00 (Q=1); `mov v0.8b, v1.8b` = 0x0EA11C20 ⇒ base 0x0EA01C00 (Q=0).

variants.$comment: ORR Vd.16B, Vn.16B, Vn.16B — Q=1, sixteen byte lanes. base 0x4EA01C00.
ORR Vd.8B, Vn.8B, Vn.8B — Q=0, eight byte lanes; the top half of the destination is zeroed, which is what makes it a 64-bit move rather than a partial write. base 0x0EA01C00.

opcodes.$comment: D-FULLC-STDBIT-ARM64-CNT-POPCOUNT (2026-08-26): MIR Popcount's arm64 realization. ★ THIS ROW HAS NO `encoding`, AND THAT IS THE FACT — AArch64 has no scalar-GPR population-count instruction at all, so there is no single instruction to name; what it has is a SIMD lane counter plus a lane reduction, reached through a register-bank round trip. That is four instructions, and D-TARGET-ENCODING-TABLE-EXPRESSES-ONLY-THE-DEGENERATE-SEQUENCE is exactly the vocabulary for saying so: the row states 'on this target this operation is realized by these machine instructions', PLURAL, and the shared substrate emits what it was told. ★★ WHAT THIS REPLACES AND WHY THE OLD PLAN WAS WRONG. Both this registry row and the x86_64 `popcount` row's own comment said a future arm64 would 'share this slot' with CNT and need no lowering change. ✔MEASURED and REFUTED: CNT alone produces eight per-byte counts in eight lanes and is not a population count, and it writes the SIMD bank while MIR Popcount's result is an integer — so a one-instruction declaration would have been a silent miscompile in two independent ways. The capability split DID survive intact, but at the level of the SEQUENCE, not the instruction. ★ NO REGISTER CLASS IS ADDED. The temporaries are `fpr` (the D/S views), which AAPCS64 already makes allocatable; the 8-byte lane arrangement touches only the low 64 bits, so the 128-bit `vr` class stays non-allocatable exactly as its register rows say. Sequence temporaries are FRESH VIRTUAL REGISTERS the ordinary allocator assigns — nothing is reserved and no fixed scratch is stolen. ★ THE FALLBACK STAYS REACHABLE. `lowerPopcount` probes this mnemonic; a target that declares no `popcount` row still lowers MIR Popcount to the branchless SWAR bit-trick, which remains pinned by the x86_64-minus-`popcount` mutant in tests/lir/test_mir_to_lir.cpp and by the arm64 mutant beside it. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-26 by EXECUTION under qemu-aarch64: the exact four-instruction sequence answers __builtin_popcountl for 0, 1, all-ones, the single high bit, byte-spread patterns and 0x5555...., at BOTH widths, with the destination register pre-dirtied to all-ones first. 4 instructions replace the SWAR's 22.

lowering.$comment: The width axis is the OPERAND's promotion width P, which is what mir_to_lir's bit-count arms thread as the operation width (the count itself is always a small integer). Both sequences share steps 2 and 3 — the lane count and the lane reduction are width-blind because the 8-byte arrangement is a property of the INSTRUCTION, not of the value that reached it. Only the two cross-class moves carry the width, and on the 32-bit arm the entry move's upper-lane zeroing is what makes the shared 8-byte tail correct.

sequences.$comment: P = 64. vec = FMOV Dd,Xn (all eight source bytes land in lanes 0..7); lanes = CNT (per-byte counts); sum = ADDV (total, 0..64, in the B view); result = FMOV Xd,Dn.

P = 32. Identical but for the two moves: FMOV Sd,Wn puts the four source bytes in lanes 0..3 AND zeroes lanes 4..7, so the shared 8-byte CNT/ADDV tail counts exactly the 32 bits that were asked about; FMOV Wd,Sn reads the total back into a W register.

opcodes.$comment: ★★★ ADD (EXTENDED REGISTER), THE ONLY REGISTER-REGISTER ADD THAT CAN NAME THE STACK POINTER — [[D-ASM-ARM64-SP-AND-XZR-SHARE-ENCODING-31-SO-MOV-SP-SILENTLY-BECOMES-ZERO]] (cycle P55, 2026-09-03). ★★ WHY IT IS A SECOND OPCODE AND NOT A SECOND VARIANT OF `add`: it takes the SAME operand kinds at the SAME widths as the shifted-register form above, and `validate()` refuses two same-shape same-width variants of one opcode — first-match dispatch would silently shadow one. Election chooses between the two OPCODES instead, which is also the tier that can read a register's role. ⚠⚠ WHAT IT REPLACES IS A SILENT MISCOMPILE: ✔MEASURED at the P55 base, `add x0, sp, x1` compiled rc=0 and emitted 0x8B0103E0 = `add x0, xzr, x1`, so x0 got x1 instead of sp+x1, and `add sp, sp, x1` emitted 0x8B0103FF = `add xzr, xzr, x1` — THE STACK POINTER WAS NEVER ADJUSTED. ✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 probed SEPARATELY and agreeing: `add x0, sp, x1` = 0x8B2163E0, `add sp, sp, x1` = 0x8B2163FF, `add x30, sp, x29` = 0x8B3D63FE (a second Rd/Rm/Rn placement, so a field-placement error cannot hide behind one probe), `add w0, wsp, w1` = 0x0B2143E0, `add wsp, wsp, w1` = 0x0B2143FF. ★ THE BAKED EXTENSION IS THE `option` FIELD AT BITS 15:13 WITH imm3=0 — UXTX (011) at width 64 and UXTW (010) at width 32, which is what both assemblers select for a plain `add Xd, SP, Xm` with no extension written. A spelling that WRITES an extension (`add x0, sp, x1, uxtb #2`) is a different, undeclared form and stays fail-loud. ⚠ Rm READS 31 AS THE ZERO REGISTER even here, so `add x0, x1, sp` is refused — ✔MEASURED, both references refuse it too, and DSS used to emit 0x8B1F0020 (`add x0, x1, xzr`) for it.

variants.$comment: The sf=0 sibling, 0x0B204000 — the X word with bit 31 cleared AND `option` moved from UXTX (011) to UXTW (010), which is the W-width extension both references pick. Not merely a cleared sf: copying the X option here would encode a 64-bit extend of a 32-bit register.

opcodes.$comment: ★★★ SUB (EXTENDED REGISTER) — the `add_ext_reg` twin, same argument, same anchor. ✔MEASURED on both references: `sub x0, sp, x1` = 0xCB2163E0, `sub sp, sp, x1` = 0xCB2163FF, `sub w0, wsp, w1` = 0x4B2143E0, `sub w9, wsp, w10` = 0x4B2A43E9 (the second placement). At the P55 base DSS emitted 0xCB0103E0 (`sub x0, xzr, x1` = NEGATE x1) and 0xCB0103FF (`sub xzr, xzr, x1` — the stack pointer untouched). ⓘ `sub_sp_reg` above is the SAME encoding with Rd=Rn=SP baked; it stays because `mir_to_lir` emits it by name for the VLA dynamic frame and its LIR shape carries no result.

★★★ CMP (EXTENDED REGISTER) = SUBS ZR, <Xn|SP>, Xm — the third of the same family, and the one whose base word bakes its destination. ✔MEASURED on both references: `cmp sp, x0` = 0xEB2063FF, `cmp sp, x30` = 0xEB3E63FF, `cmp wsp, w0` = 0x6B2043FF. At the P55 base `cmp sp, x0` emitted 0xEB0003FF = `cmp xzr, x0` — a comparison against ZERO where the stack pointer was written, rc=0. ⚠ Rd IS BAKED AS 31 AND READS AS THE ZERO REGISTER (that is what makes SUBS a compare), while Rn reads 31 as SP — the two ends of ONE instruction disagreeing about what 31 means, which is exactly the fact `regRole` exists to carry. There is no `resultSlot`, so nothing declares a result role. ⓘ `cmp x0, sp` stays refused: Rm is a ZR-reading field, and both references refuse it too.

$condCodeEncodingComment: D-AS3-COND-CODE-ARM64 (mirror of x86's table): per-cond-code nibble for the AArch64 B.cond instruction's bits [3:0]. Numeric values are the AArch64 condition codes (ARM ARM C1.2.4): EQ=0, NE=1, CS/HS=2, CC/LO=3, HI=8, LS=9, GE=10(0xA), LT=11(0xB), GT=12(0xC), LE=13(0xD). Signed comparisons map slt→LT(0xB)=11, sle→LE(0xD)=13, sgt→GT(0xC)=12, sge→GE(0xA)=10; unsigned map ult→CC/LO=3, ule→LS=9, ugt→HI=8, uge→CS/HS=2. The encoder ORs this nibble into word 0 bits 0..3 of the jcc macro (vs x86's low 4 bits of the opcode byte — same field-position abstraction, different ISA placement). The 10 integer arms are REQUIRED; the FC3.5 float arms (next comment) are per-entry optional.
$condCodeEncodingFloatComment: FC3.5 sweep-c2 (FCmp lowering — D-COND-FLOAT-NAN-TRUTHINESS-FCMP): float condition arms over the FCMP NZCV truth table (ARM ARM: equal → Z=1,C=1; less → N=1; greater → C=1; unordered → C=1,V=1). fogt = GT (Z=0∧N=V, 0xC — unordered has N=0≠V=1 → false ✓; NOTE the integer-ugt HI=8 would be TRUE on unordered, a NaN miscompile — this is why float codes are separate); foge = GE (N=V, 0xA); foeq = EQ (Z=1, 0 — unordered Z=0 → false ✓); fune = NE (Z=0, 1 — TRUE on unordered, exactly C 6.5.9 `!=`); fuo = VS (V=1, 6 — after FCMP the overflow flag IS the unordered predicate); ford = VC (7). fone is deliberately ABSENT: NE is true on unordered, and no single AArch64 cond is `ordered ∧ unequal` — its absence signals the composed realization (One = cset-NE ∧ cset-VC), the mirror of x86's foeq/fune absence. Olt/Ole need no entries — the lowering swap-canonicalizes them to fogt/foge (MI/LS would also realize them directly; the swap keeps ONE target-blind rule).
$registersComment: AAPCS64 general-purpose registers x0..x30 + zero-register XZR (encoded as 31 in source operands; uses register's hwEncoding). Stack pointer `sp` is also encoded as 31 but in the SP-slot context — hwEncoding=31 with class GPR is shared between XZR and SP at the byte level. ★★★ THE SIMD&FP FILE IS DECLARED ONCE, AS `v0..v31` (class `fpr`, 16 bytes, no `subOf`), WITH `q`/`d`/`s`/`h`/`b` AS `subOf` VIEW ROWS OF THEM — R1 of the operator's design A′, 2026-08-28. ⚠ THIS SENTENCE REPLACED ONE THAT SAID THE FILE WAS `d0..d31` (class `fpr`), WHICH WAS TRUE AND HALF THE STORY: the OTHER half, `v0..v31` as an independent class `vr`, was declared a hundred rows further down with the SAME dwarfNumbers and the SAME hwEncodings and no relation between them. Two classes over one physical file is what made `"w"` bind a class no C value could live in and what left the `vr` free list permanently empty. See the root comment on the `v0` row for the full statement.

registers.$comment: ★★★ THE ZERO REGISTER, AND THE **DEFAULT** READING OF REGISTER FIELD 31 — `encodingRole`/`encodingRoleIsDefault`, [[D-ASM-ARM64-SP-AND-XZR-SHARE-ENCODING-31-SO-MOV-SP-SILENTLY-BECOMES-ZERO]] (cycle P55, 2026-09-03). ★★ WHY THE ROLE KEYS EXIST AT ALL: `xzr` and `sp` below are DIFFERENT REGISTERS at ONE `hwEncoding`, and which one a field means is a property of the FIELD. Nothing in this table said so, and the result was a SILENT MISCOMPILE — ✔MEASURED at the P55 base through the real CLI with the words read back by `aarch64-linux-gnu-objdump`, `mov x0, sp` emitted 0xAA1F03E0, which decodes as `mov x0, xzr`, so x0 received ZERO instead of the stack pointer, rc=0 and no diagnostic; `mov sp, x0` emitted 0xAA0003FF, a NO-OP. gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 (probed SEPARATELY and agreeing on all 128 probes of that census) emit 0x910003E0 / 0x9100001F, the ADD-immediate alias — a DIFFERENT INSTRUCTION. Ten more forms were wrong the same way and fifteen more were ACCEPTED where both references refuse. ★★★ `encodingRoleIsDefault` IS WHAT KEEPS THE OTHER ~250 VARIANTS SILENT AND CORRECT. On AArch64 field 31 is the zero register EVERYWHERE except add/subtract-immediate, the extended-register forms and the load/store BASE, so the rule is declared once here and only the exceptions carry `regRole` on the field. A field that names nothing resolves to THIS row. ⓘ `xzr` still has no `dwarfNumber` — it never had one and the role keys do not give it one.
registers.name: xzr

registers.$comment: ★★★ THE STACK POINTER — the NON-default reading of register field 31, so every field that means SP must SAY so with `regRole: "stackPointer"` ([[D-ASM-ARM64-SP-AND-XZR-SHARE-ENCODING-31-SO-MOV-SP-SILENTLY-BECOMES-ZERO]]). ⚠ THE OLD COMMENT HERE WAS TRUE AND INERT, and that is the lesson worth keeping: it read *shares hwEncoding=31 with XZR at the byte level (the context determines which)* — a correct sentence, in prose, that no code could read. `validate()` now REFUSES a target document whose registers collide on (class, widthBytes, hwEncoding) without distinct `encodingRole`s and exactly one default, so the fact is enforced instead of merely written down. ⓘ The rest of the old comment still holds: the substrate treats the two as distinct names with distinct ORDINALS, and the JSON-side ordinal is what the calling-convention lookup uses.
registers.name: sp

registers.$comment:
★★★ THE AArch64 SIMD&FP REGISTER FILE, DECLARED **ONCE** (R1 of the operator's design A′, 2026-08-28 — D-TARGET-ARM64-W-CONSTRAINT-BINDS-A-CLASS-NO-C-VALUE-EVER-LIVES-IN, D-LIR-SUBREGISTER-AWARE-ALLOCATION-FOR-ALIASED-VIEWS). ⚠⚠ WHAT THIS REPLACED, AND WHY IT WAS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A STYLE: this file used to declare the SAME THIRTY-TWO PHYSICAL REGISTERS TWICE — `d0..d31` as class `fpr` (8 bytes) and `v0..v31` as class `vr` (16 bytes), ✔MEASURED 32 rows each, ZERO `subOf` on either side, and the SAME `dwarfNumber` 64..95 and `hwEncoding` on every pair. Two classes over one file is what made `"w"` bind a class no C value can live in, what made an `{fpr, vr}` move look like a missing verb (there is nothing to move BETWEEN), and what left the `vr` free list permanently empty. The GPR file was always modelled right — `x0` is the row and `w0` is its `subOf` view — and this block now says the same thing about the SIMD&FP file. `regClassForCoreType` was CORRECT throughout and is NOT touched: the config was wrong. ★★ THE ROOTS ARE `v0..v31`: the whole 128-bit register, class `fpr`, no `subOf`, and the only FP rows a calling convention may name (D-TARGET-CC-NAMES-SUB-REGISTER refuses a cc naming a view). `hwEncoding` is the 5-bit register number EVERY SIMD&FP instruction form shares; `dwarfNumber` 64+k is the V register DWARF numbers. ★★ THE VIEWS ARE `q`/`d`/`s`/`h`/`b`, exactly the five spellings `aarch64-linux-gnu-as` accepts for a scalar SIMD&FP operand, each `subOf` its `v` root at its own `widthBytes`. They are NEVER allocatable (they appear in no cc list, which `validate()` enforces): the width an instruction runs at rides the LIR instruction's width flag and the register table supplies the shared encoding. ⚠ `q_k` is the SAME WIDTH as its root on purpose — `q0` and `v0` are two assembler spellings of one 128-bit register (scalar vs vector form), and a source language that can write `str q0, [sp]` needs the name to resolve. ★ ONLY `v_k` AND `d_k` CARRY A `dwarfNumber`, AND THAT PAIR IS LOAD-BEARING: `DwarfRegisterReverseMap::build` accepts two rows sharing a number when they share an `hwEncoding` and lets the NARROWEST win, so DWARF 72 keeps resolving to `d8` — which is exactly what GNU `as` translates `.cfi_offset d8` into, and exactly the low 64 bits AAPCS64 §6.1.2 guarantees a callee preserves of v8..v15. Giving `s`/`h`/`b` numbers too would put three more rows in that collision with nothing to decide between them. ★★★ THE `q` SPELLINGS ARE **ALIASES OF THESE VERY ROWS**, AND THE SENTENCE THAT SAID THE ALIAS KEY WAS UNBUILT EXPIRED ON 2026-09-02 (cycle P55, lane lq, [[D-TARGET-ARM64-HALF-BYTE-QUAD-MEMORY-FORMS-UNDECLARED]]). It read *a same-width ALIAS is a different key, and it is not built here because nothing consumes it*, standing on a ✔RE-MEASURED fact that `q0` was not a register NAME this table declared. Both halves are now false, and the SECOND is what moved: `ldr q0,[x1,#16]` = 0x3DC00420 is assembled by gas 2.42 AND clang 18.1.3 (✔MEASURED, probed separately) and was REFUSED by DSS at the register lookup, so there is a consumer and the key is built. ★★ WHY IT IS AN `aliases` LIST ON THE `v` ROW AND NOT A `q` ROW OF ITS OWN, and the earlier reasoning survives intact: `q0` and `v0` are two ASSEMBLER SPELLINGS of one whole register (scalar form vs vector form), not two WIDTHS of it, so `subOf` is the wrong relation — R1 listed `q` among five view families and ✔MEASURED 32 violations of the STRICTLY-WIDER rule, and relaxing that `>` to `>=` to fit the config would have deleted a protection, which is backwards. That rule is now enforced at LOAD rather than only by `TargetSubRegisters.NoSubRegisterAppearsInAnyCallingConventionList` (✔MEASURED at the P55 base that a same-width `subOf` LOADED CLEAN, so the protection judged these two tables and nothing else). ★★★ AND A SECOND ROW WAS NOT MERELY UNNECESSARY, IT WAS THE WORSE ANSWER: it would have minted a SECOND ORDINAL for one machine register, and `mir_to_lir`'s `canonicalAsmRegister` walks `subOf` only — so an `asm` clobber naming `q0` would have reserved the spelling nobody allocates while `v0` stayed free, a silent wrong-register answer. With `aliases` there is ONE ordinal: `registerByName` answers `v0` for either spelling, so the asm resolution, the clobber canonicalisation and `lir_text`'s ordinal comparison agree with no second walk to get wrong, and the double-count [[D-TARGET-ALIASED-VIEWS-BOTH-ALLOCATABLE-DOUBLE-COUNT-ONE-FILE]] guards is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a rule. ⚠ A CALLING CONVENTION MAY STILL NEVER NAME ONE, and that IS a rule: `buildFreeLists` matches a cc list against each row's CANONICAL name, so `q0` in `argFprs` would match no row and silently drop v0 from the pool — `validate()` refuses it by name, beside [[D-TARGET-CC-NAMES-SUB-REGISTER]]. ⓘ THE `d`/`s`/`h`/`b` ROWS ARE UNCHANGED: they carry a WIDTH the parent does not, which is a fact about the machine and belongs in a row; an alias carries no field that differs at all.

★★★ AND SINCE 2026-09-03 EACH `v` ROW ALSO SAYS THAT ITS OWN NAME IS **NOT AN OPERAND SPELLING ON ITS OWN** — `nameRequiresLaneArrangement`, [[D-ASM-ARM64-BARE-V-REGISTER-ACCEPTED-IN-A-SCALAR-MEMORY-OPERAND]] (cycle P55, lane vd). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-03, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 probed SEPARATELY and agreeing: `ldr v0,[x9,#16]` is `Error: unexpected register type at operand 1` / `invalid operand for instruction`, and so is `ldr v0.16b,[x9]`, `ldr v0,[x9]`, `mov v0,v1`, `fadd v0,v1,v2` and `stp v0,v1,[x9]` — a bare `v` is not a scalar operand spelling ANYWHERE, at any width, in either reference. ★★ WHAT DSS DID INSTEAD, AND IT IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE ROW'S BAND: `ldr v0,[x9,#16]` compiled rc=0 and emitted **0x3DC00520**, which `aarch64-linux-gnu-objdump` decodes as `ldr q0,[x9,#16]` — BYTE-IDENTICAL to what both references emit for the `q0` spelling. So this was an UNDECLARED ALIAS producing correct bytes for a program no assembler would accept, and NOT a silent wrong answer; had the bytes decoded as anything else the row would have re-banded upward on the spot. ★★★ WHY THE KEY IS ON THE **ROW** AND NOT A NARROWING OF IT. The register is correctly declared and must stay so: `subOf` rows resolve THROUGH it, it is the only FP name a calling convention may spell, and `v0.16b` must keep working (✔MEASURED: `mov v0.16b, v1.16b` = 0x4EA11C20 on DSS and on both references). What is wrong is one SPELLING in one POSITION, so that is exactly what the key removes — `q0` (an alias) and `d0`/`s0`/`h0`/`b0` (their own rows) are untouched, and `validate()` refuses the key on a row with no `aliases` so it can never leave a register with no bare spelling at all. ⚠ THE SCOPE WAS **NARROWER** THAN THE ROW PREDICTED, ✔MEASURED rather than assumed: the row said the over-acceptance covered *every width and every mnemonic*, and it did not. `mov v0,v1`, `fmov v0,v1` and `fadd v0,v1,v2` were ALREADY refused (`A_AsmTextUnsupported`, no 128-bit variant of those opcodes), so the only mnemonics that accepted a bare `v` were the four that have a 128-bit memory form — `ldr`/`str`/`ldur`/`stur`. Bare `v` was accepted exactly where `q` is accepted and produced exactly `q`'s bytes: a complete alias, not a partial one.

registers.$comment: ★★ THE 32-BIT W VIEWS — the arm64 half of `subOf`'s first real consumer (2026-08-13); see the x86_64 twin for the full rationale. `w0` is the low 32 bits of `x0`: ONE machine register, two spellings, and the ISA distinguishes them by the instruction's sf bit rather than by a register number (the 5-bit hwEncoding is shared). So a narrow spelling resolves to the parent ordinal and the width rides the LIR instruction. `wzr` is included because it is the W view of `xzr` and `mov w0, wzr` is how AArch64 spells a 32-bit zero; `wsp` is omitted (no consumer). ⚠ NOT ALLOCATABLE, and the mechanism changed on 2026-08-13 — this sentence used to say 'both allocator paths skip a non-empty `subOf`'. BOTH skips have been DELETED as unreachable defence: ✔MEASURED, `allocatable` is built EXCLUSIVELY from the six calling-convention lists, so a row named in none of them could never enter a pool for a skip to catch. A calling convention naming a `subOf` register is now REFUSED AT CONFIG LOAD (`TargetSchemaData::validate()`'s `checkRefs`, `C_MalformedJson` with the offending JSON path). These rows appear in no cc list, which is now enforced rather than merely true.
registers.name: w0

registers.$comment: ★★★ `wsp` — THE 32-BIT VIEW OF THE STACK POINTER, ADDED 2026-09-03 ([[D-ASM-ARM64-SP-AND-XZR-SHARE-ENCODING-31-SO-MOV-SP-SILENTLY-BECOMES-ZERO]]). ⚠ IT WAS THE ONE MISSING **NAME** IN THE ENCODING-31 FAMILY, and the census that found the silent miscompile above found it too: ✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 both assemble `mov w0, wsp` = 0x110003E0, `mov wsp, w0` = 0x1100001F, `add w0, wsp, #16` = 0x110043E0, `add wsp, wsp, #16` = 0x110043FF and `cmp wsp, #16` = 0x710043FF, while DSS refused every one of them at the register lookup (A_AsmTextUnsupported). The `wzr` row beside it existed because `mov w0, wzr` is how AArch64 spells a 32-bit zero; the SP half had no consumer until the `mov`-to/from-SP alias got one. ★★ THE SHAPE IS EXACTLY `wzr`'s AND `w0`'s: a `subOf` view of its 64-bit parent at its own `widthBytes`, sharing the parent's `hwEncoding` because AArch64 distinguishes the two by the instruction's sf bit and not by a register number. NOT ALLOCATABLE — it appears in no calling-convention list, which `validate()` enforces for every `subOf` row (D-TARGET-CC-NAMES-SUB-REGISTER). No `dwarfNumber`: a narrow view inherits its parent's identity, exactly as `w0` does. ⚠ IT MUST DECLARE A ROLE: `wsp` and `wzr` are a SECOND colliding pair at (gpr, 4 bytes, 31), and `validate()` refuses a collision whose rows do not each say which reading they are. ✔MEASURED that the references refuse to MIX the widths — `mov x0, wsp` and `mov w0, sp` are errors in both — which the width axis already enforces.
registers.name: wsp

$asmConstraintsComment:
★★★ WHICH GNU INLINE-ASM CONSTRAINT LETTER MEANS WHICH REGISTER IS TARGET VOCABULARY — see the twin block in x86_64.target.json for the full rationale and for the [[D-CONFIG-ASM-DIALECT-DECLARED-AS-TARGET-VOCABULARY]] line this facet is drawn on. What THIS file adds is the proof that the mapping is config and not code.
★★ THIS TARGET IS THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE THAT MAKES THE FACET NECESSARY. ✔MEASURED, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -S`: `"=a"` here is `error: impossible constraint in 'asm'` — and so are `b`, `c`, `d`, `D` and `q`, every one of which x86_64 declares. A shared C++ table would have had to branch on the architecture to say that; this file says it by SAYING NOTHING, and the consumer's refusal renders the valid list from whichever target it was handed.
✔MEASURED, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -S`, with three competing live `"r"` operands: r→x0, w→v0, `"m"(*p)`→`[x0]`, `"i"(7)`→`7`. ⚠ THE COMPILER IS NAMED HERE BECAUSE ITS ABSENCE COST A CYCLE. Every arrow in this block is what **gcc PRINTS** — the evidence that the binding on the row below is the right one. It is not, and never was, a claim about what THIS compiler emits. An elided subject read as one: a lane took `"m"(*p)`→`[x0]` for a DSS capability claim, found the pipeline refusing the letter, and filed the two halves as a contradiction inside one config (D-ASM-MEMORY-CONSTRAINT-REFUSED-DESPITE-BEING-DECLARED). The row was RIGHT and the pipeline was WRONG — `"m"` is realized end-to-end now, witnessed by execution in `examples/c/c_inline_asm_memory_operand`. ⇒ the subject of a measurement is STATED in this file, never inferred from the paragraph it sits in. ⚠ NOTE `i` → `7` with NO sigil while x86_64 emits `$7`: the sigil is DIALECT grammar, which is exactly why the operandKind (`imm32`) is identical on both targets and the printing is not this file's business.
★★★ `w` ⇒ `fpr`, AND THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO ARGUE THE OPPOSITE FROM A REAL MEASUREMENT OF A DIFFERENT QUESTION — the clearest example in this file of an instrument answering an adjacent question. It read: *`w` → `vr`, NOT `fpr`, AND THE MEASUREMENT SETTLES IT RATHER THAN INTUITION*, on the evidence below. ✔MEASURED: `double dw(double a){ __asm__("# W %0 %1" : "=w"(o) : "w"(a)); }` emits `# W v0 v0` — gcc's DEFAULT print for a `w` operand is the V-register name regardless of the C type, and that rendering is REAL and re-measured (gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 18.1.3, -O0 and -O2, `float`/`double`/`long double`/`__int128`: all print `v0`). ⚠⚠ BUT IT ANSWERS *WHICH VIEW A BARE REFERENCE NAMES*, which is `asmBareOperandWidths`' question, NOT *which register FILE the value lives in*, which is this row's. Binding the letter to a SECOND CLASS over the same file made `"w"(double)` refuse by name at debug AND release — *binds register class 'vr', but the value it carries lives in class 'fpr'* — while gcc compiles it and allocates `d0`. ★ With the file declared ONCE (R1) there is one class over it, so the two answers stop competing: the class is `fpr`, and which VIEW a bare `%0` names stays `asmBareOperandWidths`' to say. The `d0`/`s0` narrow spellings still come from the `%d0`/`%s0` operand MODIFIERS, which are dialect grammar and live with the dialect. D-TARGET-ARM64-W-CONSTRAINT-BINDS-A-CLASS-NO-C-VALUE-EVER-LIVES-IN.
⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED: `x` and `y`. Both bind V registers here (✔MEASURED x→v0, y→v0), and the restriction is MEASURED, not taken from the letter's documented meaning — the probe pushes N simultaneous live operands through one asm and reads the largest N that still compiles: **r=30, w=30, x=16, y=8**. ★ READ THOSE CAREFULLY: 30 is the ALLOCATOR CEILING, not a set size — `r` and `w` both stop there, and this target declares 65 gpr / 32 vr rows — so `w` is only proven to be ≥30 and is taken as the full V file. `x`=16 and `y`=8 sit BELOW that ceiling, which is what makes them genuine subclass measurements (V0-V15 and V0-V7) rather than 'too many operands'. The `w` control clinches it: it COMPILES the identical 18-operand asm that `x` refuses, printing `v0 v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 v6 v7 v16 v17 v18 v19 v20 v21 v22 v23 v24 v25`. TargetRegClass cannot express a SUBSET, so declaring `x` or `y` as plain `vr` would load clean, read as support, and hand the allocator registers gcc forbids ⇒ the same refusal x86_64 applies to `Q`, and the deferral is stated in full in that file's twin comment (a FOURTH binding axis — an explicit register-name list — deliberately not built; trigger: the first client whose inline asm uses a subclass letter, which ✔MEASURED none does today).
⚠ Also absent: `k` (the stack pointer). ✔MEASURED in BOTH directions — `"=k"` as an output AND `"k"` as an input are each `error: inconsistent operand constraints in an 'asm'` — so there is no measured binding to declare. The two-direction check matters: an earlier note asserted only the output half, which would have left the input half an untested guess sitting inside a sentence that read as a measurement.

No width arithmetic reproduces both — *narrowest view ≥ the type width* yields `w0` for an `int` here (gcc renders `x0`), and *the widest view* yields `%rax` for an `int` there (gcc renders `%eax`). ★★ AND IT IS A TARGET FACT, CHECKED WITH THE INSTRUMENT `asmConstraints`' OWN CHARTER DEMANDS: under `-masm=att` vs `-masm=intel` on one processor the selected VIEW is identical and only the sigil moves, while the control (`movq %rsi, (%rdi)` → `mov QWORD PTR [rdi], rsi`) moves as a dialect fact must.
$asmBareOperandWidthsFpComment: ★★★ `fpr` IS `registerNatural` — R5 OF THE OPERATOR'S DESIGN A′, LANDED P50, AND THE ROW D-ASM-AARCH64-FP-BARE-OPERAND-WIDTH-DIVERGES-FROM-REFERENCE CLOSES AT EXACTLY THIS FLIP. ✔RE-MEASURED AT THE P50 BASE (2026-09-01), gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 18.1.3 probed SEPARATELY, -O0 AND -O2, substituted text read out of `-S` (clang under `-fno-integrated-as`, without which its integrated assembler rejects the synthetic probe mnemonic — an instrument result, not a finding): a bare `%0` on a `"w"`-bound `float`, `double`, `long double` AND `__int128` renders `v0` under BOTH references at BOTH levels — 16 of 16 rows, unanimous, the same matrix P45 measured. `v0` is the FULL 128-bit register, so the reference rule for this class is `registerNatural`, and `TargetSchema::registerClassNaturalWidthBits` answers 128 because the `v` roots are this class's only rows with no `subOf` (R1's declaration, one file, declared once). MSVC 19.51 ABSTAINS — ✔MEASURED, `__asm__` is `error C2065: undeclared identifier`, so the disjunction here is gcc ∪ clang. ★★ THE PRECONDITION THE ROW STATED FOR THIS FLIP IS ALSO LANDED, IN THE SAME CHANGE: the seven modifier letters are declared CLASS-SCOPED in `asm-arm64-gas.lang.json` (`w`/`x` ⇒ gpr; `b`/`h`/`s`/`d`/`q` ⇒ fpr, widths 8/16/32/64/128), so a template that means the narrow view can SAY so (`%d0` renders d0 under both references) and a bare reference no longer has to carry that meaning by accident. ⚠ WHAT THE FLIP CHANGED OBSERVABLY AT P50 WAS A REFUSAL'S TIER AND HONESTY, NOT AN EMITTED BYTE, AND THAT WAS STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: the dialect declared no floating-point mnemonic then, so a bare `"w"`-bound placeholder inside a real instruction previously died at the ENCODER's register-bank guard (A_NoMatchingEncodingVariant, a gpr field handed a v-register — ✔MEASURED at the P50 base) and afterwards died EARLIER and TRUER: the operand states 128 bits and the template translator's width-flag map refuses by name, pointing at the real limit (no shipped target declares a width-128 encoding variant). ★★ THE PREDICTION THAT FOLLOWED — *the day this document gains an FP instruction, bare references and `%q0` start electing with no further config or C++ change* — CAME DUE ON 2026-09-02 AND IS HALF CONFIRMED, HALF REFUTED (D-ASM-DIALECTS-DECLARE-A-REGISTER-CLASS-NO-INSTRUCTION-CAN-NAME, cycle P54: the dialect now spells `fadd`/`fsub`/`fmul`/`fdiv`/`fneg`/`fcmp`/`fmov`). ✔MEASURED: the NARROW letters elect exactly as promised and with ZERO further changes — `__asm__("fadd %d0, %d1, %d2" : "=w"(r) : "w"(a), "w"(b))` over doubles compiles rc=0 and runs to 42 under qemu-aarch64, where the same statement was `A_AsmTextUnsupported … unknown mnemonic 'fadd'` the hour before. ⚠⚠ THE HALF THAT WAS REFUTED HAS SINCE BEEN CONFIRMED, AND THE SENTENCE RECORDING IT LASTED HOURS. $registerClassOpsComment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): per-register-class move/load/store mnemonics — the same FC2 Part B table x86_64 declares. A class WITHOUT a row uses the universal defaults (mov/load/store) iff it is gpr — the substrate default class; every other row-less class FAILS LOUD at the consumer (L_RequiredLirOpcodeMissing), because the class-blind alternative is a silent miscompile (a GPR ORR/LDUR against a D-register hwEncoding assembles to valid-looking words that move the WRONG register file). fpr: move=FMOV(D), load=LDUR(D), store=STUR(D). ★★ THE TWO PARAGRAPHS ABOVE AND BELOW WERE TWO SEPARATE `$registerClassOpsComment` KEYS IN THIS DOCUMENT UNTIL 2026-08-30 (cycle P46), AND JSON LET THAT PASS: every mainstream parser -- nlohmann, which is what DSS uses -- keeps the LAST occurrence and drops the first WITHOUT A DIAGNOSTIC. So the paragraph above this sentence was dead text the loader never saw, while being the one a reader meets first. Merged rather than deleted, because neither subsumes the other: the first says WHY this table exists and what a missing row costs, the second says what a ROW MEANS now that its subject is an ordered pair. D-CONFIG-A-DUPLICATE-JSON-KEY-IS-DROPPED-WITHOUT-A-DIAGNOSTIC. D-TARGET-NO-CROSS-CLASS-MOVE-VERB: a row's subject is an ORDERED PAIR of register classes — `class` is the SOURCE and the optional `to` is the DESTINATION, `to` omitted meaning the DIAGONAL (a copy within one file), which is what every row written before this key existed meant. ★ ONE TABLE, not two: `move` answers the single question *how does this machine copy a bit pattern from class A to class B?* for every (A,B) including A == B. ⚠ `load`/`store` are DIAGONAL-ONLY and the loader refuses them off it: they relate a class to MEMORY, and memory is not a register class. ⚠ AND THE MOVE'S OWN ENCODING IS CHECKED AGAINST THE PAIR IT IS FILED UNDER, so a move whose declared banks disagree with its row is refused at load rather than writing a register number into the wrong file at run time.

registerClassOps.$comment:
★★★ THE ONE SIMD&FP CLASS, AND ITS MEMORY VERBS ARE WIDTH-ELECTED (R2 of design A′). ⚠⚠ WHAT THIS REPLACED: a SECOND `registerClassOps` row for class `vr` carrying `load: fldur_q` / `store: fstur_q` and deliberately no `move`. That row existed only because the register file was declared twice; with one class there is one row, and the Q-form memory ops are `fldur`/`fstur`'s **width-128 variants** — the same width axis `fldur`/`fstur` already use to pick STUR Dt (64) from STUR St (32), and the same axis `movq_gpr_to_xmm` keys its FMOV Dd,Xn / Sd,Wn pair on. The `_q` mnemonics are DELETED: they were a second spelling of one instruction family's widest arm. ★★ `move` IS `fmov` AND IT IS DECLARED AT WIDTHS **32/64** ONLY — the list read *16/32/64* until 2026-09-02 (cycle P54, lane ae), when `fmov`'s width-16 arm was deleted for being ABOVE THE UNION (✔MEASURED, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 both REFUSE `fmov h0, h1` at the default -march; see that opcode's `$variantsComment`). Width 16 now elects nothing here, exactly as width 128 does, and for the same fail-loud reason: nothing on this pipeline produces an F16 class-internal copy, because no shipped language forms an F16 value at all. A width-128 register-to-register SIMD move is NOT a wider FMOV — AArch64 spells it **ORR** (`mov v_d.16b, v_n.16b` is the assembler alias), a different instruction with different bytes. ✔MEASURED that nothing consumes one: an F128 value is memory-resident on this pipeline (`lowerF128Store` issues GPR word stores; `LirVerifier`'s store rule names F80 and F128 as the two memory-resident kinds), so no 128-bit value ever reaches a class-internal register copy. Leaving `fmov` UNGUARDED would be worse — it would silently encode FMOV Dd,Dn for a 128-bit move and drop the top half. So the widths that exist are declared and 128 elects NOTHING HERE, which fails loud at the emitting site naming the pair and the op.
⚠⚠ THE CLAUSE THAT SAID *declaring ORR with no consumer would be dead vocabulary* WENT FALSE LATER THE SAME DAY (2026-09-02, lane av, D-ASM-ARM64-GAS-SPELLS-NO-ROUNDING-MODE-OR-VECTOR-MOVE): ORR **IS** declared now, as the opcode `move_bytes`, and it has a consumer — the aarch64 gas dialect's `mov` row, which is a TEXT surface rather than a codegen one. The trigger-discipline reasoning was sound and the premise under it was about CODEGEN only; an inline `asm` can spell an instruction no pass ever produces. ⓘ **THIS ROW IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED**: `move` stays `fmov` at 16/32/64 and width 128 still elects nothing here. Pointing `move` at `move_bytes` would replace a fail-loud gap with an untested path — nothing in the pipeline produces a 128-bit class-internal copy, so the new verb would have no witness, which is the same dead-vocabulary objection one level up.
registerClassOps.$loadScaledComment: ★★★ THE LONG-REACH TWINS, AND THE SLOT IS PER-CLASS BECAUSE THE REACH IS (D-TARGET-REGISTER-CLASS-OPS-HAVE-NO-LONG-REACH-MEMORY-FORM). `fldur`/`fstur` reach ±256 bytes; every frame access funnels through `selectFrameMemOp`, which swaps an offset past that reach onto the SCALED unsigned-offset form. Before this pair the swap could only fire for the INTEGER file's `load`/`store` — the integer file was the only one whose twin was declared — so an FP frame access past ±256 kept `fstur` and fail-louded at the encoder. ⚠ THE INTEGER FILE DECLARES ITS OWN PAIR WITHOUT A ROW HERE: `gpr` has no diagonal registerClassOps row on this target, so its four memory verbs come from the universal `load`/`store`/`load_u`/`store_u` mnemonic defaults. That asymmetry is the SAME one `move` already had, not a new one.

registerClassOps.$comment: gpr -> fpr, the cross-FILE move: FMOV Dd,Xn at width 64 and FMOV Sd,Wn at width 32, already declared byte-pinned on `movq_gpr_to_xmm` for the SIMD popcount sequence. ★ D-TARGET-NO-CROSS-CLASS-MOVE-VERB fills the slot `registerClassOps` never had; the BYTES were here all along. The width guard is load-bearing here because the cross-file forms read a different number of bytes out of the source file, so the emitting site threads the operand's own width. ⚠ THE CLAUSE THAT USED TO STAND HERE — *in a way it is not on the diagonal: `fmov d,d` carries no width guard* — WAS ALREADY FALSE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN (R2, P47, had given the diagonal `fmov` three width-guarded arms) and is doubly false since 2026-09-02, when each of those arms got its own ftype word. The diagonal is width-keyed for the SAME reason this row is: the width IS the ftype field.

fpr -> gpr, the mirror direction: FMOV Xd,Dn at width 64 and FMOV Wd,Sn at width 32 (`movq_xmm_to_gpr`). Kept a SEPARATE opcode from the row above for the reason both opcode rows state: the variant guard keys only on (operandKinds, width) and both directions are `reg` at the same width, so one opcode carrying both would silently pick a direction.

$wideFloatSoftcallsComment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-IEEE128-ARITH (LD-2): the softfloat runtime-libcall table for IEEE binary128 `long double` arithmetic. Each row names the libgcc helper an F128 op lowers to a CALL of, plus the physical registers the operands/result are marshalled through (AAPCS64: __*tf3 take two Q-register quad args in v0/v1 and return the quad in v0; __fixtfsi takes the quad in v0 and returns the int32 in x0; __extenddftf2 takes a double in d0 and returns the quad in v0). The MIR→LIR engine keys the softcall verb on TypeKind::F128 + the PRESENCE of the row for the op (wideFloatSoftcall(op) != nullptr) — NEVER a target-name/format check; a target that declares F128 but omits this table falls straight through to the requireEncodedFloatWidth fail-loud gate (the load-bearing agnosticism condition). The helper symbols live in libgcc_s.so.1 (see wideFloatSoftcallLibraryByFormat); the lowerer auto-injects the extern import on first use. ★ D-TARGET-ENCODING-WIDTH-GUARD (LD-3) ADDED THE SIX `cmp_*` ROWS, and they differ from the arithmetic ones in ONE structural way worth stating here: their result is not a binary128 but an `int` in x0 whose SIGN answers the predicate, so the lowering finishes them with an ordinary INTEGER compare against zero (`cmp w0, 0`) and the SAME setcc/zext tail every integer compare uses — no float flags are involved at all. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-03 with both aarch64 references probed SEPARATELY and agreeing helper-for-helper (aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `bl __lttf2; cmp w0,0; blt`; clang 18.1.3 --target=aarch64-linux-gnu `bl __lttf2; cset w0, lt`); all six are exported from /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu/lib/libgcc_s.so.1 as defined text symbols (verified with `nm -D`, which matters because DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every symbol a descriptor lists — one absent name breaks the LOAD of every binary). One row per C operator, not one shared three-way compare: libgcc's `__cmptf2` is unspecified on NaN and is not exported at all, while each of these returns the sign that makes ordered predicates FALSE and `!=` TRUE on a NaN operand, which is exactly C 6.5.9.

wideFloatSoftcalls.$comment: D-TARGET-ENCODING-WIDTH-GUARD (LD-5): the SIX rows that finish the binary128 scalar surface — negate, and the five remaining conversions between `long double` and a native scalar. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-04, both aarch64 references probed SEPARATELY and agreeing helper-for-helper on all five conversions (aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `bl` and clang 18.1.3 `bl`/`b` — clang tail-CALLS the two widening helpers, which is the same helper by a different branch): `(unsigned)ld`→__fixunstfsi, `(long long)ld`→__fixtfdi, `(double)ld`→__trunctfdf2, `(float)ld`→__trunctfsf2, `(long double)someFloat`→__extendsftf2. All six symbols are DEFINED text exports of /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu/lib/libgcc_s.so.1 (`nm -D`, re-verified this cycle — it matters because DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every symbol a descriptor lists, so one absent name breaks the LOAD of every binary). ⚠⚠ TWO OF THESE RETURN 32-BIT VALUES AND THAT IS THE SILENT-MISCOMPILE RISK ON THIS AXIS: AAPCS64 §6.8.2 leaves the bits ABOVE a return type's width UNSPECIFIED, so `__fixunstfsi`'s `unsigned int` and `__trunctfsf2`'s `float` must be captured with the W/S-form move, not the X/D-form. The lowerer states that width from the MIR result type at the capture site (`registerOpWidthFlags`), the same fix LD-3 made for the comparison helpers' `cmp`. ★★ `neg` IS THE ONE ROW THAT DOES NOT MATCH WHAT THE REFERENCES EMIT, deliberately: gcc flips the sign bit inline with `eor x1, x2, #0x8000000000000000` on the high word and clang with `eor w8, w8, #0x80` on byte 15 — NEITHER calls `__negtf2`. Realizing that inline would put the LOCATION of a binary128's sign bit (byte 15, bit 7 — a byte-ORDER fact) inside the target-agnostic lowerer, which is the slow agnosticism break this project keeps paying for; the libcall says the same thing in the target's own vocabulary. ✔MEASURED under qemu-aarch64 that it IS the same thing bit for bit: `__negtf2` maps +0.0↔-0.0, flips 1.0's sign, and preserves BOTH a quiet NaN's payload and a signalling NaN's quiet bit (0x7fff…a55a → 0xffff…a55a; 0x7fff…0033 → 0xffff…0033) — a pure sign flip, so the divergence is a peephole and not a semantic one. ⓘ NO `to_u64` ROW, and its absence is a STATED boundary rather than an oversight: libgcc exports `__fixunstfdi` and this axis could take it today, but the x87 axis realizes `(unsigned long long)ld` only through a compare against 2^63 plus a conditional bias — a BRANCHING sequence the straight-line x87 lowerer cannot emit — so declaring it here alone would make one cast compile on arm64 and fail loud on x86_64. Both stay walled until both can ship.

The `float` end names `s0`, not `d0`, on BOTH of its rows. The two views share hwEncoding 0, so the emitted register FIELD is identical either way and the width flag alone elects FMOV's ftype — but a row that named `d0` for a `float` would be declaring the ABI wrongly, and the next reader would have to re-derive from the width flag what the name should have said outright.

$wideFloatSoftcallLibraryComment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-IEEE128-ARITH (LD-2): the DT_NEEDED library each minted softcall extern binds to, keyed by object-format name. $callingConventionsComment: AAPCS64 (https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa/blob/main/aapcs64/aapcs64.rst). Integer args: x0..x7. FP args: d0..d7 (D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE 2026-06-10 — declared with the FPR substrate). Caller-saved: x0..x18 (incl. x16/x17 = IP0/IP1; PLT-clobberable) + v0-v7/v16-v31 in their d views. callingConventions.$stackArgPackingComment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-STACK-ARG-ALIGNMENT — AAPCS64 §B rounds the NSAA up to a FUNDAMENTAL type's own alignment but CLAMPS a composite's to the 8-byte slot, and that split is exactly why the caps are two keys and not one. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 agreeing byte-for-byte, callee-side incoming offsets after 8 GPR + 8 FPR args and one stacked `long` so the NSAA is at an ODD slot: binary128 `long double` → +16 (the scalar cap bites); `struct __attribute__((aligned(16))){long x,y;}` → +8, NOT +16 (a composite's alignment is clamped, so the aggregate cap stays absent = the slot). ★ THE SECOND ROW IS THE PROOF THIS RULE IS CONFIG AND NOT A CONSTANT: x86_64 SysV puts that SAME 16-byte-aligned aggregate at +16. ⓘ `aligned(32)` is passed BY REFERENCE here (`ldr x1,[sp,8]` then a load through it) — a different mechanism, not a stack-alignment question. No stacked datum exceeds the slot on this target today (a binary128 past v7 is walled loud), so every placement is byte-unchanged.
callingConventions.$aggregateComment: FC7 C3 (D-FC7-STRUCT-BY-VALUE-ARG-RETURN): AAPCS64 §5.4 by-value aggregates. HFA (1-4 leaves all the same FP type) → that many FPR pieces (v0..v3 / d0..d3 for returns, d0..d7 for args). A non-HFA aggregate <=16 bytes → 1-2 GPR pieces (x0..x1 returns / x0..x7 args); > 16 bytes → BY REFERENCE: a caller-allocated copy for args; for RETURNS the caller passes the result address in x8 (`indirectResultRegister`) and the callee returns VOID (it writes through x8 — distinct from SysV/Win64's hidden-arg-then-return-pointer; `aggregateSretViaHiddenArg` is false here because indirectResultRegister is set). `aapcs64_hfa` drives the bounded classifier arm; maxRegBytes = 16 (two X-registers).
callingConventions.$aggregateStackExhaustsComment: D-FC12-VARIADIC-OVERFLOW-FIXED-AGGREGATE-STACK-ARGS: AAPCS64 §6.4.2 stage C — when a by-value composite/HFA does not fit the remaining arg registers it is placed WHOLLY on the stack and the overflowed class is EXHAUSTED (gcc aarch64_layout_arg sets aapcs_nextncrn=8 / aapcs_nextnvrn=8), so every subsequent arg of that class also goes to memory. true = no backfill (contrast SysV, which backfills the leftover registers). Read by HIR→MIR's caller+callee cursor handling + va_start's __gr_offs/__vr_offs clamp.
callingConventions.$callerSavedFprComment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): AAPCS64 §6.1.2 — v0-v7 (args/results) and v16-v31 are caller-saved; declared here in their d views. Being listed in callerSaved is what keeps the regalloc honest about them: an allocatable register NOT in callerSaved is treated as call-safe (lir_regalloc buildFreeLists), so omitting these while argFprs makes them allocatable would let a float live across a call sit unsaved in a volatile d-register — the same reason x86_64's sysv row lists all sixteen xmm registers here.
callingConventions.$calleeSavedFprComment: D-ARM64-FLOAT-SUBSTRATE (2026-06-10): AAPCS64 §6.1.2 — v8-v15 must be preserved by a callee ONLY in their LOW 64 BITS; the top 64 bits are the caller's responsibility everywhere. ⚠⚠ THIS LIST NOW NAMES `v8..v15`, THE FULL 16-BYTE ROWS, AND THE SAVE IS STILL 64 BITS WIDE — read that pairing before changing either half. It used to name `d8..d15`, and the 64-bit save was then a property of the ROW; a calling convention may only name a FULL register (D-TARGET-CC-NAMES-SUB-REGISTER) and after R1 the full register is `v_k`, so the row can no longer carry the width. ✔RE-MEASURED 2026-08-31 AND THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE IS NOW HISTORY. It read: “✔MEASURED that the save did not move: `emitPrologue` calls `emitFrameStore` with `widthFlags` DEFAULTED, and the default is 64 — for every class on every target — so the prologue still emits STUR Dt and still saves precisely the bits the ABI guarantees. ⓘ x86_64 is the control and has always had this exact shape: `ms_x64` lists the 16-byte `xmm6..xmm15` in `calleeSaved` and saves 8 bytes of each through `movsd_store`.” Both halves were true and the second was a DEFECT being read as a control: `ms_x64` preserves xmm6-15 IN FULL (✔MEASURED against MSVC 14.44.35207, which emits `movaps XMMWORD PTR [rax-24], xmm6` — sixteen bytes), so the shared default was silently right here and silently wrong there, with no diagnostic on either side. D-LIR-CALLEE-SAVED-AND-SPILL-STORES-DEFAULT-TO-WIDTH-64-BELOW-THE-SLOT removed the default; the width is now a REQUIRED argument at every frame emit, and the 64 bits this convention preserves are DECLARED beside `calleeSaved` as `calleeSavedPreservedBits`. The emitted arm64 prologue is BYTE-IDENTICAL — still STUR Dt — which is the point: the bytes did not change, the reason for them did. ★ WHAT R3 STILL OWES, WITH ITS TRIGGER UNCHANGED. The declaration now covers the SAVE. It does not constrain the ALLOCATOR, and that half is what a >64-bit FPR value would need: v8..v15 could not carry one across a call however wide DSS's own save is, because the callee may be gcc's and gcc saves what this row says. THIS SENTENCE REMAINS THE TRIGGER: the first FPR value wider than 64 bits that can be live across a call. ✔RE-MEASURED that it has still not fired — `LirVerifier`'s store rule keeps F80 and F128 memory-resident, so an FPR virtual register holds F16/F32/F64 and nothing wider.
callingConventions.$calleeSavedPreservedBitsComment: D-LIR-CALLEE-SAVED-AND-SPILL-STORES-DEFAULT-TO-WIDTH-64-BELOW-THE-SLOT. AAPCS64 §6.1.2: a callee must preserve v8-v15, and only their LOW 64 BITS — the top half is the caller's responsibility. ★★★ THIS ROW IS THE FACT ITSELF, AND UNTIL NOW IT LIVED IN A CODE DEFAULT ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE COMPILER. `emitFrameStore`'s `widthFlags` parameter defaulted to 0 (= width 64) for every register class on every target, so this convention got the right 8-byte STUR Dt by accident and x86_64's `ms_x64` — which preserves xmm6-15 IN FULL, ✔MEASURED against MSVC 14.44.35207 emitting `movaps XMMWORD PTR [rax-24], xmm6` — got a silent 8-byte save into a 16-byte slot from the same default. One default cannot serve two ABIs that disagree, so the default is gone and each ABI declares its own number; an ABI that preserves the WHOLE register declares nothing, which is why `ms_x64` has no row and this one does. ⚠ IT GOVERNS THE SAVE, NOT THE ALLOCATOR. A value WIDER than 64 bits still may not be parked in v8-v15 across a call — not because DSS's own prologue would drop it (it now saves exactly what this row says, and a foreign callee saves the same) but because the ABI publishes no more than this. That constraint is R3 of design A′ and remains on its stated trigger: the first FPR value wider than 64 bits that can be live across a call. ✔RE-MEASURED 2026-08-31 that the trigger has still not fired — `LirVerifier`'s store rule keeps F80 and F128 memory-resident, so an FPR virtual register holds F16/F32/F64 and nothing else. ⓘ SPILL SLOTS ARE NOT GOVERNED BY THIS ROW and did change on this target: a spill slot is DSS's own memory with no ABI facing it, so it now round-trips the WHOLE 16-byte register (STUR Qt) into the 16-byte slot `frameSlotStride` already sized for it, instead of the 8 bytes the same default used to write.
callingConventions.$framePointerComment: D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): x29 is the AAPCS64 frame-pointer register a VLA function reserves as a stable fixed-frame base (captured at the fixed-frame bottom via `sp_copy`, then every fixed-frame ref switches SP->x29 so it survives the runtime `sub sp,<vlaSize>`). A NON-VLA function never reserves it — x29 stays an ordinary callee-saved allocatable GPR (byte-identical frames). Consumed by lir_regalloc (pool exclusion) + lir_callconv (force-save + prologue capture + epilogue restore).
callingConventions.$entryStackPointerBiasComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-TRAMP-PROLOGUE: AArch64 BL does NOT push a return address (it writes LR / x30 directly), so process entry — whether by kernel-jump (Linux/Mac) or `RtlUserThreadStart`-BL (Windows) — leaves SP 16-byte-aligned (bias 0 mod 16). Trampoline `sub sp, 0` is emitted as nothing — `alignedSizeWithBias(shadowSpaceBytes=0, stackAlignment=16, bias=0) = 0`.
callingConventions.$callPushBytesComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-ML7-FRAME-BIAS-UNIFY: AArch64 BL writes the return address into LR/x30 — no stack push. callPushBytes=0 is the right ISA-level fact for ARM64. Non-leaf functions on ARM64 still save x30 in their prologue + reload it before `ret`; because x30 is the `linkRegister` (deliberately NOT in `calleeSaved` — it must not be allocatable), this is realized by the link-register fold in `lir_callconv.cpp::materializeOneFunc` (gated on hasCalls + cc.linkRegister), which adds x30 to `savedRegs` so it lands in `savedRegAreaSize`. Without it the epilogue `ret` returns to a clobbered LR — see D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64-NONLEAF-LINK-REGISTER. Independent of the call-push bias.
callingConventions.$vaListLayoutComment: FC12c (D-FC12C-AAPCS64-VARIADIC-CALLEE): AAPCS64 §B.4 dual-cursor variadic callee. `__va_list` = {void* __stack@0; void* __gr_top@8; void* __vr_top@16; int __gr_offs@24; int __vr_offs@28;} (32B). The prologue spills x0..x7 (GR block, 8×8=64B) then v0..v7 (VR block, 8×16=128B) into a callee-local register-save-area (regSaveAreaBytes()=192). va_start sets __gr_top=rsa+64 (past the GR block), __vr_top=rsa+192 (past the VR block), __stack=overflow base, __gr_offs=-(8-fixedGpr)*8, __vr_offs=-(8-fixedFpr)*16. va_arg(T) classifies T (GPR vs VR), reads the negative class cursor, and if <0 reads `<gr|vr>_top + (sign-extended cursor)` then bumps by the slot stride, else walks __stack by 8 (the NSAA round-up quantum, even for a double). namedArgSlotBytes=8.

callingConventions.$comment: apple_arm64 — Apple's ARM64 ABI for Apple platforms (developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms). The ABI catalog (abi_catalog.cpp) maps (arm64, MachO) → CcApple → "apple_arm64"; shipping this row CLOSES D-FF3-5 (trigger: 'apple_arm64 cc row ships in arm64.target.json') and is what lets `resolveAbi` + the entry trampoline resolve a Mach-O-ARM64 cc. The general-purpose REGISTER vocabulary is IDENTICAL to AAPCS64 — integer args x0..x7, returns x0/x1, callee-saved x19..x28+x29, link x30, sp, 16-byte stack alignment, bias 0 (BL writes LR, no push). The Apple ABI's documented DIVERGENCES from AAPCS64 are NOT register-assignment differences: (1) variadic args are ALWAYS passed on the stack (vs AAPCS64's register-then-stack) and (2) a different indirect-result-location rule. Neither is modeled at today's scalar-only asm tier (variadic support is gated at D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-VARIADIC-SIGNATURE), so for the scalar register-passing this row carries the same fields as aapcs64; a SEPARATE named row keeps the ABI identity explicit and correct, so when variadic/indirect-result lands it is updated HERE, not by silently reusing aapcs64. The always-stack variadic rule + indirect-result-location divergence are pinned at D-FF3-APPLE-ARM64-ABI-DIVERGENCE (they land WITH the proper CcApple field set when the trigger fires — a variadic OR struct-return call on arm64-Apple — not as a silent aapcs64 reuse; distinct from D-FF3-4, which is the Microsoft CcMSARM64 split).
callingConventions.name: apple_arm64
callingConventions.$aggregateComment: FC7 C3: Apple ARM64 by-value aggregate register-assignment is IDENTICAL to AAPCS64 (the documented Apple divergences are variadic-always-stack + small-int widening, NOT the struct/HFA/x8 rules) — so it carries the same aggregate fields. This CLOSES the struct-return / indirect-result half of D-FF3-APPLE-ARM64-ABI-DIVERGENCE (x8 sret modeled); the variadic-always-stack half stays open until a variadic arm64-Apple call.
callingConventions.$aggregateStackExhaustsComment: D-FC12-VARIADIC-OVERFLOW-FIXED-AGGREGATE-STACK-ARGS: Apple arm64 inherits AAPCS64 stage-C register assignment (the Apple divergences are variadic-always-stack + small-int widening, NOT the composite placement rule) — a stacked composite EXHAUSTS the overflowed class, same as aapcs64.
callingConventions.$stackArgPackingComment: D-CODEGEN-APPLE-ARM64-STACK-ARGS-NOT-NATURALLY-PACKED — the NON-variadic half of D-FF3-APPLE-ARM64-ABI-DIVERGENCE, and the three axes MEASURED to differ rather than one boolean. callingConventions.$framePointerComment: D-CSUBSET-VLA (C1b): x29 is the AAPCS64 frame-pointer register a VLA function reserves as a stable fixed-frame base (captured at the fixed-frame bottom via `sp_copy`, then every fixed-frame ref switches SP->x29 so it survives the runtime `sub sp,<vlaSize>`). A NON-VLA function never reserves it — x29 stays an ordinary callee-saved allocatable GPR (byte-identical frames). Consumed by lir_regalloc (pool exclusion) + lir_callconv (force-save + prologue capture + epilogue restore).
callingConventions.$framePointerReservationComment: D-CODEGEN-APPLE-ARM64-X29-USED-AS-GENERAL-SCRATCH-AGAINST-ITS-RESERVED-ROLE: Apple's platform ABI reserves x29 UNCONDITIONALLY, more strictly than base AAPCS64, so it is never an allocatable general register here -- not in a leaf, not under register pressure, not at any optimization level. The AAPCS64 row above deliberately does NOT declare this and keeps the default `dynamic-frame-only`; that is not an oversight but the MEASURED difference between the two ABIs. VERIFIED 2026-08-28 by compiling one high-register-pressure source six ways and counting x29 writes outside the prologue/epilogue save pair: `clang --target=arm64-apple-macos11` at -O2/-O3/-Os with `-fomit-frame-pointer` EXPLICITLY requested emits ZERO every time (clang declines the flag rather than honoring it), while `clang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu` under the identical source and flags emits FOUR (`eor x29,x9,x7`, `mov x0,x29`, `add x9,x29,x0`, `eor x10,x10,x29`) and `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc -fomit-frame-pointer` emits zero by choice rather than by prohibition. Under `DSS = (gcc union clang union MSVC) union ISO C` the disjunction therefore PERMITS allocating x29 on ELF and FORBIDS it here. WHAT BREAKS WITHOUT IT is not the unwinder -- D-CODEGEN-MACHO-ARM64-X29-ALLOCATED-WITH-NO-FRAME-RECORD measured that the table-driven backtrace survives, and that row stays CLOSED -- it is every tool that walks frames WITHOUT tables: a sampling profiler, a crash reporter, `lldb` on a stripped image, each of which reads x29 directly and saw garbage. Consumed by lir_regalloc's pool build, which publishes the reservation to lir_rewrite's spill-scratch pool. It does NOT ask the callconv pass to emit a frame record; this field says only `not allocatable`, which is the whole claim the anchor makes.
callingConventions.$variadicComment: FC12c (D-FC12C-APPLE-ARM64-VARIADIC-CALLEE): the variadic half of D-FF3-APPLE-ARM64-ABI-DIVERGENCE. Apple arm64 passes ALL variadic args on the stack (vs AAPCS64's register-then-stack), so `va_list` is a PLAIN POINTER (HomogeneousPointer strategy, like Win64) that linearly bumps over the contiguous overflow area — no register-save-area, no dual cursor. `variadicArgsAlwaysStack` forces the CALLER to stack every vararg past the fixed args; `variadicUsesOverflowBase` makes va_start anchor `ap` at the overflow (first stacked vararg) base rather than a home area (Apple has none — named args stay in their registers, read via SSA). namedArgSlotBytes=8.

$relocationsComment: AArch64 ELF relocation kinds (plan 13 AS4 + plan 14 LK6 cycle 1 + D-LK6-1 closure 2026-06-01). The 'formula' field is a closed-enum discriminator (RelocFormulaKind in target_schema.hpp): 'aarch64_call26' = (S+A-P)>>2, signed-26-bit, OR into BL/B inst[25:0]; 'aarch64_adr_prel_pg_hi21' = ((S+A)>>12)-(P>>12), signed-21-bit, ADRP-split into immlo[30:29]+immhi[23:5]; 'aarch64_add_abs_lo12' = (S+A)&0xFFF, ADD imm12[21:10]; 'linear' (used for abs64) writes 8 LE bytes. Tag values are arbitrary per-target — only the NAME round-trips with format.json cross-reference. Paired anchors: D-LK6-8 (ARM64 PLT stub bytes) + D-LK6-14 (Apple Silicon chained-fixups dispatch) remain open and are independent of the formula reshape.

relocations.$comment: TLS C2 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): the local-exec thread-pointer-offset pair — the imm12 fields of the `lea` [reg, symbol] ADD/ADD macro. S = the SIGNED tpoff the walker bit-casts into symbolVa (arm64 Variant I ⇒ POSITIVE: alignUp(tcbHeaderBytes 16, p_align) + templateOffset). hi12 = (S+A)>>12 via the NEW Aarch64TprelAddHi12 formula — the pair's RANGE GATE ([0, 0xFFFFFF]; a silent wrap would address the wrong per-thread slot, audit LOW-d). lo12 = (S+A)&0xFFF — the SAME Aarch64AddAbsLo12 formula as add_abs_lo12_nc but a DISTINCT tls-flagged KIND row: the walker's CRIT-1 cross-check keys (target ∈ tlsSymbols) XOR (kind.tls) both directions, so reusing kind 3 for a tpoff patch would either reject loud (tls symbol under a non-tls kind) or — with the flag moved — mis-admit VA patches as tpoffs. `tls: true` is what marks the patched value a tpoff, not a VA.
relocations.name: tls-tprel-hi12

relocations.$comment: D-LK-ARM64-EXTERN-DATA-ADDR-PIE-GOT (TF-C52): the GOT-page word of the `lea_extern_got` macro (ADRP of `:got:sym`). `aarch64_adr_got_page` is a REAL non-Linear RelocFormulaKind (so the ET_DYN slide-safe classifier does not mis-treat it as a Linear-absolute-in-.text fixup -- D-LK-DYN-TEXT-ABS-RELOC keys formulaKind==Linear) but DSS never APPLIES it: it is emitted ONLY into a foreign-linked relocatable object, and the `applyExecRelocations` kernel arm is an explicit fail-loud REFUSAL. Non-Linear => widthBytes auto-defaults to 4, pcRelative/addendBias must be absent (the ADRP is PC-relative BY CONSTRUCTION, encoded intrinsically). kind 7 matches both elf64-aarch64-linux{,-staticlib}.format.json's R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE (nativeId 311).
relocations.name: adr_got_page

relocations.$comment: D-LK-ARM64-EXTERN-DATA-ADDR-PIE-GOT (TF-C52): the GOT-lo12 word of the `lea_extern_got` macro (LDR of `[x,:got_lo12:sym]`). Same foreign-linked-only / fail-loud-in-kernel discipline as adr_got_page. kind 8 matches both format siblings' R_AARCH64_LD64_GOT_LO12_NC (nativeId 312).

relocations.$comment: D-UNWIND-NO-EH-FRAME-IN-RELOCATABLE-OBJECTS: a 32-bit PC-relative reference with NO implicit bias — the DWARF FDE `initial_location` field in a relocatable `.eh_frame` (DW_EH_PE_pcrel|sdata4). Unlike every other arm64 row this patches a DATA word, not an instruction field, so the formula is plain Linear (S + A - P, 4 LE bytes) rather than one of the aarch64_* bit-shift variants. kind 9 matches both elf64-aarch64-linux{,-staticlib}.format.json's R_AARCH64_PREL32 (nativeId 261). ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 against `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc -c`: `readelf -r` shows `R_AARCH64_PREL32  .text + 0` on the first FDE — the reference toolchain's own choice, addend = the function's offset within .text.
